definition_zh: 鉴定（真伪）；证明……真实；验证身份；（计算机）认证
definition_en: to prove that something is genuine or that a person or device is what it claims to be
core_image: 一枚旧印章在放大镜下被逐条比对纹路
scene: 拍卖行的人把画翻到背面，对着灯看纸的年轮。 An expert was called in to authenticate the painting.
sceneCN: 这里指鉴定物件是否为真品（第 1 个义项：证明某物为真）；句意为请来专家鉴定这幅画的真伪。

pos.zh: 鉴定真伪；证明真实性；验证身份；认证

senses.title: To prove something genuine
senses.definition: to establish that an object or document is what it claims to be
senses.definitionCN: 确认某物或文件确如其声称
senses.example: An expert was called in to authenticate the painting.
senses.exampleCN: 请来一位专家鉴定这幅画。
senses.why: Greek authentikos meant genuine or original, and the verb makes that judgement an act.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 authentikos 意为「真的、原本的」，动词把这个判断变成一项行为。

senses.title: To verify a person's identity
senses.definition: to confirm that a person is who they say they are
senses.definitionCN: 确认某人确为其自称之人
senses.example: The bank authenticates every caller before moving money.
senses.exampleCN: 银行在动钱之前会验证每一位来电者。
senses.why: Identity is the modern field where the word is used most often.
senses.whyCN: 身份是现代使用这个词最频繁的领域。

senses.title: To certify a signature or seal
senses.definition: to confirm that a signature or seal was made by the right hand
senses.definitionCN: 确认签名或印章出自有权之人
senses.example: A notary authenticated the signature on the deed.
senses.exampleCN: 公证人证明了契据上的签名。
senses.why: Law needs a trusted hand to say that another hand was genuine.
senses.whyCN: 法律需要一双可信的手来宣告另一双手为真。

senses.title: To log a user into a system
senses.titleCN: 计算机系统中认证用户
senses.definition: to check credentials before granting access
senses.definitionCN: 在授予访问权之前核验凭证
senses.example: The app authenticates users with a one-time code.
senses.exampleCN: 这款应用用一次性验证码认证用户。
senses.why: Computing shortened the legal judgement into a routine check.
senses.whyCN: 计算技术把法律的判断压缩成例行核验。

senses.title: To establish evidence as genuine
senses.definition: to show that evidence is original and unaltered
senses.definitionCN: 证明证据为原件且未被改动
senses.example: The court must authenticate the recording before using it.
senses.exampleCN: 法院在使用录音之前必须先确认其为真。
senses.why: Evidence must be traced to its source before it can speak.
senses.whyCN: 证据必须先追溯到来源，才能开口作证。

senses.title: To verify a financial transaction
senses.definition: to confirm that a payment or message came from the stated sender
senses.definitionCN: 确认支付或讯息确由所称发送者发出
senses.example: The network authenticates the transfer in seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 网络在几秒内核验了这笔转账。
senses.why: Money moves only when the sender can be proven.
senses.whyCN: 只有发送者能被证明，钱才动得了。

senses.title: To judge a work of art
senses.definition: to decide whether a work was made by the claimed artist or period
senses.definitionCN: 判定作品是否出自所称的艺术家或年代
senses.example: Two laboratories authenticated the canvas.
senses.exampleCN: 两家实验室鉴定了这幅画布。
senses.why: The art market rests on a judgement that a hand and a date are real.
senses.whyCN: 艺术市场靠的是一个判断：那双手与那个年代是真的。

senses.title: To establish a claim as credible
senses.definition: to give a statement enough support to be believed
senses.definitionCN: 给某说法足够支撑，使其可信
senses.example: The data authenticate his account of the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 数据证实了他对事故的叙述。
senses.why: The word can widen from objects to any claim that needs a warrant.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以从物件扩展到任何需要凭据的说法。

intro.en: Authenticate comes from Greek authentikos, genuine or original, through Latin authenticus and French authentique, with the English verb suffix -ate. The direct source is clear; the second element of the Greek noun authentes is source uncertain.
intro.cn: authenticate 源自希腊 authentikos「真的、原本的」，经拉丁 authenticus 与法语 authentique，再加英语动词后缀 -ate。直接来源清楚；希腊名词 authentes 的第二成分来源不确定。

items.en: Autos meant self, and it is the first element of authentes.
items.cn: autos 意为自身，是 authentes 的第一成分。

items.en: Authentes meant one who acts on his own authority, a master or doer; the second element is often read as a doer but is source uncertain.
items.cn: authentes 意为凭自身权威行事的人，即主人或行为者；第二成分常被解作「做者」，但来源不确定。

items.en: Authentikos meant genuine, original and principal, said of things that carry their own authority.
items.cn: authentikos 意为真的、原本的、主要的，用于本身带有权威的事物。

items.en: Latin authenticus and French authentique carried the adjective into English.
items.cn: 拉丁 authenticus 与法语 authentique 把这个形容词带进英语。

items.en: English added the verb suffix -ate, making the judgement an action.
items.cn: 英语加上动词后缀 -ate，把判断变成动作。

items.en: Computing gave the verb its busiest modern home, where credentials replace seals.
items.cn: 计算技术给了这个动词最繁忙的现代归宿，凭证取代了印章。

note.en: The first group shares the Greek genuine-stem; the second group names checking and proving.
note.cn: 第一组共享希腊语「真」的词干；第二组是核验与证明的近义说法。

entries.definition: The quality of being genuine.

entries.definition: The act or process of proving genuineness.

entries.definition: A person or device that verifies identity.

entries.definition: A writer or originator; from Latin auctor, not from Greek authentes.

entries.definition: To check that something is true or accurate.
entries.definitionCN: 核查某事物为真或准确。

entries.definition: To confirm that something is valid or acceptable.
entries.definitionCN: 确认某事物有效或可接受。

entries.definition: To state officially that something is true.
entries.definitionCN: 正式声明某事物为真。

entries.definition: To establish the truth of something more firmly.
entries.definitionCN: 更牢固地确立某事物的真实性。

entries.definition: To bear witness to a fact.
entries.definitionCN: 为某一事实作证。

normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的希腊来源、真实同族词与真实搭配。

normal.en: A notary authenticates a signature; a server authenticates a user.

abstract.cn: 鉴定是拿放大镜对着一枚旧印章，一条条纹路比对到吻合。

abstract.en: A thing is authentic when its origin can be traced, not merely when it looks right.
abstract.cn: 事物之为真，在于来源可追，而不只在于看起来像。

abstract.en: Every password is a small claim that someone must prove.

examples.en: The dealer refused to authenticate the letter without its envelope.
examples.cn: 没有信封，经销商拒绝证明这封信为真。

examples.en: The system authenticates each device before it joins the network.
examples.cn: 设备加入网络之前，系统会逐一认证。

examples.en: No one could authenticate the story of the missing hours.
examples.cn: 没有人能证实那几小时空白里的说法。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM CHECK: credentials accepted and a payment confirmed from its sender.

definition_zh: 迫害；因宗教、政治或族群身份而遭受的系统性打压；迫害行为或迫害时期
definition_en: systematic, often prolonged mistreatment of a group because of its religion, politics, ethnicity or other identity
core_image: 一扇被砸开的门，屋内书页散落，墙上有炭笔写的警告，窗外有人低头快步走过
scene: 旧城巷口，一群人的门被做了记号，夜里传来砸门声，邻居把窗帘拉紧，不敢点灯。 The diary records the persecution, the systematic pursuit that drove the family from the city because of its faith.
sceneCN: 这里 persecution 指「因身份而遭受的系统性打压」（第 1 个义项：持续且有目标的迫害）；句意为日记记录了迫使这家人离开城市的迫害。可辨识物件：门上的记号、散落书页、紧拉的窗帘、黑暗的窗口。

pos.zh: 迫害；迫害行为或时期（可数，复数 persecutions；不可数时指整体现象）

senses.title: Systematic persecution of a group
senses.definition: prolonged, organized mistreatment of people because of religion, politics, ethnicity or another identity
senses.definitionCN: 因宗教、政治、族群或其他身份而有组织地长期虐待一群人
senses.example: The diary records the persecution that drove the family from the city.
senses.exampleCN: 日记记录了迫使这家人离开城市的迫害。
senses.why: persecutio is a following-through: per- 'through' plus sequi 'follow', so the word pictures a pursuit that does not stop.
senses.whyCN: persecutio 是「一路跟到底」：per-「贯穿」加 sequi「跟随」，因此这个词描绘一种不肯停下的追逼。

senses.title: A single act or incident
senses.definition: one concrete act of harassment, arrest, seizure or violence aimed at a group's member
senses.definitionCN: 针对群体成员的一次具体骚扰、逮捕、查抄或暴力行为
senses.example: Each persecution was logged by the court clerk.
senses.exampleCN: 每一次迫害都被法庭书记记录下来。
senses.why: a long campaign is made of separate blows, and English lets the countable plural name those blows.
senses.whyCN: 长期运动由一次次打击构成，英语用可数复数来命名这些打击。

senses.title: A period or state of persecution
senses.definition: the span of time in which a group lives under systematic pressure
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体在系统性压力下生活的那段时间
senses.example: The persecution lasted three decades.
senses.exampleCN: 这场迫害持续了三十年。
senses.why: the noun can name a stretch of time, like reign or famine, because the condition has a beginning and an end.
senses.whyCN: 和统治期、饥荒一样，这个名词可指一段时间，因为这种状态有始有终。

senses.title: Legal and administrative persecution
senses.titleCN: 法律与行政手段的迫害
senses.definition: the use of registration, permits, courts or police powers to isolate and punish a group
senses.definitionCN: 利用登记、许可、法庭或警权来隔离并惩罚某一群体
senses.example: Registration rules turned into a form of persecution.
senses.exampleCN: 登记规则变成了一种迫害形式。
senses.why: persecution needs no uniformed mob; paperwork can pursue people just as effectively.
senses.whyCN: 迫害不需要暴民；纸面手续同样能有效追逼人。

senses.title: Social ostracism by a community
senses.definition: non-state exclusion through rumour, boycott, denial of work or housing
senses.definitionCN: 通过流言、抵制、拒绝工作或住房而实施的非国家排斥
senses.example: Persecution can begin with a whisper in the schoolyard.
senses.exampleCN: 迫害可以始于校园里的一句悄悄话。
senses.why: the pursuit can be carried out by neighbours rather than officials, which is why the word covers social pressure.
senses.whyCN: 这种追逼可由邻里而非官员实施，因此这个词也涵盖社会压力。

senses.title: Historical name for a specific persecution
senses.definition: the capitalized name given to a particular official campaign, such as the Great Persecution
senses.definitionCN: 对某次官方运动的专名，如「大迫害」
senses.example: Historians date the Great Persecution to the reign of Diocletian.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家把「大迫害」定在戴克里先统治时期。
senses.why: major campaigns receive proper names, and the common noun becomes part of a historical label.
senses.whyCN: 重大运动获得专名，普通名词便成为历史标签的一部分。

senses.title: Figurative campaign against a view or group
senses.titleCN: 比喻：对某种观点或群体的围攻
senses.definition: by extension, organized hostility toward a belief, profession or faction outside state action
senses.definitionCN: 引申指国家行为之外，对某种信念、职业或派别的有组织敌意
senses.example: Scientists described the campaign as a persecution of dissent.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家把这场运动称为对不同意见的迫害。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the asymmetry: one side pursues, the other cannot rest.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了不对称：一方追逼，另一方不得安宁。

senses.title: Abstraction: pursuit that gives no rest
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：不容对方喘息的追逼
senses.definition: any sustained pressure by a stronger party that denies a weaker party safety or peace
senses.definitionCN: 强者对弱者施加、使其失去安全或安宁的持续压力
senses.example: Persecution is pursuit that refuses to let its object rest.
senses.exampleCN: 迫害是不让对象安歇的那种追逼。
senses.why: the root sense of following explains the whole family of meanings: persecution is not one blow but an ongoing chase.
senses.whyCN: 词根的「跟随」义解释了整个词义家族：迫害不是一击，而是持续的追赶。

intro.en: Persecution comes from Latin persequi 'to follow through, pursue', built on per- 'through' and sequi 'to follow'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: persecution 来自拉丁 persequi「一路跟随、追逼」，由 per-「贯穿」与 sequi「跟随」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Persequi meant 'to follow persistently, pursue, hunt down'; the prefix per- adds the idea of carrying the action through to the end.
items.cn: persequi 意为「持续跟随、追捕、追到底」；前缀 per- 增添「把动作做到底」的意思。

items.en: Sequi meant 'to follow'; its Indo-European ancestor is usually reconstructed as *sekʷ-, a reconstruction and not a recorded form.
items.cn: sequi 意为「跟随」；其印欧祖形通常重构为 *sekʷ-，属重构而非有记录的形式。

items.en: Persecutio named a pursuit or a following after; in late Latin legal and church writing it took on the sense of hostile pursuit.
items.cn: persecutio 指追赶或追随；在晚期拉丁语的法律与教会写作中，它带上敌意追逼之义。

items.en: Old French persecution carried the word into English in the fourteenth century, first in religious contexts.
items.cn: 古法语 persecution 在十四世纪把这个词带入英语，最初用于宗教语境。

items.en: The organized sense grew in accounts of martyrs and later in political writing about minorities and dissent.
items.cn: 有组织的迫害义先在殉道者记述中成长，后来进入关于少数群体与异议的政治写作。

items.en: Source uncertain (first English citation and root shape): dictionaries differ on the earliest English use, and the Indo-European form behind sequi is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（英语首见年代与词根形态）：辞书对最早的英语用例说法不一，sequi 背后的印欧形式属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same following root that are constantly confused with persecution; group two holds neighbouring terms for organised mistreatment.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「跟随」词根、常与 persecution 混淆的词；第二组是有组织的虐待类邻近词。

entries.definition: From pro- 'forward' plus sequi: the state's pursuit of a case in court. It shares the root but names legal action, not group mistreatment.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 pro-「向前」加 sequi：国家在法庭上追究案件。同词根，但指法律诉讼，不指群体虐待。

entries.definition: To follow in order to catch; it has no built-in idea of injustice or group identity.
entries.definitionCN: 指为抓住而追赶；本身不含不义或群体身份之意。

entries.definition: To subject someone to persecution; the noun names the campaign, the verb names the repeated act.
entries.definitionCN: 指对某人实施迫害；名词指运动，动词指反复的行为。

entries.definition: The person or body that carries out persecution; it names the pursuer rather than the pursuit.
entries.definitionCN: 指实施迫害的人或机构；命名追逼者而非追逼本身。

entries.definition: Unjust exercise of power that weighs a group down; persecution stresses the chase, oppression stresses the burden.
entries.definitionCN: 指不义地行使权力压住群体；persecution 强调追逼，oppression 强调重压。

entries.definition: Differential treatment based on identity; it can exist without an active campaign of pursuit.
entries.definitionCN: 指基于身份的区别对待；可以没有主动追逼的运动而存在。

entries.definition: An organised mass attack on a particular community, often short and violent; persecution may last much longer.
entries.definitionCN: 指对某一社群的有机组织的大规模攻击，常短促而暴力；迫害可持续更久。

entries.definition: Repeated unwanted pressure on a person; it can be individual and need not target a group.
entries.definitionCN: 指对个人反复施加的不受欢迎压力；可针对个人，不必针对群体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: per- plus sequi, the shared root family and the historical proper name.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：per- 加 sequi、同根词族，以及那个历史专名。

normal.en: per- 'through' + sequi 'follow': to follow someone through every door they enter.
normal.cn: per-「贯穿」+ sequi「跟随」：跟着一个人穿过他所进的每一道门。

normal.en: The family runs persecute, persecution, persecutor, prosecute, prosecution, pursue.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 persecute、persecution、persecutor、prosecute、prosecution、pursue。

normal.en: prosecution is pro- 'forward': the court pushes a case forward, a different direction from persecution.
normal.cn: prosecution 是 pro-「向前」：法庭把案件向前推，与迫害的方向不同。

normal.en: The Great Persecution is dated to Diocletian's reign, early in the fourth century.
normal.cn: 「大迫害」定在四世纪初的戴克里先统治时期。

normal.en: Typical partners are flee, escape, campaign of and systematic.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是「逃离」「躲避」「一场……运动」与「系统性的」。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow that follows a person from room to room and never sleeps.
abstract.cn: 想象一道影子跟着人从一个房间到另一个房间，从不睡觉。

abstract.en: Picture a net drawn tighter each time the caught thing moves.
abstract.cn: 想象一张网，被捕获之物每动一下，网就收紧一分。

abstract.en: Picture a name written on a list that is checked at every door.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名字被写进名单，每道门口都要核对。

examples.en: Many families fled the persecution and crossed the border at night.
examples.cn: 许多家庭逃离迫害，在夜里越过边境。

examples.en: The law turned ordinary paperwork into an instrument of persecution.
examples.cn: 这项法律把普通文书变成了迫害工具。

examples.en: Survivors gave testimony about persecution that lasted for years.
examples.cn: 幸存者就持续多年的迫害作证。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「per（一直）+ secu（跟随）」——一直跟着某群人追打 → 迫害

root: 拉丁 persequi「追到底」= per-（贯穿）+ sequi「跟随」；名词 persecutio 指追逼。sequi 的印欧祖形 *sekʷ- 属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings follow one chase: a group is pursued because of who it is. The chase becomes single acts, a long period, legal machinery, social exclusion, a named historical campaign, a metaphor for hostility to ideas and finally the pure shape of pursuit without rest.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一场追逼展开：一群人因其身份而被追赶。这场追逼先成为单次行为，再成为长时期，再成为法律机器、社会排斥、具名的历史运动、对观念的敌意比喻，最后成为「不容喘息」的追逼本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a marked door, scattered pages and footsteps that keep coming back at night.
core.cn: 核心意象：被做了记号的门、散落的书页，以及夜里反复回来的脚步声。

branches.en: THE CAMPAIGN: the chase lasts long enough to become a period of life.
branches.cn: 运动：追逼持续到足以成为一段生活时期。

branches.en: THE BLOW AND THE FORM: one act, then a system of rules that repeats it.
branches.cn: 打击与形式：先是一次行为，再是一套重复它的规则。

branches.en: SOCIETY AND THE RECORD: neighbours join in, and major campaigns receive names.
branches.cn: 社会与记录：邻里参与，重大运动获得名称。

branches.en: THE BORROWED CHASE: hostility toward a view borrows the shape of persecution.
branches.cn: 借来的追逼：对某种观点的敌意借用了迫害的形状。

branches.en: NO REST: the root idea of following explains why the word implies endless pressure.
branches.cn: 不得安歇：词根的「跟随」解释了为何这个词暗示无尽的压力。

intro.en: Persecution is built from a Latin prefix, a Latin root and a noun suffix, all of which still build English words.
intro.cn: persecution 由拉丁前缀、拉丁词根与名词后缀构成，三者仍构成英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin sequi gives pursue, pursue's relatives, prosecute and sequence; per- adds the sense of going through to the end.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sequi 衍生 pursue、prosecute 与 sequence；per- 增添「做到底」的意思。

items.example: The prefix turns following into a chase to the finish.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「跟随」变成追到底。

items.example: The root is the plain act of following.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根就是「跟随」这个动作。

items.example: The Latin verb implied no rest for the pursued.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词暗示被追者不得安歇。

items.example: Persecution is organized, not accidental.
items.exampleCN: 迫害是有组织的，而非偶然的。

items.example: The regime persecuted the community for years.
items.exampleCN: 该政权迫害这个社群多年。

items.example: The persecutor kept a list of names.
items.exampleCN: 迫害者保存着一份名单。

items.meaning: to follow a case forward in court
items.example: The state prosecuted the officials.
items.exampleCN: 国家起诉了这些官员。

items.meaning: the conduct of a legal case
items.example: The prosecution called three witnesses.
items.exampleCN: 检方传唤了三名证人。

items.structure: pursue (Old French poursivre, from Latin prosequi)
items.meaning: to follow in order to catch
items.example: The patrol pursued the group for two days.
items.exampleCN: 巡逻队追赶这群人两天。

items.example: The events formed a clear sequence.
items.exampleCN: 这些事件形成清晰的顺序。

definition_zh: 染色体；细胞中承载基因的线状结构
definition_en: a thread-like structure of DNA and protein in the cell nucleus that carries genes
core_image: 一团细线被压缩成一对可以辨形的棒状物
scene: 显微镜下，细胞核里的细线排成一列。 Down syndrome results from an extra copy of chromosome 21.
sceneCN: 这里 chromosome 指「染色体」（第 1 个义项：细胞核中承载基因的线状结构）；句意：唐氏综合征由第 21 号染色体多出一份引起。

pos.zh: 染色体；（细菌的）环状染色体

senses.title: Gene carrier
senses.definition: a structure of DNA and protein that carries the genes of a cell
senses.definitionCN: 由 DNA 与蛋白质构成、承载细胞基因的结构
senses.example: Humans have forty-six chromosomes in most body cells.
senses.exampleCN: 人类大多数体细胞有四十六条染色体。
senses.why: Chroma named the colour seen under early dyes and soma named the body; the compound literally means a coloured body, which is what a stained chromosome looks like.
senses.whyCN: chroma 指早期染料下看到的颜色，soma 指身体；复合词字面就是「有色的物体」，这正是染色后染色体的样子。

senses.title: Visible during division
senses.definition: the condensed form of chromatin that becomes visible when a cell divides
senses.definitionCN: 染色质在细胞分裂时凝缩而成的可见形态
senses.example: Chromosomes line up along the middle of the cell before separating.
senses.exampleCN: 染色体在分开之前沿细胞中央排成一行。
senses.why: Only during division does the material condense enough to be seen as distinct bodies, so the word names that visible stage.
senses.whyCN: 只有在分裂时，这些物质才凝缩到能被看成独立小体的程度，因此这个词命名的是那个可见阶段。

senses.title: Carrier of heredity
senses.definition: the physical vehicle by which genes pass from parents to offspring
senses.definitionCN: 基因由亲代传给子代的物理载体
senses.example: Each parent contributes one chromosome of every pair.
senses.exampleCN: 每一对染色体中，父母各贡献一条。
senses.why: Once genes were located on these bodies, the chromosome became the vehicle of inheritance rather than only a stained object.
senses.whyCN: 基因被定位到这些小体上之后，染色体就从「被染色的物体」变成了遗传的载体。

senses.title: Sex chromosomes
senses.definition: the pair, X and Y, that determines biological sex in many animals
senses.definitionCN: 在许多动物中决定生物学性别的 X 与 Y 这一对
senses.example: A single chromosome decides whether the embryo develops testes.
senses.exampleCN: 一条染色体就决定了胚胎是否发育出睾丸。
senses.why: One pair carries the sex-determining genes, so the word is used in the singular when the identity of that chromosome matters.
senses.whyCN: 有一对染色体携带决定性别的基因，因此当重要的是那一条的身份时，这个词会用单数。

senses.title: Chromosome number
senses.definition: the characteristic count of chromosomes in a species
senses.definitionCN: 一个物种特有的染色体条数
senses.example: The chromosome number of a species is usually constant.
senses.exampleCN: 一个物种的染色体数目通常是恒定的。
senses.why: Because the count is species-typical, the word participates in a standard measurement rather than in a physical description.
senses.whyCN: 由于这个数目是物种的典型特征，这个词参与的是一项标准测量，而不是物理描述。

senses.title: Chromosome abnormality
senses.definition: a change in chromosome number or structure that affects development
senses.definitionCN: 染色体数目或结构的改变，影响发育
senses.example: The test looks for a chromosome abnormality in the fetus.
senses.exampleCN: 这项检查寻找胎儿的染色体异常。
senses.why: Since chromosomes hold the instructions, a change in their number or shape is a change in the instructions.
senses.whyCN: 既然染色体保存着指令，那么数目或形状的改变就是指令的改变。

senses.title: Bacterial chromosome
senses.definition: the usually circular DNA molecule of a bacterium
senses.definitionCN: 细菌通常呈环状的 DNA 分子
senses.example: The bacterial chromosome replicates before the cell divides.
senses.exampleCN: 细菌染色体在细胞分裂之前复制。
senses.why: Bacteria keep their DNA in one loop without a nucleus, and the word is stretched to cover this simpler arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 细菌把 DNA 放在一个没有细胞核的环里，这个词被延伸来涵盖这种更简单的安排。

senses.title: Chromosome in a karyotype
senses.definition: a single chromosome as displayed, counted and identified in a karyotype
senses.definitionCN: 在核型图中被展示、计数并识别的一条染色体
senses.example: The karyotype showed one chromosome with an unusual banding pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 核型图显示有一条染色体的带型异常。
senses.why: Once chromosomes are photographed and arranged in pairs, each one becomes an identifiable item in a standard display, and the word names that item.
senses.whyCN: 当染色体被拍摄并按对排列后，每一条都成为标准展示中的可识别项，这个词就命名那个项。

intro.en: Chromosome is a Greek compound coined in 19th-century German microscopy: colour plus body.
intro.cn: chromosome 是 19 世纪德国显微学造出的希腊语复合词：颜色加身体。

items.en: Greek chroma meant colour, and chrōma was also used for the skin or surface colour. The element chrom- later gave words like chromium and monochrome.
items.cn: 希腊语 chroma 指颜色，chrōma 也用于皮肤或表面颜色。成分 chrom- 后来衍生出 chromium、monochrome 等词。

items.en: Greek sōma meant body, as opposed to soul or to a part. It survives in somatic, psychosomatic and chromosome.
items.cn: 希腊语 sōma 指身体，与灵魂或局部相对。它保留在 somatic、psychosomatic、chromosome 中。

items.en: The German anatomist Wilhelm von Waldeyer-Hartz is generally credited with the term Chromosom in 1888, naming the bodies that take up dye during division. The attribution is widely accepted but the exact first printed use is debated.
items.cn: 德国解剖学家 Wilhelm von Waldeyer-Hartz 一般认为在 1888 年创造了 Chromosom 一词，用来指分裂时能吸收染料的那些小体。归属被广泛接受，但确切的首见印刷用例仍有争议。

items.en: Once chromosomes were tied to Mendelian inheritance, the word moved from cytology to genetics.
items.cn: 染色体与孟德尔遗传规律联系起来之后，这个词从细胞学进入遗传学。

items.en: The human chromosome number was established as 46 in 1956, correcting an earlier figure of 48.
items.cn: 人类染色体数目在 1956 年被确定为 46 条，纠正了此前 48 条的结论。

note.en: The first group separates chromosome from the materials and structures inside it; the second separates it from the units that carry genes at a different scale.
note.cn: 第一组把 chromosome 与它内部的物质和结构分开；第二组把它与在别的尺度上承载基因的单元分开。

entries.definition: The complex of DNA and protein as it exists between divisions; when it condenses into visible bodies, those bodies are chromosomes.
entries.definitionCN: 指分裂间期 DNA 与蛋白质的复合物；当它凝缩成可见小体时，那些小体才是染色体。

entries.definition: One of the two identical strands of a chromosome after copying; the two chromatids together make one chromosome.
entries.definitionCN: 指复制后染色体中两条相同丝状物之一；两条染色单体合起来才算一条染色体。

entries.definition: The adjective for 'of chromosomes'; it modifies abnormality, location or mapping, while chromosome is the countable noun.
entries.definitionCN: 是形容词，意为「染色体的」，修饰 abnormality、location、mapping 等；chromosome 是可数名词。

entries.definition: A segment of DNA that codes for a product; a chromosome is a long molecule carrying many genes.
entries.definitionCN: 指编码产物的 DNA 片段；一条染色体是携带许多基因的长分子。

entries.definition: The complete set of genetic material of an organism; chromosomes are the physical packages in which it is stored.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个生物的全部遗传物质；染色体是储存这些物质的物理包装。

entries.definition: A small circular DNA molecule separate from the bacterial chromosome, often carrying drug-resistance genes.
entries.definitionCN: 指细菌中独立于染色体的小型环状 DNA 分子，常携带抗药基因。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: chroma 'colour' + soma 'body': the coloured body seen under the microscope.
normal.cn: chroma「颜色」+ soma「身体」：显微镜下那个被染上颜色的小体。

normal.en: The family runs chromosomal, chromatin, chromatid and chromosome mapping.
normal.cn: 同族词有 chromosomal、chromatin、chromatid、chromosome mapping。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: sex chromosome, X chromosome, chromosome number, extra chromosome.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：性染色体、X 染色体、染色体数目、多余染色体。

normal.en: Humans have 46 chromosomes in 23 pairs.
normal.cn: 人类有 46 条染色体，共 23 对。

normal.en: A chromosome is a library shelf; a gene is one book on it.
normal.cn: 染色体像一排书架，基因是架上的一本书。

abstract.en: Picture a very long thread wound tight until it looks like a short thick rod.
abstract.cn: 想象一根很长的线被紧紧缠绕，直到看起来像一根短粗的棒。

abstract.en: A stained chromosome is a suspect lit up under a lamp: the dye reveals what was invisible.
abstract.cn: 染色后的染色体像灯下被照亮的嫌疑人：染料让原本看不见的东西显形。

abstract.en: An extra chromosome is one duplicate page bound into a manual.
abstract.cn: 多出一条染色体，就像手册里多装订了一页副本。

examples.en: Each human cell usually contains 23 pairs of chromosomes.
examples.cn: 每个人类细胞通常含有 23 对染色体。

examples.en: The extra chromosome 21 is the cause of Down syndrome.
examples.cn: 多出的第 21 号染色体是唐氏综合征的成因。

examples.en: Chromosomes must be copied and separated precisely before a cell divides.
examples.cn: 细胞分裂前，染色体必须被精确复制并分开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「chromo（颜色）+ some（体）」→ 染色后显形的「有色小体」→ 染色体

root: 希腊语 chroma「颜色」+ sōma「身体」→ 德语 Chromosom（1888 年 Waldeyer 提出）→ 英语 chromosome。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the gene-carrying body to its visible form, its role in heredity, the sex pair, the species count, the abnormality, the bacterial loop, and finally the single chromosome as it is displayed and identified in a karyotype.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「承载基因的小体」出发，经过它可见的形态、遗传作用、性染色体、物种数目、异常、细菌环状 DNA，最后到核型图中被展示并识别的那一条染色体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long thread folded into a compact rod that takes up dye.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根长线折叠成能吸收染料的紧凑短棒。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: the gene carrier as a structure, and the condensed form in which it becomes visible.
branches.cn: 对象：作为结构的基因载体，以及使它变得可见的凝缩形态。

branches.en: INHERITANCE: the vehicle from parents to offspring, including the pair that sets sex.
branches.cn: 遗传：从亲代到子代的载体，包括决定性别的那一对。

branches.en: COUNT: the species-typical number becomes a measurable property.
branches.cn: 数目：物种特有的条数成为可测量的属性。

branches.en: ERROR: an abnormal count or shape changes the instructions.
branches.cn: 错误：数目或形状异常会改变指令。

branches.en: SIMPLER FORMS: the bacterial loop and the single chromosome as it appears in a karyotype.
branches.cn: 更简单的形态：细菌的环状 DNA，以及核型图中出现的那一条染色体。

intro.en: Chromosome is a Greek-Greek compound with no English affix; its parts are still transparent in scientific vocabulary.
intro.cn: chromosome 是希腊语与希腊语的复合词，不含英语词缀；它的成分在科学词汇中仍然透明。

latinIntro.en: Both elements are Greek: chroma for colour and sōma for body. Latin plays no part, though the word was coined in German scientific Latin and reached English through it.
latinIntro.cn: 两个成分都来自希腊语：chroma 表颜色，sōma 表身体。拉丁语没有参与构词，但这个词是在德语科学拉丁语环境中造出，再经其进入英语。

items.example: The chromosome carries hundreds of genes.
items.exampleCN: 这条染色体携带数百个基因。

items.example: Chromosomal DNA is stored in the nucleus.
items.exampleCN: 染色体 DNA 储存在细胞核中。

items.meaningCN: 构成染色体的 DNA 与蛋白质物质
items.example: Chromatin loosens in the active regions.
items.exampleCN: 染色质在活跃区域会变得松散。

items.meaning: one strand of a copied chromosome
items.meaningCN: 复制后染色体的一条丝
items.example: Each chromatid is pulled to a pole.
items.exampleCN: 每条染色单体被拉向一极。

items.meaning: separation of substances by colour bands
items.meaningCN: 按色带分离物质的方法
items.example: Chromatography separated the pigments.
items.exampleCN: 层析法把色素分离开来。

items.example: Somatic cells do not form gametes.
items.exampleCN: 体细胞不形成配子。

items.meaning: a chromosome other than a sex chromosome
items.meaningCN: 除性染色体之外的染色体
items.example: Humans have 22 pairs of autosomes.
items.exampleCN: 人类有 22 对常染色体。

items.example: The genome is split across chromosomes.
items.exampleCN: 基因组分布在多条染色体上。

items.meaning: the protective end of a chromosome
items.meaningCN: 染色体末端的保护结构
items.example: Telomeres shorten with each division.
items.exampleCN: 端粒随着每次分裂而缩短。

latinEntries.meaning: a body, as opposed to a soul or part
latinEntries.meaningCN: 身体（相对于灵魂或局部）

latinEntries.meaning: used in compounds for a body or particle
latinEntries.meaningCN: 用于复合词，表示身体或小体

definition_zh: v. 扰乱；使中断；破坏（正常进程）
definition_en: to stop something continuing as normal by breaking its order or flow
core_image: 时刻表上被整列划掉的班次；一排被喊声撞歪的椅子；一条断了一环而其余松垂的链条

sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：罢工让铁路服务整整三天无法正常跑下去。

pos.zh: 扰乱；使中断；破坏

senses.title: Stop the normal run
senses.definition: to prevent something from continuing as it normally does
senses.definitionCN: （动词）使某事无法照常继续
senses.example: The strike disrupted rail services for three days.
senses.exampleCN: 罢工使铁路服务中断了三天。
senses.why: A timetable with a whole column crossed out.
senses.whyCN: 时刻表上被整列划掉的班次。

senses.title: Throw into confusion
senses.definition: to throw a meeting or process into disorder
senses.definitionCN: （动词）把会议或进程搅得混乱
senses.example: Protesters disrupted the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 抗议者扰乱了会议。
senses.why: A row of chairs knocked out of line by shouting.
senses.whyCN: 一排被喊声撞歪的椅子。

senses.title: Break the flow
senses.definition: to break the normal structure or flow of a system
senses.definitionCN: （动词）打断一个系统正常的结构或流动
senses.example: The flood disrupted the supply chain.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水打断了供应链。
senses.why: A chain with one link snapped and the rest slack.
senses.whyCN: 一条断了一环而其余松垂的链条。

intro.en: Disrupt comes from Latin disruptus, broken apart, the past participle of disrumpere, from dis- plus rumpere, to break; the same break root gives rupture, interrupt and erupt.
intro.cn: disrupt 来自拉丁语 disruptus「被打断的」，是 disrumpere 的过去分词，由 dis- 加 rumpere「打破」组成；同一个打破词根也给出 rupture、interrupt 与 erupt。

items.en: Latin rumpere means to break.
items.cn: 拉丁语 rumpere 意为打破。

items.en: Disrumpere meant to break apart.
items.cn: disrumpere 意为打断、撕裂。

items.en: Disruptus is the participle, broken apart.
items.cn: disruptus 是分词形式，意为被打断的。

items.en: English disrupt first means to break asunder.
items.cn: 英语 disrupt 最初意为撕裂开来。

items.en: The sense of interrupting normal activity becomes common.
items.cn: 打断正常活动这一意思变得常见。

items.en: Disrupt is used for overturning whole industries.
items.cn: disrupt 被用于表示颠覆整个行业。

note.en: Disrupt is breaking a flow apart; its look-alikes share the break root, and its neighbours name other ways of spoiling an orderly run.
note.cn: disrupt 是把流动打断；形近词共用打破词根，近义词则是别的破坏有序运行的方式。

entries.definition: a break or burst in something
entries.definitionCN: 某物的破裂或爆裂

entries.definition: to stop someone speaking or acting
entries.definitionCN: 打断某人说话或行动

entries.definition: a sudden bursting out
entries.definitionCN: 突然喷出

entries.definition: to interrupt the calm or order of something
entries.definitionCN: 打断某物的平静或秩序

entries.definition: a state of confusion

entries.definition: to obstruct the progress of something
entries.definitionCN: 阻碍某事的进展

dict_mnemonic.text: disrupt ＝ dis-（分开）＋ rupt（打破，拉丁语 rumpere，与 rupture、interrupt、erupt、bankrupt 同根）＝「把原本连着的东西打断」，即扰乱、使中断；商业语境里进一步指把旧模式整段打断。

root: 拉丁语 rumpere（打破）→ disrumpere（打断）→ disruptus（被打断的）→ 英语 disrupt

sensesIntro.en: A flow cut in three places: a crossed-out timetable, chairs out of line and a chain with a snapped link.
sensesIntro.cn: 流动在三处被切断：划掉的时刻表、歪掉的椅子与断了一环的链条。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a timetable with a whole column crossed out while a chain hangs slack with one link snapped
core.cn: 核心意象：时刻表上被整列划掉的班次，同时一条链条断了一环而松垂着

branches.en: A service that cannot run as usual.
branches.cn: 无法照常运行的服务。

branches.cn: 被搅成喧闹的有序集会。

definition_zh: 杰出的；非凡的；异常的；例外的
definition_en: unusually good, or unusually different from the normal case
core_image: 一排同样高的树里，有一棵高出许多，树梢几乎碰到云。
scene: 音乐老师听完所有学生的演奏。 After hearing every student play, the music teacher says only that this child's pitch is exceptional.
sceneCN: 这里 exceptional 是「远高于一般水平的、杰出的」（第 1 个义项：异常优秀或令人印象深刻）；句意：听完所有学生演奏后，音乐老师只说这个孩子的音准极为出色。

pos.zh: 杰出的；非凡的；异常的；例外的；特殊教育的

senses.title: Far above average
senses.titleCN: 杰出的：远高于一般水平
senses.definition: unusually good or impressive, far above the average
senses.definitionCN: 异常优秀或令人印象深刻，远高于平均水平
senses.example: She has an exceptional ear for harmony.
senses.exampleCN: 她对和声有非凡的听觉。
senses.why: Exceptional starts from exception: the person is lifted out of the ordinary row. The direction of the lift here is upward.
senses.whyCN: exceptional 从‘例外’出发：这个人被从普通的一排里拎出来；这里的拎出方向是向上。

senses.title: Unusual or rare
senses.titleCN: 异常的：不常发生，因而显眼
senses.definition: unusual and therefore notable, without necessarily being good
senses.definitionCN: 不寻常因而值得注意，不一定含褒义
senses.example: The storm was exceptional for its early date.
senses.exampleCN: 这场风暴因来得太早而异常。
senses.why: Here the lift is sideways: the case simply does not sit in the usual distribution, and the judgement is neutral.
senses.whyCN: 这里的拎出是横向的：这一例干脆不在通常分布里，判断是中性的。

senses.title: Forming an exception
senses.definition: forming an exception to a rule or general statement
senses.definitionCN: 构成规则或一般陈述之外的特殊情形
senses.example: This is an exceptional case that the policy did not foresee.
senses.exampleCN: 这是政策没有预见到的例外情形。
senses.why: This is the literal legal sense: the adjective describes a case that has been taken out of the rule's scope.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面上的法律义：形容词描述一个被移出规则适用范围的情形。

senses.title: Outstanding student
senses.titleCN: 特别出色的学生：天赋或成绩超常
senses.definition: describing a pupil or student whose ability is far above the expected level
senses.definitionCN: 形容能力远高于预期水平的学生
senses.example: The school created a programme for exceptional learners.
senses.exampleCN: 学校为超常学习者设立了一个项目。
senses.why: Education uses the word as a neutral technical label for children at the far end of a distribution, whether that end is high or low.
senses.whyCN: 教育领域把这个词当作中性技术标签，指分布两端的孩子，既可以是高端，也可以是低端。

senses.title: Exceptional size or degree
senses.titleCN: 超常的：尺寸或强度超出常规
senses.definition: much larger, stronger, or more intense than is normal
senses.definitionCN: 比正常情况大得多、强得多或强烈得多
senses.example: The bridge was built to withstand exceptional loads.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥按承受超常荷载来建造。
senses.why: Engineering uses the word for values beyond the design range: the structure is designed for the ordinary and then checked for the exception.
senses.whyCN: 工程上用这个词指超出设计范围的数值：结构先按常规设计，再针对例外情形校核。

senses.title: Extraordinarily good quality
senses.definition: of extraordinarily high quality
senses.definitionCN: 质量高到少见的
senses.example: The wine was exceptional, even for that famous vineyard.
senses.exampleCN: 这款酒即使对那个著名酒庄而言也属卓越。
senses.why: The word praises by placing the object outside its class: it is not merely a good wine, it is a wine that leaves the category.
senses.whyCN: 这个词通过把对象放到同类之外来赞美：它不只是好酒，而是离开了‘好酒’这一类别。

senses.title: Special needs
senses.titleCN: 特殊教育的：需要额外支持的孩子
senses.definition: in education, describing children who need special support because of disability or high ability
senses.definitionCN: 教育中形容因残障或超常能力而需要额外支持的孩子
senses.example: Funding was increased for exceptional children in the district.
senses.exampleCN: 该学区增加了对特殊需求儿童的拨款。
senses.why: The euphemistic use keeps the logic of exception: these children fall outside the standard classroom design and need a separate arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 这个委婉用法保留例外逻辑：这些孩子落在标准课堂设计之外，需要单独安排。

senses.title: Exceptionally allowed
senses.titleCN: 破例允许的：作为特殊情况被批准
senses.definition: allowed only as a special case, contrary to the usual practice
senses.definitionCN: 仅作为特殊情况、违背通常做法而被允许
senses.example: The committee granted exceptional permission to use the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会破例批准使用礼堂。
senses.why: Here the adjective modifies the permission itself: the rule stays in place, but one case is allowed to step outside it.
senses.whyCN: 这里形容词修饰的是‘许可’本身：规则仍然有效，但有一个情形被允许跨到线外。

intro.en: Exceptional is exception plus -al. It first meant ‘forming an exception’; the sense ‘unusually good’ is a later 19c development.
intro.cn: exceptional 是 exception 加 -al。它最初意为“构成例外的”；“异常优秀”义是 19 世纪较晚的发展。

items.en: To take out, from ex- out and capere take. The participle exceptus supplies the stem seen in exception and exceptional.
items.cn: 取出，来自 ex-‘向外’与 capere‘拿’。分词 exceptus 提供了 exception 与 exceptional 中可见的词干。

items.en: A taking out, an exception. The noun entered English through French and kept a legal flavour for centuries.
items.cn: 取出、例外。该名词经法语进入英语，数百年间都带法律色彩。

items.en: Exceptional is recorded in the 17th century meaning ‘of the nature of an exception’. It described cases and conditions, not people's talents.
items.cn: exceptional 在 17 世纪有记录，意为‘属于例外性质的’。它描述情形与条件，不描述人的才能。

items.en: The sense ‘unusual, uncommon’ developed next. Anything rare enough to leave the ordinary class could be called exceptional.
items.cn: 接着发展出‘不寻常、罕见’义。任何罕见得足以离开普通类别的东西，都可称为 exceptional。

items.en: The positive sense ‘excellently unusual’ is recorded in the early 19c. Praise borrowed the logic of rarity: good beyond the normal range.
items.cn: 正面义‘异常优秀’在 19 世纪早期有记录。赞美借用了‘稀有’的逻辑：好到超出正常范围。

items.en: Special education fixed exceptional as a technical label in the 20c. Engineering and law kept the neutral ‘outside the normal range’ sense.
items.cn: 20 世纪特殊教育把 exceptional 固定为技术标签；工程与法律则保留中性的‘超出正常范围’义。

note.en: The first group shares the exception stem and includes two words that are often confused; the second compares adjectives of high quality or rarity.
note.cn: 第一组共享 exception 词干，并包含两个常被混淆的词；第二组比较表示‘高品质或罕见’的形容词。

entries.definition: a case outside a rule. Exceptional is the adjective describing such a case or a quality beyond the norm.
entries.definitionCN: 规则之外的案例；exceptional 是描述这类案例或超常性质的形容词。

entries.definition: open to objection; blameworthy. It is not a stronger form of exceptional and carries disapproval.
entries.definitionCN: 可反对的；该受批评的。它不是 exceptional 的比较级，而带不赞同意味。

entries.definition: beyond objection; entirely proper. It is the opposite of exceptionable, not of exceptional.
entries.definitionCN: 无可指摘的；完全妥当的。它是 exceptionable 的反义，不是 exceptional 的反义。

entries.definition: to an unusual degree. It often means ‘extremely’ rather than ‘as an exception’.
entries.definitionCN: 达到不寻常的程度；常表示‘极其’，而非‘作为例外地’。

entries.definition: exceptionally good, standing out from others. It is warmer and more evaluative than exceptional.
entries.definitionCN: 杰出、从众人中站出来的；比 exceptional 更温暖、更具评价性。

entries.definition: very unusual or remarkable. It stresses departure from the ordinary order rather than from a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 非常不寻常或非凡；强调离开‘寻常秩序’，而非离开某条规则。

entries.definition: not happening often. It is neutral and can describe bad as easily as good.
entries.definitionCN: 不常发生的；中性，可描述坏也可描述好。

entries.definition: existing in small numbers or occurring seldom. It is about frequency, not quality.
entries.definitionCN: 数量少或很少发生；讲频率，不讲质量。

entries.definition: deviating from what is standard or expected. It sounds technical and often implies a problem.
entries.definitionCN: 偏离标准或预期的；听起来技术化，常暗示有问题。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: exception plus -al. The person or thing is lifted out of the ordinary row, either upward or sideways.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：exception 加 -al。人或物被从普通的一排里拎出来，方向可上可侧。

normal.en: Exception plus -al: exceptional means standing outside the ordinary row.
normal.cn: exception 加 -al：exceptional 就是站在普通队列之外。

normal.en: The tallest tree in a row is exceptional without breaking any rule.
normal.cn: 一排树里最高的那棵，不违反任何规则，却就是 exceptional。

normal.en: Exceptional weather is not good weather; it is weather outside the normal range.
normal.cn: exceptional 天气不是好天气，而是正常范围之外的天气。

normal.en: An exceptional student is one the standard lesson plan cannot fully hold.
normal.cn: exceptional 学生，是标准教案装不下的那个学生。

normal.en: Exceptional permission keeps the rule and opens one door.
normal.cn: 破例许可保留规则，只打开一扇门。

abstract.en: Every scale creates exceptions at both ends; the word does not decide which end is good.
abstract.cn: 每个量表都在两端制造例外；这个词本身不决定哪一端是好的。

abstract.en: Praise and abnormality use the same grammar: outside the normal class.
abstract.cn: 赞美与异常用的是同一套语法：在正常类别之外。

abstract.en: What a society calls exceptional is a map of what it expects.
abstract.cn: 一个社会称为 exceptional 的东西，就是它期待的分布图。

examples.en: The orchestra gave an exceptional performance despite the broken string.
examples.cn: 尽管琴弦断了，乐团仍奉献了一场非凡的演出。

examples.en: The judge allowed the evidence only under exceptional circumstances.
examples.cn: 法官仅在特殊情况下才允许采纳该证据。

examples.en: An exceptional year for rainfall left the reservoirs full.
examples.cn: 降雨异常充沛的一年让水库蓄满了水。

dict_mnemonic.text: “一颗赛破神”——一颗棋子破了神的常规，成了例外：exceptional 异常的、非凡的。

root: 由 exception 加 -al 构成，源头是拉丁 excipere（ex-‘向外’+ capere‘拿’）；本义为“属于例外性质的”，后引申出“罕见、异常优秀”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of exceptional, one move: lift a case out of the ordinary row. Upward lift gives ‘outstanding’, sideways lift gives ‘unusual’, legal lift gives ‘excepted’, and the classroom lift gives ‘special needs’.
sensesIntro.cn: exceptional 的八个义项共用一个动作：把一个情形从普通队列里拎出来。向上拎是‘杰出’，横向拎是‘异常’，法律拎是‘除外’，课堂拎是‘特殊需求’。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one tree in a row that rises far above the others.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排树中有一棵远远高出其他树。

branches.en: THE UPWARD LIFT: outstanding ability and exceptional quality leave the ordinary class from above.
branches.cn: 向上的拎出：非凡能力与卓越品质从上方离开普通类别。

branches.en: THE SIDEWAYS LIFT: rare weather and special permission simply sit outside the usual distribution.
branches.cn: 横向的拎出：异常天气与特殊许可只是位于通常分布之外。

branches.en: THE LEGAL LIFT: a case is formally removed from a rule's scope.
branches.cn: 法律上的拎出：情形被正式移出规则范围。

branches.en: THE EDUCATIONAL LIFT: pupils beyond the standard design, at either end, need a separate arrangement.
branches.cn: 教育上的拎出：超出标准设计的学童，无论高低端，都需要单独安排。

branches.en: THE ENGINEERING LIFT: loads beyond the design range are checked separately.
branches.cn: 工程上的拎出：超出设计范围的荷载被单独校核。

intro.en: Exceptional is exception plus the relational suffix -al. The adverb exceptionally often weakens into ‘extremely’, a sign of how far the word has travelled from law.
intro.cn: exceptional 是 exception 加关系后缀 -al。副词 exceptionally 常弱化为‘极其’，这说明该词离开法律有多远。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is capere, with the compound excipere and the noun exceptio. The same family yields accept, receive, and capture.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基是 capere，复合动词 excipere，名词 exceptio。同一词族还产生 accept、receive、capture。

items.example: The rule has one exception.
items.exampleCN: 这条规则有一个例外。

items.example: The result was exceptional for its consistency.
items.exampleCN: 这个结果因一致性而异常出色。

items.example: The winter was exceptionally mild.
items.exampleCN: 这个冬天异常温和。

items.example: The study examined exceptionality in early readers.
items.exampleCN: 该研究考察早期阅读者的超常现象。

items.meaning: the belief that a group is uniquely exempt from common rules
items.meaningCN: 例外论；认为某群体独特而不受共同规则约束的信念
items.example: The speech appealed to a sense of national exceptionalism.
items.exampleCN: 演讲诉诸一种民族例外论情感。

items.example: No one except the porter was allowed in.
items.exampleCN: 除搬运工外，任何人都不许进入。

items.example: The remark was exceptionable and was withdrawn.
items.exampleCN: 那句话可遭反对，因而被撤回。

items.example: Her references were unexceptionable.
items.exampleCN: 她的推荐信无可指摘。

items.example: He accepted the terms without complaint.
items.exampleCN: 他毫无怨言地接受了条件。

items.example: The sensor captured a faint signal.
items.exampleCN: 传感器捕捉到一个微弱信号。

definition_zh: 方法论的；方法上的；方法论层面的；方法学上的；方法严谨的；学科方法论的；方法论个人主义的；方法多元的
definition_en: relating to methodology, that is, to the principles and rules by which methods of inquiry are chosen and justified
core_image: 一张路线图被放到灯下，人们争论的不是哪条路好走，而是这张图本身画得对不对
scene: 这里指「方法论的」。 The map is placed under a lamp, and the argument is no longer about which road to take but about how the map was drawn: that argument is methodological.
sceneCN: 这里 methodological 是「方法论层面的」（第 3 个义项：方法论层面的争论）；句意：地图被放到灯下，争论的不再是该走哪条路，而是这张图本身是怎么画的，这就是方法论层面的争论。图中可辨识物件：地图、台灯、放大镜、岔口标注、指向图面的两只手。

pos.zh: 方法论的；方法上的；方法论层面的

derivatives.zh: 在方法论上；从方法角度

senses.title: Relating to the theory of methods
senses.titleCN: 方法论的：关于方法理论的
senses.definition: relating to methodology as the study of the principles behind methods of inquiry
senses.definitionCN: 指与作为「研究方法背后原则之研究」的方法论有关的
senses.example: The book's contribution is methodological rather than empirical.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书的贡献在于方法论，而不在于实证。
senses.why: Methodology plus -ical gives a relating adjective. The word points at the theory of method, so a methodological point is about how inquiry should be set up, not about what was found.
senses.whyCN: methodology 加 -ical 构成关系形容词。这个词指向方法的理论，因此「方法论上的观点」说的是探究应如何设置，而不是发现了什么。

senses.title: Of the methods used in a particular study
senses.titleCN: 方法上的：关于某项研究所用的方法
senses.definition: relating to the specific methods and procedures adopted in a study, as opposed to its subject matter
senses.definitionCN: 指与某项研究具体采用的方法和程序有关，而非与其研究对象有关
senses.example: The two papers differ on methodological grounds: one uses interviews, the other surveys.
senses.exampleCN: 这两篇论文的差别在方法上：一篇用访谈，一篇用问卷。
senses.why: Here the adjective descends from theory to practice and simply means 'of the methods used'. The same form covers both the abstract principles and the concrete instruments.
senses.whyCN: 这里形容词从理论落到实践，只表示「所用的方法之属」。同一形式既覆盖抽象原则，也覆盖具体工具。

senses.title: A debate about how research is done
senses.titleCN: 方法论层面的：争论的是做法本身
senses.definition: describing a disagreement about how research should be conducted rather than about its results
senses.definitionCN: 指关于研究应如何进行的争论，而不是关于研究结果的争论
senses.example: The quarrel between the two schools is methodological, not political.
senses.exampleCN: 两个学派之间的争执是方法论层面的，不是政治性的。
senses.why: When scholars disagree about whether to count or to interpret, the dispute is not about facts but about the rules for producing facts. English marks that level with this adjective.
senses.whyCN: 当学者争论该计数还是该解释时，争的不是事实，而是产生事实的规则。英语用这个形容词标记这一层级。

senses.title: A methodological flaw: a fault in the design
senses.titleCN: 方法学缺陷：设计本身的毛病
senses.definition: describing a weakness in the design, sampling or analysis that undermines a study's conclusions
senses.definitionCN: 指研究设计、取样或分析中的弱点，足以削弱其结论
senses.example: Reviewers found a methodological flaw in the sampling procedure.
senses.exampleCN: 评审在取样程序中发现了一处方法学缺陷。
senses.why: A flaw is methodological when the results might be right but the route to them was faulty. The word locates the error in the plan, not in the data.
senses.whyCN: 当结果也许没错、但通往结果的路线有问题时，缺陷就是方法学上的。这个词把错误定位在计划里，而不是数据里。

senses.title: Methodological rigour: strictness about procedure
senses.titleCN: 方法严谨：对程序一丝不苟
senses.definition: describing the strictness and consistency with which methods are applied and reported
senses.definitionCN: 指方法被应用与报告时的严格与一致程度
senses.example: The study is praised for its methodological rigour.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究因方法严谨而受到称赞。
senses.why: Rigour here means that every step can be inspected and repeated. The adjective turns methodology into a standard of quality that a reader can check.
senses.whyCN: 这里的严谨指每一步都可被检查、可被重复。形容词把方法论变成一种读者可以核查的质量标准。

senses.title: Of a discipline's characteristic approach
senses.titleCN: 学科方法论的：某学科特有的做法
senses.definition: describing the approach typical of a discipline, such as the methodological outlook of economics or history
senses.definitionCN: 指某学科典型的方法进路，如经济学或历史学的方法论取向
senses.example: Each discipline has its own methodological habits.
senses.exampleCN: 每个学科都有自己的方法论习惯。
senses.why: Disciplines differ less in what they study than in how they argue. The adjective names those shared habits of proof that make a field recognisable to its members.
senses.whyCN: 学科之间的差别，与其说在研究对象，不如说在论证方式。这个形容词指那些共享的论证习惯，正是它们让一个领域对其成员可辨认。

senses.title: Methodological individualism: explain by individuals
senses.titleCN: 方法论个人主义：用个体来解释整体
senses.definition: in social science, the principle that social facts should be explained through the actions of individual people
senses.definitionCN: 社会科学中的原则：社会事实应通过个人的行动来解释
senses.example: Methodological individualism rejects explanations that treat groups as agents.
senses.exampleCN: 方法论个人主义拒绝把群体当作行动者的解释。
senses.why: Here the adjective names a rule about what may count as an explanation. It is methodology applied to the question of which entities are allowed to act in a theory.
senses.whyCN: 这里形容词命名的是「什么才算解释」的规则。它是把方法论用在「理论中允许哪些实体行动」这一问题上。

senses.title: Methodological pluralism: several methods accepted
senses.titleCN: 方法多元：承认多种方法并存
senses.definition: the view that a field should accept several methods rather than insist on one
senses.definitionCN: 认为一个领域应接受多种方法、而不强求唯一方法的立场
senses.example: Methodological pluralism lets one question be answered by experiment and by interview.
senses.exampleCN: 方法多元让同一个问题既可用实验、也可用访谈来回答。
senses.why: Pluralism about methods is a claim about the rules of inquiry, not about the world. The adjective keeps it on the level of methodology, where such claims belong.
senses.whyCN: 方法多元是关于探究规则的主张，而不是关于世界的主张。形容词把它保持在方法论层面，这类主张正属于该层面。

intro.en: Methodological is methodology plus -ical, the adjective ending that came into English from Latin -icalis and Greek -ikos. Methodology itself is a learned coinage of around 1800 from Greek methodos 'way of inquiry' plus -logia 'study of'. The adjective is recorded in the 19th century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: methodological 是 methodology 加 -ical，这个形容词词尾经拉丁语 -icalis 与希腊语 -ikos 进入英语。methodology 本身是 1800 年前后用希腊语 methodos「探究之路」加 -logia「研究」造出的学术词。该形容词在 19 世纪见于记载。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Methodological becomes a common label in reviews, where a fault in design is called methodological rather than factual.
items.cn: methodological 在评审语言中成为常用标签，设计上的毛病被称为方法层面的，而不是事实层面的。

items.en: The adjective is recorded alongside the noun, as philosophy of science begins to discuss the rules of method explicitly.
items.cn: 这个形容词与名词一同见于记载，正值科学哲学开始明确讨论方法规则之时。

items.en: Methodology is coined from Greek pieces, at first naming the theory of method rather than a set of methods.
items.cn: methodology 用希腊成分造出，最初指方法的理论，而不是一套方法。

items.en: methodos 'way of inquiry' joins meta- 'after, beyond' with hodos 'way'; -logia names the study of something.
items.cn: methodos「探究之路」由 meta-「在后、超出」与 hodos「路」构成；-logia 意为对某事物的研究。

items.en: The adjective ending -icalis supplies the English -ical, and Latin methodus carries the Greek noun into European learning.
items.cn: 形容词词尾 -icalis 提供英语的 -ical，拉丁语 methodus 则把这个希腊名词带入欧洲学术。

note.en: The first group separates a genuinely different adjective and a mere rhyme from the true family; the second compares neighbouring adjectives of planning and execution.
note.cn: 第一组把一个真正不同的形容词与一个只是押韵的词从同族中分出来；第二组比较规划与执行层面相邻的形容词。

entries.definition: orderly and systematic in one's habits. It describes a person or a way of working, not the theory of method, so a methodical worker is not thereby methodological.
entries.definitionCN: 指习惯上有条理、有系统。它描述人或工作方式，而不是方法的理论，因此一个有条理的人并不因此就是方法论意义上的。

entries.definition: the study of methods, or a system of methods. The adjective merely turns this noun into a modifier.
entries.definitionCN: 对方法的研究，或一套方法体系。形容词只是把这个名词变成修饰语。

entries.definition: relating to weather. It comes from meteōron 'a thing raised in the air', not from methodos, and shares only a similar sound.
entries.definitionCN: 与天气有关的。它出自 meteōron「升到空中的东西」，并非来自 methodos，只是读音相近。

entries.definition: relating to the steps that must be followed. It names the execution of a method, where methodological names the reasoning behind the method.
entries.definitionCN: 与必须遵循的步骤有关。它指方法的执行，而 methodological 指方法背后的理由。

entries.definition: done according to a fixed and orderly plan. It praises the order itself, not the justification of the order.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定而有序的计划进行。它称赞的是秩序本身，而不是秩序的理由。

entries.definition: concerned with ideas rather than practice. Methodology can be theoretical, but theoretical work need not be about method at all.
entries.definitionCN: 关心理念而非实践。方法论工作可以是理论的，但理论工作未必与方法的理论有关。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real pieces of the word and its real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想只使用这个词真实的构成成分和真实同族词，不用编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: -logical is the adjective ending that points at a field of study, so methodological points at the study of methods.
normal.cn: -logical 是指向某研究领域的形容词词尾，所以 methodological 指向对方法的研究。

normal.en: Methodical describes a tidy worker; methodological describes an argument about how to work.
normal.cn: methodical 形容人有条理；methodological 形容关于「该怎么做」的论证。

normal.en: The -logia in both words goes back to logos, 'word, reason', so a methodological claim is a claim with reasons.
normal.cn: 两个词里的 -logia 都追溯到 logos「言说、理性」，因此方法论主张是有理由的主张。

normal.en: Greek hodos 'way' is hidden in the middle of the word: methodology is literally the study of roads.
normal.cn: 希腊语 hodos「路」藏在这个词的中段：methodology 字面就是「对路的研究」。

normal.en: A methodological flaw is a flaw in the route, not in the destination.
normal.cn: 方法学缺陷是路线上的缺陷，而不是目的地上的缺陷。

abstract.en: Picture a map being audited: the argument is about the drawing, not the landscape.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图正在被审核：争的是画法，而不是山水本身。

abstract.en: Every methodological question can be rephrased as 'how would we know that?'
abstract.cn: 每个方法论问题都可以改写成：「我们怎么会知道这一点？」

abstract.en: The word marks the level at which a disagreement cannot be settled by more data.
abstract.cn: 这个词标记出那个层级：在那里的分歧无法靠更多数据来解决。

examples.en: The criticism was methodological: the sample was too small to support the claim.
examples.cn: 这个批评是方法层面的：样本太小，支撑不了结论。

examples.en: Their methodological differences made collaboration difficult.
examples.cn: 他们在方法上的分歧让合作变得困难。

examples.en: The paper is methodologically sound but stylistically clumsy.
examples.cn: 这篇论文在方法上站得住，只是文笔笨拙。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「没瑟得逻辑扣」——方法这张图要是逻辑上扣不上，就成方法论问题 → methodological 方法论的

root: 希腊语 methodos「探究之路」＝meta-＋hodos「路」；加 -logia「研究」成 methodology；再加 -ical（拉丁 -icalis、希腊 -ikos）→ methodological。核心是「就路线图本身对不对提出质疑」，而不是讨论路上看到什么。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses keep one image: a map being examined rather than used. What changes is the question asked of it — is it the right theory, which routes were chosen, why the routes differ, where the drawing is faulty, how strict the drawing is, whose habits it shows, or which entities it allows to act.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保留同一个意象：一张被审视而非被使用的地图。变化的只是对它提出的问题——理论对不对、选了哪些路、为何各选各的、画错在哪里、画得多严格、体现谁的习惯，还是允许哪些实体行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a route map held under a lamp while two people argue about how it was drawn.
core.cn: 核心意象：路线图被举到灯下，两个人争论它是怎么画的。

branches.en: FROM THEORY TO PRACTICE: the adjective covers both the principles of method and the concrete methods a study adopted.
branches.cn: 从理论到实践：这个形容词既覆盖方法的原则，也覆盖某项研究实际采用的方法。

branches.en: THE LEVEL OF DISPUTE: when the quarrel is about how facts are produced, the adjective names that level.
branches.cn: 争论层级：当争执在于事实如何产生时，这个形容词命名了该层级。

branches.en: QUALITY CONTROL: a flaw sits in the design, and rigour is the strictness with which the design is followed and reported.
branches.cn: 质量控制：缺陷在设计里，严谨则是设计与报告被遵循的严格程度。

branches.en: DISCIPLINARY HABITS: each field has shared manners of proof that its members recognise at once.
branches.cn: 学科习惯：每个领域都有共享的论证方式，其成员一眼就能认出。

branches.en: RULES OF EXPLANATION: individualism and pluralism decide which entities may act and which methods may be used.
branches.cn: 解释规则：个人主义与多元主义决定哪些实体可以行动、哪些方法可以使用。

intro.en: Methodological is methodology plus -ical. The ending -ical, from Latin -icalis and Greek -ikos, makes a relating adjective; methodology is method plus -ology from Greek -logia.
intro.cn: methodological 是 methodology 加 -ical。词尾 -ical 出自拉丁语 -icalis 与希腊语 -ikos，构成关系形容词；methodology 则是 method 加出自希腊语 -logia 的 -ology。

latinIntro.en: The Greek pieces are meta- 'after, beyond', hodos 'way' and logos 'reason, word', with -ikos forming the adjective. Latin supplies only the carrier forms methodus and -icalis.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊成分是 meta-「在后、超出」、hodos「路」与 logos「理性、言说」，-ikos 构成形容词。拉丁语只提供 methodus 与 -icalis 这两个载体形式。

items.meaning: relating to the principles of method
items.meaningCN: 与方法原则有关的；方法论的
items.example: They raised a methodological objection.
items.exampleCN: 他们提出了一个方法论上的反对意见。

items.meaning: the study of methods, or a method system
items.example: The methodology was described in detail.
items.exampleCN: 研究方法被详细描述。

items.meaning: a way of doing or investigating
items.example: They tried a new method of dating the sample.
items.exampleCN: 他们尝试了一种新的样品测年方法。

items.meaningCN: 有条理的；按步骤行事的
items.example: Her methodical approach saved time later.
items.exampleCN: 她有条理的做法在后来省了时间。

items.example: He methodically recorded every reading.
items.exampleCN: 他有条理地记下每个读数。

items.meaningCN: 在方法论上；从方法角度看
items.example: The study is methodologically innovative.
items.exampleCN: 这项研究在方法上有创新。

items.meaning: one who studies methods of inquiry
items.meaningCN: 方法论研究者；方法学家
items.example: A methodologist joined the review panel.
items.exampleCN: 一位方法学家加入了评审组。

items.structure: meta- (beyond) + analysis (Greek analyein, to break up)
items.meaning: a statistical combining of many study results
items.meaningCN: 元分析；把多项研究结果合并统计（meta- 表示超出）
items.example: The meta-analysis pooled twelve trials.
items.exampleCN: 这项元分析合并了十二项试验。

items.meaningCN: 元数据；描述数据的数据
items.example: The file's metadata records its author.
items.exampleCN: 这个文件的元数据记录着作者。

items.structure: Greek hodos (way), the second element of method
items.meaningCN: 路；道路；行程（method 的第二成分）
items.example: The same hodos appears in period, meaning a way around.
items.exampleCN: 同一个 hodos 也出现在 period 中，原意是绕行的一圈路。

latinEntries.meaning: a pursuit, a way of inquiry
relating to, of the nature of

definition_zh: 海岸线；岸线；水陆交界线；（湖泊、水库的）岸线
definition_en: the line where water meets the land, especially along the sea, a lake or a reservoir; also the strip of land and shallow water on either side of that line
core_image: 一条湿沙与干草之间的细线沿着水面弯过去，浪痕刚留在沙上，又被下一道浪抹平
scene: 风暴过后，牧场外的浅滩被水推开了一道新的边，水与草的分界换了位置。 After the storm a new shoreline curved across the flooded pasture.
sceneCN: 这里 shoreline 指「水与陆地相交的那条线」（第 1 个义项：水陆交界的那条线）；句意：风暴过后，一条新的岸线蜿蜒穿过被淹的牧场。图中可辨识物件：浅水边缘的湿泥、被水推倒的草、弯曲的水痕、低矮的围栏。

pos.zh: 海岸线；岸线；水陆交界线（可指海、湖、水库）
岸带（交界线两侧的陆地与浅水地带）

derivatives.zh: 岸；岸边陆地（shoreline 的第一部分）
线；行；排 / 画线；沿……排列（shoreline 的第二部分）

senses.title: The water's edge as a line
senses.titleCN: 水陆交界的那条线（海岸线）
senses.definition: the line along which the surface of a sea, lake or other water body meets the land
senses.definitionCN: 海水、湖水等水体表面与陆地相接的那条线
senses.example: The shoreline moved a few metres inland after the winter storms.
senses.exampleCN: 冬季风暴过后，岸线向内陆移动了几米。
senses.why: the compound joins a place word to a geometric one, so the referent is not the wet ground but the boundary drawn along it.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词把一个地点词与一个几何词连接起来，所指不是湿地面，而是沿其画出的界线。

senses.title: The shore as a strip
senses.titleCN: 岸带：交界线两侧的陆地与浅水
senses.definition: the belt of land and shallow water on either side of that line, treated as one zone
senses.definitionCN: 交线两侧的陆地与浅水地带，被当作一个整体区域
senses.example: The shoreline zone supports reeds, shellfish and young fish.
senses.exampleCN: 岸带生境养育芦苇、贝类与幼鱼。
senses.why: ecology and planning widen the line into a zone, because processes on land and in water act on each other across the belt.
senses.whyCN: 生态学与规划把这条线放宽为一个带，因为陆上与水中的过程在这条带上相互作用。

senses.title: Lake and reservoir edge
senses.titleCN: 湖岸线与水库岸线（非海洋水体）
senses.definition: the corresponding edge of a lake, reservoir or impounded river, which may rise and fall with the water level
senses.definitionCN: 湖泊、水库或拦河蓄水体的相应边缘，会随水位升降而移动
senses.example: The reservoir shoreline drops sharply each dry season.
senses.exampleCN: 每逢旱季，水库岸线都会大幅下退。
senses.why: line in the compound is neutral about salt water, so the word covers any standing water body with a defined edge.
senses.whyCN: 复合词里的线一词对咸淡并无限定，因此凡有明确边缘的静水体都能用它。

senses.title: Erosion and shifting
senses.definition: the retreat, advance or reshaping of that line under waves, currents, tides and sediment supply
senses.definitionCN: 在波浪、水流、潮汐与泥沙供给作用下，这条线的后退、前进或改变形状
senses.example: Groynes were built to slow shoreline erosion.
senses.exampleCN: 人们修建丁坝以减缓岸线侵蚀。
senses.why: a line that can be mapped can also be measured over time, so the noun becomes the object of erosion studies.
senses.whyCN: 可以画在图上的一条线也能随时间测量，于是这个名词成了侵蚀研究的对象。

senses.title: Length and shape
senses.titleCN: 岸线长度与形态（测量义）
senses.definition: the measured length and outline of the line, including its curves, headlands and inlets
senses.definitionCN: 这条线的实测长度与轮廓，包括弯折、岬角与湾口
senses.example: The survey recorded a shoreline of eleven kilometres.
senses.exampleCN: 测量记录到的岸线长度为十一公里。
senses.why: once the edge is treated as a curve, its length depends on the scale of measurement, which is why shoreline figures are often qualified.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把边缘当作曲线，其长度就取决于测量尺度，因此岸线数值常需注明条件。

senses.title: Shoreline planning and law
senses.titleCN: 岸线规划与管理（政策义）
senses.definition: the planning, rules and permits that decide what may be built or done along that line
senses.definitionCN: 决定沿线可以建造什么、可以做什么的规划、规则与许可
senses.example: Shoreline management plans set new building back from the water.
senses.exampleCN: 岸线管理规划要求新建筑从水边后退。
senses.why: administration needs a fixed object to regulate, so the physical line becomes a legal boundary with setbacks and permits.
senses.whyCN: 行政管理需要一个固定的管制对象，于是实体线变成带有退让距离与许可的法律边界。

senses.title: Shoreline vegetation and habitat
senses.definition: the plants and animals living along the edge, from dune grass and reeds to mangrove and nesting birds
senses.definitionCN: 沿边缘生活的植物与动物，从沙丘草、芦苇到红树林与筑巢鸟类
senses.example: Shoreline vegetation held the sand in place during the gale.
senses.exampleCN: 大风期间，岸线植被把沙固定住了。
senses.why: the strip sense narrows again to its living cover, since roots at the edge are what bind sediment and shelter young animals.
senses.whyCN: 岸带义再收窄到其活体覆盖层，因为正是边缘的根系固定沉积物并庇护幼小动物。

senses.title: The traced outline on maps
senses.titleCN: 地图与影像上的岸线轮廓（制图义）
senses.definition: the drawn or photographed outline of that boundary on maps, charts and aerial images
senses.definitionCN: 在地图、海图与航拍影像上画出的或拍下的该界线轮廓
senses.example: The old chart shows a shoreline now buried under the port.
senses.exampleCN: 旧海图上画出的岸线如今已被港口压在下面。
senses.why: a map must fix one moment of a moving edge, so the noun also names the printed contour rather than the place itself.
senses.whyCN: 地图必须把移动的边缘固定在某一时刻，因此这个名词也指印出的轮廓，而非地点本身。

intro.en: Shoreline is an English compound of shore and line, recorded in the nineteenth century when coastal surveys began mapping the water's edge. Line descends from Latin linea 'thread, plumb line' through Old French. Shore's own origin is unsettled: it is often linked to Middle Low German schore, but that remains a hypothesis.
intro.cn: shoreline 是 shore 与 line 的英语复合词，19 世纪海岸测量开始测绘水边时见于记载。line 经古法语来自拉丁 linea「线、铅垂线」。shore 本身的来源尚无定论：常被联系到中古低地德语 schore，但这仍属假说。

items.en: Shore in the sense 'land bordering a large body of water' is recorded about 1300; English did not inherit it from Old English, which used other words for the coast.
items.cn: shore 以「邻接大片水体的陆地」义约在 1300 年见于记载；英语并未从古英语继承这个词，古英语用别的词表示海岸。

items.en: The usual suggestion is Middle Low German schore 'shore, bank' or Middle Dutch scorre 'land washed by the sea'; the forms are close, but the borrowing route is unproved.
items.cn: 常见的说法是它来自中古低地德语 schore「岸、滩」或中古荷兰语 scorre「受海冲刷的陆地」；词形相近，但借入途径未得到证明。

items.en: Line goes back to Latin linea 'string, linen thread, plumb line', a derivative of linum 'flax', and to the verb lineare 'to make straight'.
items.cn: line 可回溯到拉丁 linea「绳、亚麻线、铅垂线」，由 linum「亚麻」派生，并关联动词 lineare「使成直线」。

items.en: Old French ligne carried the word into Middle English, where line meant both a cord and a drawn mark.
items.cn: 古法语 ligne 把这个词带入中古英语，line 同时指绳索与画出的记号。

items.en: Shoreline is recorded in the nineteenth century, when hydrographic surveys needed a word for the mapped edge of the water.
items.cn: shoreline 在 19 世纪见于记载，当时水文测量需要一个词来指被测绘的水边界线。

items.en: Source uncertain (shore's origin and shoreline's first date): shore's pre-English source is unsettled and the Low German link is only a hypothesis; the earliest citation of shoreline is approximately dated, and any reconstructed ancestor is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（shore 的来源与 shoreline 的首见年代）：shore 在英语之前的来源无定论，与低地德语的关联仅为假说；shoreline 的最早书证只有约略年代，凡重构的祖形均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds spelling-similar words: shore and its compounds share the first element, while shoring is a homonym from a separate word and is not related at all. Group two holds true near-synonyms that differ in scale, water type or register.
note.cn: 第一组是拼写相近的词：shore 及其复合词共享第一个成分，而 shoring 来自另一个同形异义词，完全不同源。第二组是真近义词，差别在尺度、水体类型或语体。

entries.definition: The land along the edge of a sea or lake; the first element of shoreline, but it names the land, not the boundary line.
entries.definitionCN: 指海或湖边缘的陆地；是 shoreline 的第一个成分，但它指陆地，而不是界线。

entries.definition: Timber or metal props holding up a wall, trench or ship; it belongs to a separate verb shore 'to prop', so it has no connection with the coast.
entries.definitionCN: 指支撑墙体、沟槽或船体的木料或金属撑柱；它属于另一个动词 shore「支撑」，与海岸毫无关联。

entries.definition: A bird that feeds along the water's edge, such as a sandpiper; same first element, but it names an animal, not a line.
entries.definitionCN: 指在水边觅食的鸟，如鹬；第一个成分相同，但指动物而非线。

entries.definition: Towards the shore; same first element, but the suffix makes it a direction word rather than a boundary noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指向岸的方向；第一个成分相同，但后缀使它成为方向词而非界线名词。

entries.definition: The edge of the sea seen as a continuous line, often over a long stretch or on a map; shoreline is more local and also covers lakes.
entries.definitionCN: 指被看作连续线的海缘，常指长距离或地图上的走向；shoreline 更局部，也可指湖泊。

entries.definition: The raised edge of a river or channel; it is the usual word for rivers, while shoreline is usual for seas, lakes and reservoirs.
entries.definitionCN: 指河流或水道隆起的边缘；河岸通常用这个词，而海岸、湖岸与水库岸线通常用 shoreline。

entries.definition: The sloping strip of sand or stones at the water's edge; it names the material surface, while shoreline names the boundary itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指水边由沙或砾石构成的斜坡带；它指物质表面，shoreline 指界线本身。

entries.definition: A literary or archaic word for the shore, especially the ground left bare by the tide; it is poetic where shoreline is technical.
entries.definitionCN: 指岸的书面或古旧说法，尤指退潮后露出的地面；它是诗语，而 shoreline 偏技术。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real compounds and real collocations of the word, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的复合词与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Break the word into its two real parts: shore is the land edge, line is the boundary, and the compound names the boundary itself.
normal.cn: 把词拆成两个真实成分：shore 是陆地边缘，line 是界线，复合词指的就是这条界线。

normal.en: Shoreline change is the standard research term for the measured retreat or advance of the edge.
normal.cn: shoreline change 是衡量岸线后退或前进的标准研究说法。

normal.en: Shoreline management plans are legal documents in many countries, which shows how a physical line becomes policy.
normal.cn: 岸线管理规划在许多国家是有法律效力的文件，这说明一条实体线如何变成政策对象。

normal.en: A reservoir shoreline moves up and down every year, a fact that reminds you the word is not limited to the sea.
normal.cn: 水库岸线每年上下移动，这提醒你这个词并不限于海洋。

normal.en: Shoreline vegetation is the planting used in coastal restoration, because roots at the edge hold sediment.
normal.cn: 岸线植被是海岸修复中采用的种植方式，因为边缘的根系能固定沉积物。

abstract.en: Picture a wet line drawn on sand, erased by the next wave and drawn again a little further in.
abstract.cn: 想象湿沙上画着一条线，下一道浪把它抹掉，又在稍里侧重新画出来。

abstract.en: Picture a map where the blue and the green touch along one thin contour, and that contour is the whole subject.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，蓝与绿沿着一条细轮廓相接，而这条轮廓就是全部主题。

abstract.en: Picture houses set back from the water while the line between water and land creeps towards them year by year.
abstract.cn: 想象房屋从水边后退，而水陆之间的那条线年复一年向它们爬来。

examples.en: The shoreline shifted inland after three days of high waves.
examples.cn: 三天大浪之后，岸线向内陆移动了。

examples.en: Reeds along the shoreline shelter young fish from the current.
examples.cn: 岸线边的芦苇为幼鱼遮挡水流。

examples.en: The lake shoreline is lowest at the end of the dry season.
examples.cn: 旱季末尾，湖岸线退到最低处。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「shoreline」读似「秀来恩」——「秀」像岸，「来恩」像一条线，岸上来了线，就是岸线

root: 英语复合词，由 shore + line 构成。shore 来源不确定，一般认为与中古低地德语 schore「岸、滩」、中古荷兰语 scorre 有关，属假说；line 来自拉丁 linea「亚麻线、铅垂线」（经古法语 ligne）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from one geometric fact: water and land meet along a line. That line is then widened into a strip, moved to lakes and reservoirs, watched as it shifts, measured, governed, planted, and finally printed on a map.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都始于一个几何事实：水与陆沿着一条线相接。这条线随后被放宽成一条带，移到湖泊与水库，被观察其移动、被测量、被管制、被种上植物，最后被印在地图上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin wet line curving between water and land.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条细而湿的线，在水与陆地之间弯过。

branches.en: THE LINE: the simplest reading, the boundary itself.
branches.cn: 那条线：最简单的读法，即界线本身。

branches.en: THE DRAWN LINE: maps and images turn the boundary into an outline.
branches.cn: 被画出的线：地图与影像把界线变成轮廓。

branches.en: THE ZONE AND OTHER WATERS: the edge as a strip, and the same edge on lakes and reservoirs.
branches.cn: 岸带与其他水体：边缘成了一条带，同样也出现在湖泊与水库上。

branches.en: A LINE THAT MOVES: erosion shifts it, survey measures it.
branches.cn: 会移动的线：侵蚀使它移动，测量把它量出。

branches.en: A LINE THAT IS GOVERNED AND PLANTED: plans set it back, roots hold it.
branches.cn: 被治理与被种植的线：规划让它后退，根系把它固定。

intro.en: Shoreline is a native-English compound, not a suffixed derivation: shore and line each arrive whole, and the compound simply puts the two nouns together. Its wider family comes from compounds and prefixes built on shore, and from the many words built on line.
intro.cn: shoreline 是英语本族复合词，不是加后缀的派生：shore 与 line 各自完整进入，复合词只是把两个名词并置。它更大的词族来自以 shore 构成的复合词与前缀形式，以及由 line 构成的大量词。

latinIntro.en: Only the second element has a Latin source: linea 'thread, plumb line'. Shore has no Latin ancestor; Latin litus 'shore' and ora 'coast' translate the idea but are not related to it, so the entries below cover the line side only.
latinIntro.cn: 只有第二个成分有拉丁来源：linea「线、铅垂线」。shore 没有拉丁语祖先；拉丁 litus「岸」与 ora「海岸」只是语义对应词，并非其来源，因此下列条目只覆盖 line 这一侧。

items.meaning: the land along the edge of water
items.example: We walked along the shore at low tide.
items.exampleCN: 退潮时我们沿着岸走。

items.meaning: a long thin mark; a boundary
items.example: A line of stones marks the path.
items.exampleCN: 一排石头标出小路。

items.meaning: the edge where water meets land
items.example: The shoreline is mapped every five years.
items.exampleCN: 岸线每五年测绘一次。

items.example: Shoreland owners need a permit to build.
items.exampleCN: 沿岸陆地的业主建房需要许可。

items.example: The current pushed the boat shoreward.
items.exampleCN: 水流把小船推向岸边。

items.example: Longshore drift moves sand along the beach.
items.exampleCN: 沿岸流把沙沿着海滩搬运。

items.meaning: towards or on the land from the sea
items.example: An onshore wind kept the beach cool.
items.exampleCN: 向岸风让海滩保持凉爽。

items.meaning: away from the shore, out at sea
items.example: The turbine stands offshore, beyond the surf.
items.exampleCN: 风机立在离岸处，在碎浪之外。

items.meaning: a bird that feeds at the water's edge
items.example: Shorebirds gather on the flats at low tide.
items.exampleCN: 退潮时岸鸟聚集在滩上。

latinEntries.meaning: a line, string, linen thread, plumb line
of a line; made of lines
a line, an outline, a feature

definition_zh: （美式）主菜；（英式）开胃菜；进入的途径
definition_en: the main dish of a meal in American usage, or a way of being admitted to a group or activity
core_image: 菜单翻到中间那页，最贵的一盘被端上桌；另一层含义是有人替你把门推开
scene: 这家店的主菜选择很少，多数客人转而点面食。 The entree list was short, so many guests chose pasta.
sceneCN: 这里 entree 是「主菜」（第 1 个义项：美式用法中的正餐主盘）；句意：主菜清单很短，许多客人选了面食。

pos.zh: 主菜；开胃菜；进入的途径

senses.title: The main dish of a meal
senses.definition: the principal dish served in the middle of a meal, listed on menus
senses.definitionCN: 正餐中段上桌的主盘，通常列在菜单上
senses.example: Pick an entree before the soup arrives.
senses.exampleCN: 在汤上桌前选好主菜。
senses.why: The French word meant an entering, and the dish that enters the table is the one served in the middle.
senses.whyCN: 法语原义为进入，而登上桌的那道菜就成了中段的主盘。

senses.title: A course served at the start of a meal
senses.definition: in British and formal use, the first small course after which the main dish follows
senses.definitionCN: 在英式与正式用法中指紧随其后的第一小盘
senses.example: The set menu begins with a cold entree.
senses.exampleCN: 套餐以一道冷头盘开场。
senses.why: Old French menus placed the entrée first, so the older English use kept the opening position.
senses.whyCN: 古法语菜单把 entrée 列在首位，因此较早的英语用法保留开席的位置。

senses.title: A way of being admitted to a group
senses.definition: something that gives a person access to a profession or social circle
senses.definitionCN: 使人得以进入某职业或社交圈的凭借
senses.example: A internship can be an entree into journalism.
senses.exampleCN: 实习可能成为进入新闻行业的门径。
senses.why: Transferred from the door of a dining room to the door of a career, the noun keeps the idea of being let in.
senses.whyCN: 从餐厅的门转移到职业的门，这个名词保留了被放入的概念。

intro.en: Entree is the French entrée, a noun of entering from entrer, which continues Latin intrare.
intro.cn: entree 即法语 entrée，表进入的名词，出自 entrer，承自拉丁语 intrare。

items.en: Intrare means to go into.
items.cn: intrare 意为进入。

items.en: Entrer and its noun entry carry the sense inward.
items.cn: entrer 及名词 entry 把词义带入法语。

items.en: French dining menus use entrée for the opening dish.
items.cn: 十七世纪法式菜单以 entrée 称首盘。

items.en: English cookery books borrow the word with the menu.
items.cn: 十八世纪英语食谱连同菜单借入该词。

items.en: American restaurants shift the term to the main plate.
items.cn: 十九世纪美国餐馆把该词转指主盘。

items.en: Figurative use names any door into a profession.
items.cn: 现代英语中以比喻指进入某行业的门径。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same entering stem; group two holds other course and access words.
note.cn: 第一组是同一进入词干的词；第二组是其他表示菜品或门路的词。

entries.definition: The written French form, still seen on menus that keep the accent.
entries.definitionCN: 保留重音符号的法语写法，菜单上仍可见。

entries.definition: The ordinary English noun of entering, from the same French stem.
entries.definitionCN: 英语中表进入的普通名词，与它同词干。

entries.definition: An idiom of chain restaurants, where the phrase sits beside a list of plates.
entries.definitionCN: 连锁餐馆的说法，指与主菜并列的项。

entries.definition: The starter in British usage, which overlaps the older sense of the word.
entries.definitionCN: 英式头盘，与该词的旧义部分重叠。

entries.definition: The unambiguous British name for the central dish.
entries.definitionCN: 英式对主盘不含混的说法。

entries.definition: The first plate in British menus, matching the older entree sense.
entries.definitionCN: 英式菜单的第一盘，对应旧义。

entries.definition: A route into a field, used in the figurative sense.
entries.definitionCN: 进入某领域的路径，用于比喻义。

entries.definition: A position secured inside a group, as in get a footing.
entries.definitionCN: 在群体中站稳的位置，如 get a footing。

normalIntro.en: Think of a door: the American reading is the dish that enters the table, and the figurative reading is the door itself.
normalIntro.cn: 把词想成一扇门：美式指登上桌的菜，比喻义就是门本身。

normal.en: In the United States the entree is the main plate.
normal.cn: 在美国，entree 指主盘。

normal.en: In Britain it can mean the course that comes first.
normal.cn: 在英国它可指最先上的那道。

normal.en: Say an entree into a field for the access sense.
normal.cn: 表进入某领域时说 an entree into a field。

normal.en: Menus keep the accent mark in formal writing.
normal.cn: 正式菜单书写常保留重音符号。

normal.en: Do not spell it envelope; the ending is the same as in entry.
normal.cn: 不要拼作 envelope；词尾与 entry 相同。

abstract.en: Picture a waiter lifting a cover off the central plate.
abstract.cn: 想象侍者揭开中间餐盘的盖。

abstract.en: Imagine the first page of a menu turning itself.
abstract.cn: 想象菜单第一页自己翻动。

abstract.en: Think of a card that admits you through a side door.
abstract.cn: 想想一张带你走侧门入场的卡。

examples.en: The restaurant lists three entrees and six sides.
examples.cn: 这家餐厅列出三道主菜与六种配菜。

examples.en: Fluent French was her entree into diplomacy.
examples.cn: 流利的法语是她进入外交界的门径。

examples.en: A tasting entree arrives in small bowls.
examples.cn: 一份试味头盘用小碗端上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺来」——音近 entree，菜端上来时说俺来了，所以是主菜或头盘；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 intrare（进入）→ 古法语 entrer／entrée → 英语 entree，核心义「进入；登桌的首盘」，与 entry 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The noun names a dish by its place in the meal and, by transfer, a person's place at the door of a career.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词按菜品在餐席中的位置命名，并由此转移到人在职业门口的位子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the thing that comes in first, whether a plate or a person.
core.cn: 核心意象：最先入席者，无论是一盘菜还是一位客人。

branches.en: American menus fix the word on the central dish.
branches.cn: 美式菜单把词固定在中间那道。

branches.en: Older usage keeps it at the opening of the meal.
branches.cn: 较早用法把它留在开席位置。

branches.en: The door image transfers the word to professions.
branches.cn: 门的意象把词转移到职业领域。

branches.en: Both readings are menu positions that vary by country.
branches.cn: 两义都是随地区不同的菜单位置。

branches.en: Being first in and being let in share one idea.
branches.cn: 先入席与被放入共享同一概念。

intro.en: A Latin prefix of inward motion plus a French nominal ending forms this borrowed noun.
intro.cn: 拉丁语表向内的前缀加法语名词词尾构成这个借入名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin In means into and intra means within; intrare is the verb of going in.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 in 表向内，intra 表在内，intrare 是进入的动词。

items.example: Intrare is the source verb.
items.exampleCN: intrare 是源头动词。

items.meaning: a door or the right to enter
