items.exampleCN: entrance 保留入场义。

items.example: Intrude also continues intrare.
items.exampleCN: intrude 同样承自 intrare。

items.example: The old term survives in menus.
items.exampleCN: 旧称在菜单中残留。

definition_zh: 呼吸频率；每分钟呼吸次数
definition_en: the number of breaths a person or animal takes in one minute, used as a basic physiological measure
core_image: 一只秒表与一起一伏的胸口，旁边记着每分钟的次数
scene: 这里指「呼吸频率」。 A respiration rate above twenty can be an early warning sign.
sceneCN: 这里 respiration rate 指「呼吸频率」（第 1 个义项：每分钟呼吸的次数，作为生理指标）；句意：呼吸频率超过二十次可能是早期警报信号。图中可辨识物件：秒表、起伏的胸廓、计数板、监护仪数值。

pos.zh: 呼吸频率；每分钟呼吸次数（可数，常用单数形式作指标名）

senses.title: Breaths per minute
senses.titleCN: 呼吸频率：每分钟呼吸次数
senses.definition: the count of complete breaths taken in one minute
senses.definitionCN: 一分钟内完成的完整呼吸次数
senses.example: A respiration rate above twenty can be an early warning sign.
senses.exampleCN: 呼吸频率超过二十次可能是早期警报信号。
senses.why: Rate turns an action into a countable quantity per unit time, so breathing becomes a number.
senses.whyCN: rate 把动作变成单位时间内的可计数量，于是呼吸变成了一个数字。

senses.title: Resting rate
senses.titleCN: 静息呼吸频率：安静状态下的基线值
senses.definition: the rate measured while the subject is calm, seated and not speaking
senses.definitionCN: 受试者安静坐着、不说话时测得的数值
senses.example: Her resting respiration rate is fourteen.
senses.exampleCN: 她的静息呼吸频率是十四次。
senses.why: Baselines require a controlled state, so the phrase is qualified by 'resting'.
senses.whyCN: 基线需要受控状态，因此这个短语常用 resting 限定。

senses.title: Rate during exertion
senses.titleCN: 运动时的呼吸频率：随耗氧上升
senses.definition: the rate reached during exercise or hard work, which rises with oxygen demand
senses.definitionCN: 运动或重体力劳动时达到的频率，随需氧量上升
senses.example: His respiration rate doubled during the sprint.
senses.exampleCN: 短跑时他的呼吸频率翻了一倍。
senses.why: The measure is useful precisely because it tracks effort, so an exertional sense is standard.
senses.whyCN: 这个指标之所以有用，正因为它跟随用力程度，因此运动义是标准用法。

senses.title: Abnormal rate
senses.titleCN: 异常呼吸频率：过速或过缓
senses.definition: a rate outside the expected range, faster (tachypnea) or slower (bradypnea) than normal
senses.definitionCN: 超出预期范围的频率，比正常更快（呼吸过速）或更慢（呼吸过缓）
senses.example: A falling respiration rate worried the night nurse.
senses.exampleCN: 呼吸频率下降让夜班护士担心。
senses.why: Clinical language needs to name deviation, so the phrase carries a diagnostic sense.
senses.whyCN: 临床语言需要命名偏离，因此这个短语带有诊断义。

senses.title: A vital sign
senses.titleCN: 生命体征：入院与查房必测的指标
senses.definition: one of the standard vital signs recorded with temperature, pulse and blood pressure
senses.definitionCN: 与体温、脉搏、血压一起记录的标准生命体征之一
senses.example: The nurse wrote the respiration rate on the observation chart.
senses.exampleCN: 护士把呼吸频率写在观察记录表上。
senses.why: Hospitals standardized four or six vital signs, and breathing was reduced to one of them.
senses.whyCN: 医院把生命体征标准化为四项或六项，呼吸被简化为其中一项。

senses.title: An animal measure
senses.titleCN: 动物生理指标：实验与养殖中的测量
senses.definition: the breathing rate of an animal, used in laboratory physiology or livestock monitoring
senses.definitionCN: 动物的呼吸频率，用于实验室生理学或养殖监测
senses.example: The calves' respiration rate rose in the hot shed.
senses.exampleCN: 犊牛在炎热的棚里呼吸频率上升。
senses.why: The measure is species-neutral, so it travels from clinics to barns and laboratories.
senses.whyCN: 这个指标不区分物种，因此从诊所走进畜舍与实验室。

senses.title: Sleep monitoring
senses.titleCN: 睡眠呼吸监测：夜间频率变化
senses.definition: the rate tracked overnight to detect pauses or drops in breathing during sleep
senses.definitionCN: 夜间持续追踪的频率，用于发现睡眠中的呼吸暂停或下降
senses.example: The sleep study logged her respiration rate every thirty seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 睡眠监测每三十秒记录一次她的呼吸频率。
senses.why: Sleep studies need a continuous record rather than one measurement, so the compound names a value tracked through the night.
senses.whyCN: 睡眠监测需要连续记录而非一次测量，因此这个复合词命名的是整夜被追踪的数值。

senses.title: Component of ventilation
senses.titleCN: 每分通气量的组成：频率乘潮气量
senses.definition: one factor in minute ventilation, which equals respiration rate multiplied by tidal volume
senses.definitionCN: 每分通气量的一个因子，通气量等于呼吸频率乘以潮气量
senses.example: Minute ventilation rises when either the respiration rate or the tidal volume increases.
senses.exampleCN: 呼吸频率或潮气量任一上升，每分通气量都会增加。
senses.why: Physiology treats the rate as one multiplier in a product, not as an isolated number.
senses.whyCN: 生理学把频率看作乘积中的一个乘数，而非孤立的数字。

senses.title: How it is counted
senses.titleCN: 计数方法：观察胸廓起伏计时一分钟
senses.definition: the practical procedure of counting chest rises for a full minute, or for fifteen seconds and multiplying
senses.definitionCN: 观察胸廓起伏满一分钟，或数十五秒再乘以四的实用方法
senses.example: Count the respiration rate while the patient thinks you are taking the pulse.
senses.exampleCN: 趁病人以为你在测脉搏时数呼吸频率。
senses.why: The phrase also names the measurement act, because a rate must be produced by counting.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语也命名测量动作，因为频率必须通过计数才能得出。

intro.en: Respiration rate joins Latin respiratio 'breathing' to rate, from Latin rata pars 'a fixed portion'. The compound is a modern physiological label. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: respiration rate 把拉丁 respiratio「呼吸」与 rate 连接起来，后者出自拉丁 rata pars「固定的份额」。这个复合词是现代生理学标签。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Respiratio, from respirare 'to breathe again', named breathing as an action.
items.cn: respiratio 出自 respirare「再次呼吸」，把呼吸命名成一个动作。

items.en: Rate descends from Latin rata pars, 'a reckoned or fixed portion', from reri 'to reckon'. Ratio and ration belong to the same family.
items.cn: rate 出自拉丁 rata pars「经计算或固定的份额」，源于 reri「计算」。ratio 与 ration 属同一词族。

items.en: English rate first meant an estimated value or a fixed charge, and only later a measured amount per unit of time.
items.cn: 英语 rate 最初指估算的价值或固定费用，后来才指单位时间内的测量量。

items.en: Nineteenth-century physiology began expressing breathing as a frequency per minute, making it comparable between patients.
items.cn: 19 世纪生理学开始把呼吸表示成每分钟的频率，使不同病人之间可以比较。

items.en: Twentieth-century hospital practice fixed respiration rate as a vital sign; 'respiratory rate' became the more common clinical wording.
items.cn: 20 世纪医院实践把 respiration rate 固定为生命体征；respiratory rate 成为更常见的临床说法。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the exact date when the compound was first written is uncertain, and the deeper root behind reri is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词根）：这个复合词首次书写的年代存疑；reri 背后的更深词根属重构形式。

note.en: The first group holds closely related terms that are easily confused in clinical use; the second holds near-synonyms for the measured frequency of breathing.
note.cn: 第一组是临床使用中容易混淆的近邻术语；第二组是「测得的呼吸频率」的近义词。

entries.definition: The usual clinical wording for the same measurement; it is largely interchangeable with respiration rate.
entries.definitionCN: 同一测量在临床上的常用说法，与 respiration rate 基本可互换。

entries.definition: The number of heartbeats per minute; it counts the pump, not the breath.
entries.definitionCN: 每分钟心跳次数；数的是泵，不是呼吸。

entries.definition: The volume of air moved per minute, a product of rate and tidal volume; it is not the breath count itself.
entries.definitionCN: 每分钟移动的空气体积，等于频率乘潮气量，并不是呼吸次数本身。

entries.definition: The breathing process; adding rate makes it a quantity rather than an activity.
entries.definitionCN: 呼吸过程；加上 rate 之后，它变成一个量而非活动。

entries.definition: A plain-language equivalent of respiration rate, common in physiology and animal science.
entries.definitionCN: respiration rate 的通俗同义说法，常见于生理学与动物科学。

entries.definition: The total volume of air breathed per minute; it rises with rate but is measured in litres, not breaths.
entries.definitionCN: 每分钟吸入的空气总量；随频率上升，但以升计量，而非次数。

entries.definition: The palpable beat of the arteries, used as a quick check on heart rate rather than breathing.
entries.definitionCN: 可触及的动脉搏动，用来快速判断心率而非呼吸。

entries.definition: The air moved in one ordinary breath; paired with rate, it determines minute ventilation.
entries.definitionCN: 一次平常呼吸所移动的空气量；与频率配对决定每分通气量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: respiration + rate: breathing expressed as a count per minute.
normal.cn: respiration + rate：把呼吸表示成每分钟的次数。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the clinic: resting respiration rate, elevated respiration rate, normal respiration rate.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出临床语境：静息呼吸频率、呼吸频率升高、正常呼吸频率。

normal.en: rate comes from Latin rata pars 'fixed portion', the same family as ratio and ration.
normal.cn: rate 出自拉丁 rata pars「固定份额」，与 ratio、ration 同族。

normal.en: Minute ventilation = respiration rate × tidal volume.
normal.cn: 每分通气量 = 呼吸频率 × 潮气量。

normal.en: Clinicians often say respiratory rate and write RR.
normal.cn: 临床医生常说 respiratory rate，并缩写为 RR。

abstract.en: Picture a stopwatch and a counting hand rising and falling with each chest movement.
abstract.cn: 想象一只秒表，与胸口起伏同步抬起落下的计数手指。

abstract.en: Picture a monitor beside a hospital bed showing a small green number for breaths.
abstract.cn: 想象病床旁的监护仪上，一个绿色小数字显示呼吸次数。

abstract.en: Picture a night-time chart with a line that dips whenever breathing slows.
abstract.cn: 想象一张夜间图表，呼吸变慢时曲线随之下沉。

examples.en: An adult's normal resting respiration rate is about twelve to twenty.
examples.cn: 成年人正常的静息呼吸频率约为每分钟十二到二十次。

examples.en: Fever and pain can raise the respiration rate.
examples.cn: 发热与疼痛会使呼吸频率升高。

examples.en: The monitor alarms when the respiration rate falls below eight.
examples.cn: 当呼吸频率低于八次时，监护仪会报警。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「respiration 呼吸 + rate 速率」——每分钟呼吸多少次 → respiration rate 呼吸频率

root: 拉丁 respiratio「呼吸」+ 英语 rate（出自拉丁 rata pars「固定份额」）→ 现代生理学复合词 respiration rate。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one number: a count of breaths per minute can be a baseline, an exertion value, a warning, a vital sign, an animal measure, a sleep record, a multiplier in ventilation, or a procedure for counting.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个数字展开：每分钟呼吸次数可以是基线值、运动值、警报、生命体征、动物指标、睡眠记录、通气量中的乘数，也可以是一套计数操作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stopwatch beside a chest, turning each rise and fall into a count.
core.cn: 核心意象：胸旁的一只秒表，把每次起伏变成一个计数。

branches.en: THE NUMBER AND ITS MAKING: the rate is both a quantity and the procedure of counting that produces it.
branches.cn: 数字与制法：频率既是一个量，也是产生这个量的计数操作。

branches.en: TWO CONDITIONS: the same measure is taken at rest as a baseline and under effort as a load.
branches.cn: 两种状态：同一指标在静息时作为基线，在用力时作为负荷。

branches.en: THE CLINIC: deviation from the normal range turns the number into a warning and a vital sign.
branches.cn: 临床：偏离正常范围使这个数字变成警报与生命体征。

branches.en: OTHER BODIES AND OTHER HOURS: the measure travels to animals and to overnight sleep studies.
branches.cn: 别的身体与别的时段：这个指标延伸到动物，也延伸到整夜的睡眠监测。

branches.en: ONE FACTOR IN A PRODUCT: rate multiplied by tidal volume gives minute ventilation.
branches.cn: 乘积中的一个因子：频率乘以潮气量得到每分通气量。

intro.en: Respiration rate is a two-word compound: a Latin noun of breathing plus an English noun of reckoning.
intro.cn: respiration rate 是双词复合：一个拉丁「呼吸」名词加一个英语「计算」名词。

latinIntro.en: Respiratio comes from spirare 'to breathe'; rate comes from Latin rata pars, from reri 'to reckon', the same family as ratio and ration.
latinIntro.cn: respiratio 出自 spirare「呼吸」；rate 出自拉丁 rata pars，源于 reri「计算」，与 ratio、ration 同族。

items.meaningCN: 每分钟计数的呼吸次数
items.example: The respiration rate was recorded at eighteen.
items.exampleCN: 记录的呼吸频率是十八次。

items.meaning: the clinical wording of the same measure
items.meaningCN: 同一指标在临床上的说法
items.example: Respiratory rate is the fourth vital sign.
items.exampleCN: 呼吸频率是第四项生命体征。

items.example: Respiration supplies oxygen to tissues.
items.exampleCN: 呼吸为组织供氧。

items.example: Respiratory disease can alter the rate.
items.exampleCN: 呼吸系统疾病会改变呼吸频率。

items.example: The heart rate rose with fever.
items.exampleCN: 发热时心率上升。

items.example: The ratio of breaths to heartbeats is about one to four.
items.exampleCN: 呼吸与心跳之比约为四比一。

items.example: Each hiker carried a daily ration.
items.exampleCN: 每位徒步者携带一天的配给。

items.meaningCN: 一次呼吸移动的空气量
items.example: Tidal volume and rate together give minute ventilation.
items.exampleCN: 潮气量与频率一起得出每分通气量。

definition_zh: 数据库管理；对数据库进行建立、维护、控制与保障的一整套工作
definition_en: the work of building, maintaining, controlling and protecting a database and the data inside it
core_image: 一间档案室里，成排的抽屉贴着编号标签，管理员拿着登记簿核对每一份进出的卷宗
scene: 档案室里成排的抽屉都贴着编号，管理员拿着登记簿核对每一份进出的卷宗。 Good database management kept the clinic's patient records accurate for twenty years.
sceneCN: 这里 database management 指对数据库进行建立、维护与控制的一整套工作（第 1 个义项：日常管理工作）；句意：良好的数据库管理让这家诊所的病人记录二十年保持准确。

pos.zh: 数据库管理；数据库管理工作；数据库管理系统（作定语）

senses.title: The routine work of keeping a database healthy
senses.titleCN: 维持数据库正常运转的日常工作
senses.definition: the day-to-day work of loading, checking, updating and repairing a database
senses.definitionCN: 对数据库进行装载、检查、更新与修复的日常工作
senses.example: Database management here means nightly checks, not a new product.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的数据库管理指的是每晚的检查，而不是一款新产品。
senses.why: the compound names an activity, so it first means the work people do rather than the tool they use.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词指一项活动，因此首先表示人做的工作，而不是人用的工具。

senses.title: The software system that runs a database
senses.titleCN: 运行数据库的软件系统
senses.definition: the program layer that stores, queries and controls access to data
senses.definitionCN: 负责存储、查询与控制数据访问的程序层
senses.example: The vendor sells database management to hospitals and banks.
senses.exampleCN: 这家厂商把数据库管理系统卖给医院和银行。
senses.why: the phrase is shortened from the longer name of the system, and the activity noun came to stand for the software that performs it.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语由系统全称缩略而来，动作名词转而指执行该动作的软件。

senses.title: The organisational function
senses.definition: the team and role responsible for data holdings inside an organisation
senses.definitionCN: 组织内部负责数据资产团队与岗位
senses.example: Database management sits between the application team and the network team.
senses.exampleCN: 数据库管理处在应用团队与网络团队之间。
senses.why: a repeated technical duty becomes a permanent office, and the duty's name becomes the office's name.
senses.whyCN: 反复出现的技术职责会固定成一个常设岗位，职责之名就成了岗位之名。

senses.title: Control of access and quality
senses.titleCN: 对访问权限与数据质量的控制
senses.definition: the setting of permissions, standards and rules for who may read or change data
senses.definitionCN: 为谁可读取或修改数据设定权限、标准与规则
senses.example: Database management decides which clerk may see the billing table.
senses.exampleCN: 数据库管理决定哪位职员可以查看计费表。
senses.why: a database holds other people's facts, so administration naturally grows into governance.
senses.whyCN: 数据库装着别人的事实，因此「管理」自然长成「治理」。

senses.title: Performance and capacity work
senses.titleCN: 性能与容量方面的工作
senses.definition: the tuning of queries, indexes and storage so that a system stays fast as it grows
senses.definitionCN: 调整查询、索引与存储，使系统在增长中保持速度
senses.example: Slow reports were solved by better database management, not new hardware.
senses.exampleCN: 报告变慢是靠更好的数据库管理解决的，而不是靠新硬件。
senses.why: the practical core of the job is keeping response time acceptable, and that core is named by the compound.
senses.whyCN: 这项工作最实际的核心是让响应时间可接受，复合词就指这个核心。

senses.title: Backup and recovery responsibility
senses.definition: the practice of copying data and restoring it after failure
senses.definitionCN: 复制数据并在故障后恢复的做法
senses.example: Database management proved its worth the night the disk failed.
senses.exampleCN: 磁盘坏掉的那一夜，数据库管理证明了它的价值。
senses.why: the value of administration is clearest after a loss, and the phrase covers that duty too.
senses.whyCN: 管理的价值在损失之后最清楚，这个短语也涵盖这项责任。

senses.title: A course or subject of study
senses.definition: the taught subject covering data models, query languages and administration
senses.definitionCN: 讲授数据模型、查询语言与管理实务的课程
senses.example: The evening course in database management filled in two days.
senses.exampleCN: 那门数据库管理晚间课程两天就报满了。
senses.why: a skill taught in classrooms becomes a subject title, and the activity phrase serves as the title.
senses.whyCN: 在课堂上讲授的技能会变成课程名，活动短语就成了课程名。

senses.title: A product or market category
senses.definition: the commercial class of tools sold for organising and protecting data
senses.definitionCN: 为组织与保护数据而出售的那一类商业工具
senses.example: Analysts rank database management among the steadier software markets.
senses.exampleCN: 分析人士把数据库管理列为较稳定的软件市场之一。
senses.why: an activity that everyone needs becomes a shelf in the market, named after the activity.
senses.whyCN: 人人需要的活动会变成市场上的一个货架，并以活动本身命名。

intro.en: Database management is a twentieth-century compound of three older pieces: Latin data, Greek basis through Latin, and Italian handling through French. Each part kept its own history.
intro.cn: database management 是二十世纪的三段式复合词：拉丁语 data、经拉丁语转手的希腊语 basis，以及经法语进入英语的意大利语「操作」。每一段都保留了自己的来历。

items.en: Latin datum means something given, the neuter participle of dare, to give. Its plural data entered English as a mass of facts.
items.cn: 拉丁语 datum 意为「被给予的东西」，是 dare「给予」的中性分词。其复数 data 进入英语，指一批事实。

items.en: Greek basis meant a step or a pedestal, and Latin basis kept that sense of a supporting bottom before English used it for a foundation of any kind.
items.cn: 希腊语 basis 指台阶或基座，拉丁语 basis 保留了「支撑的底部」之意，后来英语用它指任何基础。

items.en: Italian maneggiare meant to handle or train horses, from mano, hand. French took it as manage and English borrowed the French verb.
items.cn: 意大利语 maneggiare 意为「操作、驯马」，来自 mano「手」。法语借入为 manage，英语又借入这个法语动词。

items.en: English joined data and base in the mid-twentieth century to name a structured store of records held for machine processing.
items.cn: 英语在二十世纪中叶把 data 与 base 拼合，指为机器处理而保存的结构化记录集合。

items.en: Management first meant the handling of a household or an estate, then the running of an enterprise, and only later the care of a technical system.
items.cn: management 原指料理家务或田产，后来指经营企业，再后来才指照管技术系统。

items.en: The full phrase settled once databases became large enough to need a specialist, and it now names both the work and the software that supports it.
items.cn: 当数据库大到需要专职人员时，这个完整短语才固定下来，如今既指这项工作，也指支持它的软件。

note.en: The first group shares the words inside the compound; the second group names neighbouring kinds of information work.
note.cn: 第一组共享复合词内部的几个词；第二组是相邻的信息工作类别。

entries.definition: The organised store itself; management is the work done on it and the system that runs it.
entries.definitionCN: 指被组织起来的存储本身；management 是对它做的工作以及运行它的系统。

entries.definition: The running of people or operations in general; joined to database it loses its staff sense.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指对人或者业务的经营；与 database 组合后不再指人员层面的管理。

entries.definition: The broader discipline covering all data, not only what sits inside one database.
entries.definitionCN: 范围更大的学科，涵盖全部数据，而不只是某个数据库里的内容。

entries.definition: The role that carries out the work; the phrase database management names the work itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指承担这项工作的岗位；database management 指工作本身。

entries.definition: The policy side: who owns data, what may be done with it and who answers for mistakes.
entries.definitionCN: 偏政策的一面：数据归谁所有、可以怎么用、出错谁负责。

entries.definition: An older term for the same control work, often used when the emphasis is on records and standards rather than software.
entries.definitionCN: 指同一类管控工作的旧称，多用于强调记录与规范，而非软件。

entries.definition: The management of all information resources, of which a database is one technical part.
entries.definitionCN: 对全部信息资产的管理，数据库只是其中一个技术部分。

entries.definition: The control of documents through their life cycle, including retention and disposal.
entries.definitionCN: 按生命周期管理文件，包括保存期限与销毁。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations from the three real parts and the real technical phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：来自三个真实构件与真实技术搭配。

normal.en: Data is the Latin plural of datum, something given; a database is a structured gift of facts.
normal.cn: data 是 datum「被给予之物」的拉丁复数；database 就是被整理好的事实。

normal.en: Basis meant a pedestal, so a database is a set of records with a base under it.
normal.cn: basis 原指基座，所以 database 是一批底下有基座的记录。

normal.en: Manage came from handling horses by hand, and the word still carries the sense of steady control.
normal.cn: manage 来自用手照看马匹，至今仍带「稳稳掌控」的意思。

normal.en: The phrase names work and software: database management tasks, database management system.
normal.cn: 这个短语既指工作也指软件：数据库管理任务、数据库管理系统。

normal.en: Three duties anchor it: access control, performance, recovery.
normal.cn: 三项职责锚定它：访问控制、性能、恢复。

abstract.en: Picture a cabinet whose drawers rearrange themselves when someone searches too slowly.
abstract.cn: 想象一个柜子，当有人查找太慢时，抽屉会自己重新排列。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger that refuses to open for a reader who has not signed the register.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账簿，没在登记簿上签名的人打不开它。

abstract.en: Picture a copy of every page kept in another room, waiting for the day the first room burns.
abstract.cn: 想象每一页的副本都放在另一间屋里，等着第一间屋烧掉的那天。

examples.en: Good database management is mostly boring, which is exactly the point.
examples.cn: 好的数据库管理大部分时候很枯燥，而这正是它的意义。

examples.en: The firm outsourced database management but kept control of the data.
examples.cn: 公司把数据库管理外包，但数据控制权仍握在自己手里。

examples.en: She took a course in database management before joining the audit team.
examples.cn: 她加入审计团队之前修了一门数据库管理课程。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「得他（data）被子（base）满街（manage）门特」——给成堆数据盖上被子、管好门，就是数据库管理

root: 拉丁 datum「被给予之物」→ data；希腊 basis「基座」→ 拉丁 basis → base；意大利 maneggiare「用手操作」→ 法语 manage → 英语 management；二十世纪中叶拼成 database，再加 management 成复合词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses cover the daily work, the software layer, the organisational role, governance, performance, recovery, teaching and the market.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项涵盖日常工作、软件层、组织职能、治理、性能、恢复、教学与市场。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rows of labelled drawers in an archive, with a clerk checking every file in and out against a register.
core.cn: 核心意象：档案室成排贴标签的抽屉，管理员按登记簿核对每份卷宗的进出。

branches.en: DAILY CARE: routine upkeep on one side, tuning for speed and growth on the other.
branches.cn: 日常照管：一边是例行维护，一边是为速度与增长做调优。

branches.en: SYSTEM AND MARKET: the software that performs the work, and the commercial class it is sold in.
branches.cn: 系统与市场：执行工作的软件，以及它所在的商业类别。

branches.en: ROLE AND SUBJECT: a permanent office inside an organisation, and a taught course outside it.
branches.cn: 岗位与课程：组织内的常设职位，以及组织外讲授的课程。

branches.en: GOVERNANCE: permissions, standards and the rules about who may read or change data.
branches.cn: 治理：权限、标准，以及谁可读取或改动数据的规则。

branches.en: RECOVERY: copies kept against failure, the duty that proves the work was worth doing.
branches.cn: 恢复：为故障而保存副本，这项职责证明工作值得做。

intro.en: The compound has no prefix or suffix of its own; it is held together by two Latin-based nouns and one Italian-based one.
intro.cn: 这个复合词本身没有前后缀，而是由两个拉丁来源名词与一个意大利来源名词拼合而成。

latinIntro.en: Latin gives datum and basis; Italian gives maneggiare, which French shaped into manage before English took it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供 datum 与 basis；意大利语提供 maneggiare，法语把它塑造成 manage，英语再借入。

items.example: The noun supplies the first half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供复合词的前半部分。

items.structure: plural of datum used as a mass noun
items.example: English treats the plural as a body of facts.
items.exampleCN: 英语把这个复数当作一批事实来用。

items.example: The second half supplies the idea of a supporting structure.
items.exampleCN: 后半部分提供「支撑结构」的意思。

items.example: The hand is the image inside the Italian verb of handling.
items.exampleCN: 「手」是意大利语「操作」动词里的意象。

items.meaning: to handle, to train a horse
items.example: The verb reached English through French.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词经法语进入英语。

items.example: The verb is the base of the second noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是第二个名词的词基。

items.example: The ending turns manage into a name for the work.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把 manage 变成工作的名称。

items.example: The first two pieces were joined in the twentieth century.
items.exampleCN: 前两个构件在二十世纪被拼在一起。

items.meaning: the care of such a store
items.example: The full compound adds the work to the object.
items.exampleCN: 完整复合词在对象之后加上工作本身。

definition_zh: adj. 自信而坚定表达自我的；（作风）强硬张扬的
definition_en: Confidently stating your needs and opinions without being aggressive; of a manner or style, forceful and insistent.
core_image: 声音不高，但把自己的要求说得清清楚楚
scene: 她学会平静而坚定地说出自己的要求。 She learned to be assertive without raising her voice.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：assertive 指敢于清楚表达自己，同时不侵犯别人。

pos.zh: 自信坚定的；强硬主张的

forms.label: 形容词原级（比较级用 more）

senses.title: Confident without aggression
senses.definition: able to state your needs and opinions clearly while still respecting other people
senses.definitionCN: 能清楚说出自己的需要与看法，同时仍尊重别人
senses.example: Being assertive is not the same as being rude.
senses.exampleCN: 敢于表达并不等于无礼。
senses.why: The root means to join a claim to yourself, so the word describes holding your own position, not pushing others off theirs.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「把主张接到自己身上」，所以这个词说的是守住自己的位置，而不是把别人挤下去。

senses.title: Forceful in manner or style
senses.definition: of a tone, design or performance, insistent and unwilling to be overlooked
senses.definitionCN: 指语气、设计或表现气势逼人，不肯被忽视
senses.example: The wine has an assertive smoky flavour.
senses.exampleCN: 这款酒有一股张扬的烟熏味。
senses.why: Applied to things rather than people, the word loses its praise and simply means demanding attention.
senses.whyCN: 用于事物而非人时，这个词失去褒义，只表示「要求被注意」。

intro.en: Assertive comes from Latin asserere, from ad, to, plus serere, to join: to lay a hand on someone and claim their freedom, hence to claim firmly.
intro.cn: assertive 出自拉丁语 asserere，由 ad「向」加 serere「连接」构成：把手按在某人身上宣布其自由，因而引申为「坚定主张」。

items.en: Latin serere meant to join or bind in a row, and gives series and insert.
items.cn: 拉丁语 serere 意为「连接成排」，产生 series 与 insert。

items.en: With ad, to, asserere meant to join a claim to yourself, used in the formal freeing of a slave.
items.cn: 加上 ad「向」后，asserere 意为「把主张接到自己身上」，用于正式宣布奴隶获释的仪式。

items.en: The noun assertio named a formal claim of freedom, and later any firm statement.
items.cn: 名词 assertio 指正式的自由宣告，后来指任何坚定的陈述。

items.en: English took assert in the sixteenth century with the sense of stating firmly.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 assert，意为坚定地陈述。

items.en: The adjective assertive appears in the nineteenth century, at first often meaning merely dogmatic.
items.cn: 形容词 assertive 出现于十九世纪，起初常只表示「独断」。

items.en: Psychology in the 1970s made assertiveness a skill between passivity and aggression, giving the word its praise.
items.cn: 二十世纪七十年代的心理学把「敢于表达」定为介于被动与攻击之间的技能，赋予这个词褒义。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the claim root and sets the two wrong extremes beside it; the near-meaning group lists neighbouring kinds of confidence.
note.cn: 形近组保留「主张」词根，并把两个错误的极端摆在旁边；近义组列出邻近的几种自信。

entries.definition: To state firmly that something is true.
entries.definitionCN: 坚定地陈述某事为真。

entries.definition: A firm statement of fact or belief.
entries.definitionCN: 对事实或信念的坚定陈述。

entries.definition: Ready to attack or dominate others.
entries.definitionCN: 随时要攻击或压倒他人。

entries.definition: Accepting things without resistance.
entries.definitionCN: 不加抵抗地接受。

entries.definition: Sure of your own ability.
entries.definitionCN: 确信自己的能力。

entries.definition: Strong and effective in manner.
entries.definitionCN: 作风强而有力。

entries.definition: Quietly sure of yourself.
entries.definitionCN: 沉静地相信自己。

entries.definition: Quick and firm in deciding.
entries.definitionCN: 决断迅速而坚定。

normalIntro.en: Assertive is assert plus -ive: inclined to state your own claim, without stepping on anyone else.
normalIntro.cn: assertive 就是 assert 加 -ive：倾向于说出自己的主张，而不踩着别人。

normal.en: Assert is the verb, assertion the noun.
normal.cn: assert 是动词，assertion 是名词。

normal.en: Assertiveness is the skill, assertively the adverb.
normal.cn: assertiveness 是这项能力，assertively 是副词。

normal.en: Compare with more and most, never with -er.
normal.cn: 比较级用 more 与 most，不用 -er。

normal.en: Assertive sits between passive and aggressive.
normal.cn: assertive 位于 passive 与 aggressive 之间。

normal.en: Of flavours or designs it just means insistent.
normal.cn: 用于味道或设计时只表示「张扬」。

abstract.en: Picture a steady voice saying no once.
abstract.cn: 想象一个平稳的声音把「不」说了一次。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand raised calmly in a loud meeting.
abstract.cn: 想象在喧闹会议中平静举起的一只手。

abstract.en: Think of a flavour that refuses to sit back.
abstract.cn: 想象一种不肯退到后面的味道。

examples.en: He grew more assertive after the course.
examples.cn: 上完那门课后他更敢于表达了。

examples.en: She spoke assertively but never rudely.
examples.cn: 她说得坚定，却从不无礼。

examples.en: The design is bold and assertive.
examples.cn: 这个设计大胆而张扬。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：assert「断言」+ -ive「倾向……的」——倾向于把自己的主张说出来，就是 assertive。

root: 拉丁语 serere「连接成排」加 ad-「向」构成 asserere「把手按上并宣告」，名词 assertio 指正式宣告；英语 assert 加 -ive 成 assertive，二十世纪七十年代被心理学赋予褒义。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses hold a position firmly: a person stating a claim without aggression, and a taste or design that refuses to be overlooked.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都是稳稳守住一个位置：一个人不侵犯地提出主张，以及一种不肯被忽视的味道或设计。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a level voice stating its own need clearly
core.cn: 核心意象：声音不高，却把自己的要求说得清清楚楚

branches.en: A steady voice saying no once.
branches.cn: 把「不」说了一次的平稳声音。

branches.en: A hand raised calmly in a loud room.
branches.cn: 喧闹房间里平静举起的手。

branches.en: A smoky flavour that will not sit back.
branches.cn: 不肯退后的烟熏味。

branches.en: A design that demands attention.
branches.cn: 要求被注意的设计。

branches.en: Both refuse to be overlooked.
branches.cn: 两者都拒绝被忽视。

intro.en: Assertive is as- from ad- plus -sert from serere, join, plus -ive; the same root builds assert, insert, series and dissertation.
intro.cn: assertive 由 ad- 变来的 as- 加出自 serere「连接」的 -sert 再加 -ive 构成；同一词根还构成 assert、insert、series 与 dissertation。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is serere, to join, asserere, to claim by laying a hand on, and assertio, a formal claim.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 serere「连接」、asserere「按手宣告」与 assertio「正式宣告」。
