definition_zh: 天然生境；自然栖息地；物种原本栖居的环境
definition_en: the environment in which a species lives without human replacement of its food, shelter or breeding conditions
core_image: 林间一片未被开垦的湿地，芦苇从水里长到岸上，鸟在苇丛深处筑巢，四周没有围栏与水泥
scene: 山谷深处那片湿地没有被排干，也没有围栏，鸟仍在苇丛里筑巢。 The reserve keeps the natural habitat of the heron intact.
sceneCN: 这里指物种在无人改造的条件下原本栖居的环境（第 1 个义项：物种自然存活的环境）；句意为保护区让这种鹭的天然生境保持完整。

pos.zh: 天然生境；自然栖息地
某物种的原生分布环境

derivatives.zh: 该短语的核心词，由拉丁语「它栖居」一词直接借来，义为「生境；栖息地」
由表示「居住」的拉丁词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「居住；住所」
由表示「在内」的前缀加表示「持有、占据」的词干构成，义为「栖居于」
由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「居民；栖居者」
由该动词加表示「可……的」的形容词尾构成，义为「可居住的」
由表示否定的前缀加该形容词构成，义为「不自然的；反常的」

senses.title: The environment a species lives in unaided
senses.titleCN: 物种无需人工维持即可栖居的环境
senses.definition: the surroundings in which a species finds food, shelter and breeding conditions without human replacement of them
senses.definitionCN: 某一物种无需人类代为提供食物、隐蔽与繁殖条件即可获得这些条件的环境
senses.example: The orchid survives only in its natural habitat, where a specific bee pollinates it.
senses.exampleCN: 这种兰花只在其天然生境中存活，那里有特定的蜂为它传粉。
senses.why: Habitat is a Latin form meaning it dwells, so the phrase points to the dwelling a species occupies by itself.
senses.whyCN: 生境一词本义是「它居住」，因此这个短语指向物种自己占用的那个居所。

senses.title: The native range of a species
senses.definition: the geographic area where a species evolved or arrived without human transport
senses.definitionCN: 某一物种在无人为搬运的情况下演化形成或自然到达的地理范围
senses.example: Outside its natural habitat the frog is replaced by a close relative.
senses.exampleCN: 在其原生分布区之外，这种蛙会被近缘种取代。
senses.why: Range and dwelling overlap in the wild: a species occupies the ground it is fitted to.
senses.whyCN: 在野外，分布范围与居所是重叠的：一个物种占据的是它已经适应的那片地面。

senses.title: A habitat type such as forest or marsh
senses.titleCN: 森林、沼泽这类生境类型
senses.definition: a category of environment defined by its vegetation, water and climate rather than by one species
senses.definitionCN: 按植被、水体与气候划分的环境类别，而不是按单一物种划分
senses.example: Reedbed is a natural habitat that filters water as well as sheltering birds.
senses.exampleCN: 芦苇荡是一种天然生境，在庇护鸟类的同时也过滤水质。
senses.why: Classification works upward from physical conditions, so the same phrase names a kind of place as well as a home.
senses.whyCN: 分类是从物理条件往上归并的，因此同一个短语既指一个家，也指一类地方。

senses.title: The set of requirements a species needs
senses.titleCN: 物种生存所需的生境要件
senses.definition: the specific combination of food, cover, water and breeding sites a species requires
senses.definitionCN: 某一物种所需的食物、隐蔽物、水源与繁殖场所的特定组合
senses.example: Draining the spring removed a requirement of its natural habitat.
senses.exampleCN: 排干泉水，就等于抽掉了它天然生境中的一项要件。
senses.why: A habitat can be described as a list of conditions, and the phrase covers that list as well as the place.
senses.whyCN: 生境可以被描述成一份条件清单，这个短语既指地点，也指那份清单。

senses.title: Undisturbed, original condition
senses.definition: the state of an environment before drainage, clearing or other human change
senses.definitionCN: 在排水、开垦或其他人为改变之前的环境状态
senses.example: The marsh was returned to something close to its natural habitat.
senses.exampleCN: 这片沼泽被恢复到接近其原始天然状态。
senses.why: Natural carries the sense of what is born with a thing, so the phrase can mark a baseline rather than a location.
senses.whyCN: 「天生的」这一形容词带有「与生俱来」的意思，因此这个短语可以标出一条基准线，而不只是一个位置。

senses.title: A legally protected natural area
senses.titleCN: 受法律保护的天然生境区域
senses.definition: an area given legal protection because it supports species that depend on it
senses.definitionCN: 因其维系着依赖它的物种而受到法律保护的区域
senses.example: Building within the natural habitat of the turtle now requires a permit.
senses.exampleCN: 在这类龟的天然生境内施工，现在需要许可证。
senses.why: Protection attaches to the place itself, so the phrase shifts from ecology to law.
senses.whyCN: 保护直接附着在地点上，于是这个短语从生态学滑向了法律。

senses.title: The object of loss and degradation
senses.titleCN: 生境丧失与退化的对象
senses.definition: what is measured, mapped or lost when land is converted or polluted
senses.definitionCN: 土地被转用或受污染时被测量、绘图或丧失的对象
senses.example: Road building is the leading cause of natural habitat loss in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 修路是该地区天然生境丧失的首要原因。
senses.why: Anything countable can be lost, and the phrase became the unit in which losses are reported.
senses.whyCN: 凡是可计数的东西都会丧失，这个短语于是成了报告损失时使用的单位。

senses.title: A rebuilt substitute for the original
senses.definition: a constructed or restored area designed to replace habitat that was destroyed
senses.definitionCN: 为替代已被破坏的生境而人工建造或恢复的区域
senses.example: The ponds were dug as a natural habitat for the displaced amphibians.
senses.exampleCN: 这些池塘是为被迁走的两栖动物挖出的替代天然生境。
senses.why: The word keeps its shape even when people do the building, because the aim is to mimic the original conditions.
senses.whyCN: 即使由人来建造，这个词仍保持原样，因为目标是模仿原来的条件。

intro.en: Both halves are Latin borrowings. Natural goes back to the verb to be born, and habitat is a Latin verb form meaning it dwells, taken whole into English as a noun.
intro.cn: 两半都是拉丁语借词：前半「天生的」追溯到「出生」这一动词，后半「生境」本是拉丁语动词形式「它居住」，整体借入英语后作名词用。

items.en: Nasci meant to be born, and its participle produced the adjective for what belongs to birth.
items.cn: 这个词意为出生，其分词形式给出了表示「与生俱来」的形容词。

items.en: Natura named the course of birth and the character a thing is born with, hence nature.
items.cn: 这个词指出生的过程与事物天生的性质，于是有了「自然」之义。

items.en: Habere meant to have or hold, and it underlies the frequentative verb for occupying a place.
items.cn: 这个词意为持有、占据，是表示「反复占据某处」的动词的来源。

items.en: Habitare meant to dwell or inhabit, and English inhabits several words from this stem.
items.cn: 这个词意为居住、栖居，英语从这一词干借入了好几个词。

items.en: The third person singular of the verb, meaning it dwells, was borrowed unchanged as an English noun in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 该动词的第三人称单数形式意为「它居住」，十八世纪被原样借入英语作名词。

items.en: English then added natural in front to separate the original dwelling from a substitute one; the combination is a modern descriptive phrase.
items.cn: 英语随后在前面加上表示「天生」的限定词，用以区分原本的居所与替代的居所，这一组合是近代描述性短语。

note.en: The first group shares habitat or nature; the second group names the places and conditions a species needs.
note.cn: 第一组共用 habitat 或 nature 的成分；第二组是表示物种所需场所与条件的相邻说法。

entries.definition: The core noun: the place and conditions where an organism lives.
entries.definitionCN: 核心名词：生物生活的地点和条件。

entries.definition: The act of dwelling, or a place built for people to live in.
entries.definitionCN: 指居住行为，或供人居住的处所。

entries.definition: To live in a place, used of animals, plants and people.
entries.definitionCN: 指栖居于某处，动物、植物与人皆可用。

entries.definition: One who lives in a place.
entries.definitionCN: 指居住在某地者。

entries.definition: A person who studies living things in the field; it shares nature but not habitat.
entries.definitionCN: 指在野外研究生物的人；共用一个「自然」成分，但不含生境成分。

entries.definition: The area a species occupied before human transport, close to the range sense of the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 指物种在人为搬运之前占据的区域，接近该短语的分布区义。

entries.definition: A community plus its physical surroundings, a larger unit than a habitat.
entries.definitionCN: 指生物群落加上其物理环境，是比生境更大的单位。

entries.definition: The specific place where a species reproduces, one requirement within a habitat.
entries.definitionCN: 指物种繁殖的具体场所，是生境要件之一。

entries.definition: Land untouched by human use, close to the undisturbed sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指未经人类使用的土地，接近「未受扰动」义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Latin verb it dwells and the real compounds built on it.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用拉丁语「它居住」这一动词，以及由它构成的真实复合词。

normal.en: Habitat is a whole Latin verb form, so it says it dwells rather than dwelling.
normal.cn: 「生境」是一个完整的拉丁语动词形式，说的是「它居住」，而不是「居住」这个抽象动作。

normal.en: Inhabit, inhabitant and habitation all sit on the same holding stem.
normal.cn: 「栖居」「栖居者」「住所」都站在同一个表示「占据」的词干上。

normal.en: A zoo cage can satisfy an animal but it is not its natural habitat, because the conditions are supplied.
normal.cn: 动物园的笼子能满足动物，但不是它的天然生境，因为条件是被人供给的。

normal.en: Natural marks what is born with a thing, so the phrase always implies a baseline before human change.
normal.cn: 「天生的」标记与生俱来的东西，因此这个短语总暗示人为改变之前的基准。

normal.en: Restoring habitat means rebuilding the water, cover and breeding sites a species lost.
normal.cn: 恢复生境就是重建物种失去的水、隐蔽物与繁殖场所。

abstract.en: Habitat is a fitted shape: the species is cut to the place, and the place is cut to the species.
abstract.cn: 生境是一个彼此贴合的形状：物种被裁成地方的样子，地方也被裁成物种的样子。

abstract.en: Losing habitat is not moving a house but deleting the address the species was born with.
abstract.cn: 丧失生境不是搬走一座房子，而是删掉物种与生俱来的那个地址。

abstract.en: A substitute habitat can imitate the structure and still miss the history that filled it.
abstract.cn: 替代生境可以模仿结构，却仍可能缺失曾把它填满的那段历史。

examples.en: The bats lost their natural habitat when the cave was opened to visitors.
examples.cn: 洞穴向游客开放后，这些蝙蝠失去了天然生境。

examples.en: Reedbeds are the natural habitat of many declining marsh birds.
examples.cn: 芦苇荡是许多数量下降的沼泽鸟类的天然生境。

examples.en: The plant grows far outside its natural habitat in warmer gardens.
examples.cn: 这种植物在更温暖的花园里长到了其天然生境之外很远的地方。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「奈扯柔 海比泰特」——奈扯是天生，海比泰特是它住的地方，天生就住的地方就是天然生境

root: 拉丁语 natura「自然、天性」← nasci「出生」构成表示「自然的」形容词；拉丁语 habitat「它居住」，为 habitare「栖居」的第三人称单数，habere「持有」的反复形式；该形式十八世纪直接借入英语作名词，与表示「自然的」形容词组合为近代描述性短语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the dwelling a species occupies by itself, through range, type, requirements and baseline condition, to law, loss and reconstruction.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从物种自己占用的居所出发，经分布区、类型、要件与基准状态，直到法律、丧失与重建。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an undrained marsh where reeds, water and nesting birds hold their own arrangement without a fence.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片未排干的沼泽，芦苇、水与筑巢的鸟在没有围栏的情况下自行保持秩序。

branches.en: THE PLACE AND ITS TYPE: the dwelling a species occupies and the category of environment it belongs to.
branches.cn: 地点与类型：物种占用的居所，以及它所属的环境类别。

branches.en: THE MAP: the native range that holds the dwelling at geographic scale.
branches.cn: 地图：在地理尺度上容纳这一居所的原生分布区。

branches.en: THE CHECKLIST: food, cover, water and breeding sites that must all be present.
branches.cn: 清单：食物、隐蔽物、水源与繁殖场所必须齐备。

branches.en: THE BASELINE AND THE COPY: original condition, and the rebuilt substitute that tries to imitate it.
branches.cn: 基准与复制：原始状态，以及试图模仿它的人工替代。

branches.en: THE LEDGER: protected ground on one side, and measured loss on the other.
branches.cn: 账本：一边是受保护的地面，一边是被计量的丧失。

intro.en: One Latin birth stem and one Latin dwelling stem carry the whole phrase, and each still builds new English words.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁语「出生」词干和一个拉丁语「居住」词干撑起整个短语，两者至今仍在造新词。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies recorded forms for both halves: nasci and natura on one side, habere, habitare and habitat on the other.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语为两半都提供了有记录的形式：一边是「出生」与「天性」，另一边是「持有」「栖居」与「它居住」。

items.meaning: belonging to birth or inherent character
items.example: It marks what is not supplied by people.
items.exampleCN: 它标记非由人供给的东西。

items.structure: Latin verb form used as noun
items.meaning: it dwells; the place where something lives
items.example: The form was borrowed whole, not derived in English.
items.exampleCN: 该形式是整体借入，并非英语内部派生。

items.example: It is the base of the dwelling verbs.
items.exampleCN: 它是诸「居住」动词的基座。

items.example: It supplies the noun and the English verb.
items.exampleCN: 它提供了名词与英语动词。

items.example: It marks living inside a place.
items.exampleCN: 它标记「住在里面」。

items.example: It makes the word for a resident.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示居住者的词。

items.example: It makes the noun for the act of dwelling.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示居住行为的名词。

items.example: It is the recorded source of the first half.
items.exampleCN: 它是有记录的、前半部分的来源。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb form, third person singular

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语动词形式整体借入，义为「生境」
由表示「在内」的前缀加表示「持有」的词干构成，义为「栖居于」
由该动词加施动名词词尾构成，义为「栖居者」
由该词干加动作名词词尾构成，义为「居住；住所」

definition_zh: 洪亮的；回响的；引起共鸣的；共振的
definition_en: producing a deep prolonged sound, or responding strongly at a particular frequency; also stirring a shared feeling
core_image: 空厅里一个低音久久不散，墙与地板都跟着轻轻回应
scene: 合唱团离场很久，空荡的大厅里仍留着一阵低沉的回响。 A resonant hum stayed in the empty hall long after the choir left.
sceneCN: 这里 resonant 指「深沉而持久的回响」（第 1 个义项：声音饱满并在空间中延续）；句意：合唱团离开很久之后，一阵洪亮的低鸣仍留在空荡的大厅里。图中可辨识物件：空座椅、穹顶、声波弧、木地板。

pos.zh: 洪亮的；回响的；共振的；引起共鸣的

senses.title: Deep and long-lasting in sound
senses.definition: of a sound: full, low and slow to fade, as if the space keeps returning it
senses.definitionCN: 指声音：饱满、低沉、消退缓慢，仿佛空间在不断把它送回来
senses.example: The resonant bass filled the wooden hall.
senses.exampleCN: 洪亮的低音充满了木制大厅。
senses.why: The Latin word is the present participle of 'to resound', so the adjective describes something that keeps sounding back.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词是「回响」的现在分词，因此形容词描述的是不断把声音送回来的东西。

senses.title: A space that returns sound
senses.titleCN: 会把声音送回来的空间
senses.definition: describing a room, cave or hall whose surfaces reflect sound strongly
senses.definitionCN: 描述墙面强烈反射声音的房间、洞穴或厅堂
senses.example: The resonant cave repeated every footstep twice.
senses.exampleCN: 这座回响的洞穴把每个脚步重复两遍。
senses.why: Hard curved surfaces send sound back instead of absorbing it, and the same adjective covers the place as covers the sound.
senses.whyCN: 坚硬弯曲的表面把声音送回而不吸收，因此同一个形容词既修饰声音也修饰地点。

senses.title: Stirring a shared feeling
senses.definition: of a word, image or event: producing a strong emotional response that many people recognise
senses.definitionCN: 指词语、形象或事件：激起许多人共有的强烈情感回应
senses.example: Her short farewell was more resonant than a long speech.
senses.exampleCN: 她简短的告别比一篇长演讲更能引起共鸣。
senses.why: Emotional response was modelled on physical resonance: one thing sets another vibrating in sympathy.
senses.whyCN: 情感回应是照着物理共振来理解的：一物使另一物应和振动。

senses.title: Responding at a natural frequency
senses.titleCN: 在固有频率上强烈响应
senses.definition: in physics: responding with a large amplitude when driven at the frequency the system prefers
senses.definitionCN: 物理学上：被以系统偏好的频率驱动时以大振幅响应
senses.example: The resonant mode of the crystal amplifies the signal.
senses.exampleCN: 晶体的共振模态放大了这个信号。
senses.why: A system pushed at its own rate stores energy instead of resisting it, so it answers far more strongly than at other rates.
senses.whyCN: 被以自身速率推动的系统会储存能量而非抵抗，因此响应远强于其他速率。

senses.title: A device built to resonate
senses.definition: describing a cavity, circuit or tube designed to hold and amplify one frequency
senses.definitionCN: 描述为容纳并放大某一频率而设计的腔体、电路或管
senses.example: The resonant cavity stores microwaves for a fraction of a second.
senses.exampleCN: 共振腔把微波储存几分之一秒。
senses.why: Once physics understood the effect, engineers built objects whose whole purpose is to be resonant.
senses.whyCN: 物理学理解这一效应之后，工程师就造出以「共振」为全部目的的物件。

senses.title: In tune with an idea or group
senses.titleCN: 与某种观念或群体相呼应
senses.definition: followed by with: closely connected to something and likely to stir agreement
senses.definitionCN: 后接表示「与」的介词：与某物紧密相连，容易激起认同
senses.example: The speech was resonant with the worries of the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇讲话与人群的忧虑相互呼应。
senses.why: The construction 'resonant with' keeps the physical idea of two things sharing a rate, transferred to shared concerns.
senses.whyCN: 「与……相呼应」这一结构保留了「两物共享同一速率」的物理想法，只是转到了共同关切上。

senses.title: A voice with body and depth
senses.definition: describing a voice that seems to come from a large, well-filled space
senses.definitionCN: 描述仿佛出自一个宽阔饱满空间的嗓音
senses.example: The actor's resonant voice carried to the back row.
senses.exampleCN: 演员洪亮的嗓音传到了最后一排。
senses.why: A chest voice excites more of the body's cavities, so acoustics supplies the everyday praise of a good speaking voice.
senses.whyCN: 胸腔发声会激起身体更多空腔，因此声学为日常对好嗓音的称赞提供了说法。

senses.title: An image that will not fade
senses.definition: of a name, image or phrase: continuing to be remembered and repeated long after it appears
senses.definitionCN: 指名称、形象或短语：出现很久之后仍被记住与引用
senses.example: The name remains resonant a century after the strike.
senses.exampleCN: 那场罢工过去一个世纪，这个名字仍能引起回响。
senses.why: What stays in memory behaves like a sound that keeps returning, so the acoustic adjective became a word about lasting meaning.
senses.whyCN: 留在记忆里的东西，行为像不断返回的声音，于是这个声学形容词成了「意义持久」的说法。

intro.en: Resonant is the English form of Latin resonans, the present participle of resonare 'to sound again'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: resonant 是拉丁 resonans 的英语形式，而 resonans 是 resonare「再次发声」的现在分词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sonare meant 'to sound, to make a noise', and its noun sonus meant 'sound'. The deeper origin of the root is not established.
items.cn: sonare 意为「发声、发出响声」，其名词 sonus 意为「声音」。这个词根更早的来源尚无定论。

items.en: Re- 'again, back' plus sonare produced resonare, 'to resound, to send a sound back'.
items.cn: 「再次、返回」加「发声」构成 resonare，意为「回响、把声音送回来」。

items.en: The present participle resonans described anything currently resounding, and English took that form rather than the abstract noun.
items.cn: 现在分词 resonans 描述正在回响之物，英语采用的就是这一形式，而非抽象名词。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the adjective covered both echoing spaces and full sounds, and later spread to figurative meaning.
items.cn: 从十六世纪起，这个形容词既修饰回响的空间，也修饰饱满的声音，后来扩展到比喻意义。

items.en: Physics added the strict sense of a system driven at its natural frequency, and engineering added resonant cavities and circuits.
items.cn: 物理学增添了「系统被固有频率驱动」的严格义，工程学又增添了共振腔与共振电路。

items.en: The first dates for the technical senses are approximate; the Latin participle is fully attested.
items.cn: 各技术义的最早年代为约数；拉丁分词本身有完整书证。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same resounding root plus one look-alike from a sitting root; group two holds adjectives of sound and feeling.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「回响」词根的几种形式，外加一个出自「坐」词根的形近词；第二组是声音与感受方面的近义形容词。

entries.definition: The noun for the effect itself, either the physical response or the emotional echo; the adjective describes what has it.
entries.definitionCN: 指效应本身的名词，既可指物理响应，也可指情感回声；形容词则描述具有这一效应之物。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to resound or to stir a shared feeling; it names the action that the adjective qualifies.
entries.definitionCN: 意为回响或激起共同感受的动词；它指形容词所修饰的那个动作。

entries.definition: From Latin residere 'to remain sitting', built on sedere 'to sit': a person who lives somewhere, with nothing acoustic about it.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁语「留在坐着」，构于「坐」：指住在某处的人，与声音毫无关系。

entries.definition: An object or cavity designed to resonate, from the same root plus an agent suffix; it is the instrument, not the quality.
entries.definitionCN: 为共振而设计的物体或腔体，由同一词根加施动后缀构成；它指器具，而非性质。

entries.definition: From Latin sonorus 'full of sound': deep and rich in tone, but without the idea of being driven at a natural frequency.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁语「充满声音」：音色深沉丰厚，但不含被固有频率驱动的意思。

entries.definition: Simply returning a sound from a surface; it lacks the sustained reinforcement that resonant implies.
entries.definitionCN: 只表示声音从表面返回来；缺少这个词所含的持续增强。

entries.definition: Bringing images or feelings to mind; it overlaps with the figurative sense of resonant but not with the acoustic one.
entries.definitionCN: 使形象或感受浮现；它与这个词的比喻义重叠，但不涉及声学义。

entries.definition: Originally 'vibrating', now 'full of life or bright'; it suggests energy rather than a returning sound.
entries.definitionCN: 原义「振动的」，今多指「有活力的、鲜艳的」；它暗示能量，而非返回的声音。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin re- 'again' plus sonare 'to sound': sounding again.
normal.cn: 拉丁「再次」加「发声」：再次发声。

normal.en: The family runs resonant, resonance, resonate, resonator, resonantly.
normal.cn: 同族词包括洪亮的、共振、共鸣、共鸣器、以回响的方式。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: resonant voice, resonant frequency, resonant cavity.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：洪亮的嗓音、共振频率、共振腔。

normal.en: The phrase resonant with links the physical idea to shared feelings.
normal.cn: 「与……相呼应」这一搭配把物理概念接到共同感受上。

normal.en: Beware resident: it comes from sitting, not sounding.
normal.cn: 当心那个表示「居民」的形近词：它出自「坐」而非「发声」。

abstract.en: Picture a hall that keeps answering after the singer has gone.
abstract.cn: 想象歌者离开后仍在应答的厅堂。

abstract.en: Picture a word that keeps ringing in the mind years later.
abstract.cn: 想象一个多年后仍在脑中作响的词。

abstract.en: Picture a glass that grows louder the more exactly it is matched.
abstract.cn: 想象玻璃杯被匹配得越准，响声就越大。

examples.en: His resonant voice needed no microphone.
examples.cn: 他洪亮的嗓音不需要扩音器。

examples.en: The chamber is resonant at one microwave frequency.
examples.cn: 这个腔体在一个微波频率上发生共振。

examples.en: The date is resonant for everyone in the room.
examples.cn: 这个日期让屋里每个人都心有回响。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「reson（回响）+ ant（形容词尾）」——会一直回响的，就是洪亮共鸣的

root: 拉丁 resonans（resonare「再次发声」的现在分词）= re-「再次」+ sonare「发声」。英语 resonant。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe answering: a full sound, an echoing room, a stirred feeling, a driven system, a built cavity, an agreeing idea, a deep voice and an image that keeps returning.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述「应答」：饱满的声音、回响的房间、被激起的感受、受驱的系统、造出的腔体、相合的观念、深沉的嗓音，以及不断返回的形象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a low note still hanging in an empty hall, answered faintly by walls and floor.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个低音仍悬在空厅里，墙壁与地板轻轻应和。

branches.en: THE VOICE: a full tone and a deep speaking voice are the same bodily resonance heard in two settings.
branches.cn: 嗓音：饱满的音与深沉的说话声，是同一身体共振在两种场合被听到。

branches.en: THE ROOM: hard surfaces return sound, so the place itself can be called resonant.
branches.cn: 房间：坚硬表面把声音送回，因此地点本身也能被称为回响的。

branches.en: THE SHARED FEELING: a word or speech answers a group's concerns, the emotional form of matching a frequency.
branches.cn: 共同感受：词语或讲话应和群体的关切，这是「频率相合」的情感形式。

branches.en: THE ENGINEERED RESPONSE: physics names the effect, and engineering builds cavities that exploit it.
branches.cn: 工程响应：物理学为效应命名，工程学则造出利用它的腔体。

branches.en: THE AFTERLIFE: what keeps being remembered behaves like a sound that will not stop returning.
branches.cn: 余响：被不断记住之物，行为像不肯停止返回的声音。

intro.en: Resonant is a Latin participle turned English adjective, with a prefix, a sounding verb and a participle ending.
intro.cn: resonant 是由拉丁分词转成的英语形容词，含一个前缀、一个发声动词与一个分词结尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin resonare and sonare also yield resonance, resonate, sonorous and consonance in English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 resonare 与 sonare 在英语里还衍生出 resonance、resonate、sonorous 与 consonance。

items.example: The prefix marks a return of the sound.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出声音的返回。

items.example: The verb is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整个词族的基础。

items.example: The ending makes an adjective of ongoing action.
items.exampleCN: 这个结尾造出表示持续动作的形容词。

items.example: The valley resounded after the bell.
items.exampleCN: 钟声之后山谷回响。

items.example: The resounding choir filled the nave.
items.exampleCN: 回响的合唱充满中殿。

items.example: A resonant note hung in the air.
items.exampleCN: 一个洪亮的音悬在空气里。

items.example: The cavity has a sharp resonance.
items.exampleCN: 这个腔体有一个尖锐的共振点。

items.meaning: to echo or stir a feeling
items.example: The image resonated with voters.
items.exampleCN: 这个形象在选民中引起共鸣。

latinEntries.structure: sonare, sono, sonavi, sonatum (v., first conjugation)

definition_zh: 大陆漂移；大陆块在地球表面相对移动的假说
definition_en: the idea that the continents have moved slowly across the Earth's surface over geological time
core_image: 几块大陆像浮冰一样在地球表面缓慢漂开，彼此之间的海岸线曾经拼得严丝合缝
scene: 相隔大洋的两岸竟然发现了同一种古老蕨类的化石。 Fossils of the same fern occur on landmasses now separated by an ocean, evidence for continental drift.
sceneCN: 这里 continental drift 指「大陆漂移」（第 1 个义项：大陆块在地表相对移动的假说）；句意为同一种古老蕨类的化石出现在如今被大洋隔开的陆块上，这成为大陆漂移的证据。

pos.zh: 大陆漂移（说）；大陆块的水平移动

senses.title: The hypothesis of moving continents
senses.titleCN: 大陆漂移说：大陆会移动的假说
senses.definition: the hypothesis that continents have moved slowly across the globe over geological time
senses.definitionCN: 认为大陆在地质时间里缓慢移动的假说
senses.example: Fossils of the same fern occur on landmasses now separated by an ocean, evidence for continental drift.
senses.exampleCN: 同一种古老蕨类的化石出现在如今被大洋隔开的陆块上，这成为大陆漂移的证据。
senses.why: The phrase names the motion directly: continental tells us what moves, drift tells us how slowly and freely.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语直接命名运动：continental 说明移动的是什么，drift 说明移动得缓慢而自由。

senses.title: The motion itself
senses.definition: the actual relative motion of continents over the Earth's surface
senses.definitionCN: 大陆在地球表面实际的相对运动
senses.example: Continental drift continues today at a few centimetres a year.
senses.exampleCN: 大陆漂移今天仍在继续，每年几厘米。
senses.why: Like most theory names, the phrase can denote the process as well as the idea about it.
senses.whyCN: 像多数理论名称一样，这个短语既可指过程，也可指关于过程的想法。

senses.title: Wegener's proposal
senses.definition: the specific early-twentieth-century proposal of Alfred Wegener
senses.definitionCN: 阿尔弗雷德·魏格纳在二十世纪初提出的具体假说
senses.example: Wegener's continental drift was rejected at first for lacking a mechanism.
senses.exampleCN: 魏格纳的大陆漂移说最初因缺少机制而被否定。
senses.why: The phrase is historically tied to one proposal, so it can name that proposal rather than the general process.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语在历史上与一个具体提案绑定，因此可指那个提案而非一般过程。

senses.title: The evidence from matching coasts
senses.definition: the evidence that coastlines and rock sequences on opposite sides of an ocean match
senses.definitionCN: 大洋两岸的海岸线与岩层序列能够对上的证据
senses.example: The matching coastlines of South America and Africa were early support for continental drift.
senses.exampleCN: 南美与非洲海岸线的吻合是大陆漂移说的早期支持。
senses.why: If two shores fit like puzzle pieces, the simplest reading is that they were once one piece.
senses.whyCN: 如果两岸像拼图一样吻合，最简单的解释就是它们曾经是一块。

senses.title: The fossil evidence
senses.definition: the evidence that identical fossils occur on continents now far apart
senses.definitionCN: 相同化石出现在如今天各一方的不同大陆上的证据
senses.example: Glossopteris fossils were a key clue for continental drift.
senses.exampleCN: 舌羊齿化石是大陆漂移说的关键线索。
senses.why: A plant that cannot cross an ocean should not appear on both sides unless the land was once joined.
senses.whyCN: 一种无法跨洋传播的植物不该出现在两岸，除非那片陆地曾经相连。

senses.title: The missing mechanism
senses.definition: the weakness of the early theory, which could not explain what moved the continents
senses.definitionCN: 早期理论的弱点：无法解释是什么推动了大陆
senses.example: Continental drift stalled until seafloor spreading supplied a mechanism.
senses.exampleCN: 大陆漂移说停滞不前，直到海底扩张提供了机制。
senses.why: A theory that describes motion without a driver is incomplete, which is why the phrase is often paired with 'hypothesis'.
senses.whyCN: 只描述运动而不给出驱动力的理论是不完整的，因此这个短语常与「假说」搭配。

senses.title: The ancestor of plate tectonics
senses.definition: the earlier framework that plate tectonics later absorbed and explained
senses.definitionCN: 后来被板块构造吸收并解释的早期框架
senses.example: Plate tectonics grew out of continental drift and seafloor spreading.
senses.exampleCN: 板块构造由大陆漂移与海底扩张发展而来。
senses.why: The old idea supplied the observation; the new theory supplied the machinery, so the two are ancestor and descendant.
senses.whyCN: 旧想法提供了观察，新理论提供了机制，因此两者是前身与后继的关系。

senses.title: A metaphor for slow separation
senses.titleCN: 比喻：缓慢而巨大的分离
senses.definition: used figuratively for things that separate slowly and irreversibly
senses.definitionCN: 比喻缓慢而不可逆地分开的事物
senses.example: The two departments underwent a kind of continental drift.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个部门经历了一种缓慢的分离。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows the pace of the process: almost invisible day by day, enormous over time.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻借用了过程的节奏：逐日几乎看不见，长期却极其巨大。

intro.en: Continental drift is a modern scientific phrase. Its two words are ordinary English, but the idea was assembled from geology, fossils and coastlines in the early twentieth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: continental drift 是现代科学短语。两个词都是普通英语词，但其观念是二十世纪初从地质、化石与海岸线证据中组装起来的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Continental comes from Latin continere 'to hold together'; drift comes from Old English drifan 'to drive, be driven', which later gave the sense of being carried by currents.
items.cn: continental 来自拉丁语 continere「连在一起」；drift 来自古英语 drifan「驱动、被推动」，后来产生「被水流带走」的意思。

items.en: Drift first meant driving or being driven; the modern sense of slow, passive movement developed in the context of ships, snow and currents.
items.cn: drift 最初指驱动或被驱动；现代「缓慢被动移动」义是在船只、雪与洋流的语境中发展出来的。

items.en: Alfred Wegener proposed that the continents had once been joined and later moved apart, supported by matching coasts, fossils and rock belts.
items.cn: 阿尔弗雷德·魏格纳提出大陆曾经相连、后来分开，并用海岸吻合、化石与岩带作为证据。

items.en: The idea was widely resisted because no known force could move continents through the ocean floor.
items.cn: 这个想法长期遭到抵制，因为当时不知道有什么力量能让大陆穿过洋底移动。

items.en: Seafloor spreading and plate tectonics supplied the mechanism, and continental drift was absorbed as part of the larger theory.
items.cn: 海底扩张与板块构造提供了机制，大陆漂移被吸收为更大理论的一部分。

items.en: The phrase survives as the historical name of the early hypothesis and as a general label for the relative motion of continents.
items.cn: 这个短语作为早期假说的历史名称保留下来，也用作大陆相对运动的通称。

note.en: Group one separates the phrase from look-alike and sound-alike words; group two separates it from the theories and processes it is often mixed with.
note.cn: 第一组把这个短语与形近、音近词分开；第二组把它与常被混淆的理论和过程分开。

entries.definition: a first version of a text, or a plan; it is spelled with -a and has nothing to do with moving land.
entries.definitionCN: 文本的初稿或计划；拼写用 -a，与陆地移动无关。

entries.definition: the noun or verb meaning slow passive movement; continental drift adds the object that moves.
entries.definitionCN: 表示缓慢被动移动的名词或动词；continental drift 加上了移动的对象。

entries.definition: floating without control; the prefix a- adds the sense of being loose.
entries.definitionCN: 失去控制地漂浮；前缀 a- 增添了「松脱」的意思。

entries.definition: the adjective meaning 'relating to a continent'; alone it does not imply any theory.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「与大陆有关的」形容词；单独使用时不含任何理论含义。

entries.definition: the fuller theory of moving lithospheric plates that explained and replaced continental drift.
entries.definitionCN: 解释并取代大陆漂移说的、关于岩石圈板块运动的更完整理论。

entries.definition: the creation of new ocean floor at ridges; it provided the mechanism continental drift lacked.
entries.definitionCN: 在大洋中脊生成新洋底；它为大陆漂移说提供了所缺的机制。

entries.definition: the apparent movement of the poles relative to a continent; it is not the same as continents moving apart.
entries.definitionCN: 极相对于大陆的视移动；这与大陆彼此分开不同。

entries.definition: movement from one place to another, usually by people or animals; it lacks the geological scale.
entries.definitionCN: 人或动物从一个地方到另一个地方的移动；它没有地质尺度的含义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real evidence types and real historical sequence, so the phrase is remembered as a story rather than a slogan.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的证据类型与真实的历史顺序，因此这个短语作为一段故事被记住，而不是口号。

normal.en: The phrase says exactly what it means: continents drift, slowly and passively, like rafts on a current.
normal.cn: 这个短语说的就是字面意思：大陆漂移，缓慢而被动，像水流上的筏子。

normal.en: The three classic clues are matching coastlines, matching fossils and matching rock belts.
normal.cn: 三条经典证据是海岸线吻合、化石吻合与岩带吻合。

normal.en: Wegener proposed the drift; seafloor spreading explained it; plate tectonics replaced it with a fuller framework.
normal.cn: 魏格纳提出漂移，海底扩张解释漂移，板块构造以更完整的框架取代它。

normal.en: The old theory's weakness was the missing mechanism, not the evidence.
normal.cn: 旧理论的弱点是缺少机制，而不是缺少证据。

normal.en: Continents move about as fast as a fingernail grows, which is why the drift is invisible in a lifetime.
normal.cn: 大陆移动的速度大约和指甲生长一样快，所以在一生之中看不见这种漂移。

abstract.en: Abstractly, continental drift is separation without a visible cause: pieces move apart so slowly that each day looks unchanged.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，大陆漂移是没有可见原因的分离：碎块移动得如此缓慢，以至于每一天看起来都没变。

abstract.en: Its lesson is that a correct observation can wait decades for the right mechanism.
abstract.cn: 它给出的启示是：一个正确的观察可能等待数十年才等到合适的机制。

abstract.en: Symbol: two puzzle pieces that once fitted, now separated by a widening gap with small arrows.
abstract.cn: 符号：两块曾经吻合的拼图，如今被一条不断变宽的缝隙分开，缝中有小箭头。

examples.en: Continental drift explained why similar fossils appear on distant continents.
examples.cn: 大陆漂移说解释了为什么相似化石出现在相距遥远的大陆上。

examples.en: The idea of continental drift was debated for decades before plate tectonics.
examples.cn: 在板块构造出现之前，大陆漂移的想法被争论了几十年。

examples.en: Modern measurements confirm continental drift at a few centimetres per year.
examples.cn: 现代测量证实大陆漂移的速度是每年几厘米。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「大陆 + 漂移」—— 大陆像木筏一样在软层上慢慢漂开 → continental drift 大陆漂移

root: continental 源自拉丁语 continere（连在一起）；drift 源自古英语 drifan（驱动、被推动），本义指被水流或风力带走。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of continental drift. The thread runs from the hypothesis, to its evidence, to its missing mechanism, and finally to its place in plate tectonics.
sensesIntro.cn: continental drift 的八个义项。主线从假说，到证据，到缺失的机制，最后到它在板块构造中的位置。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: continents separating slowly like rafts on a current.
core.cn: 核心意象：大陆像水流上的筏子一样缓慢分开。

branches.en: IDEA AND MOTION: the phrase names both the hypothesis and the process.
branches.cn: 想法与运动：这个短语既指假说，也指过程。

branches.en: ONE PROPOSAL: it is historically tied to Wegener's specific claim.
branches.cn: 一个提案：它在历史上与魏格纳的具体主张绑定。

branches.en: EVIDENCE: fitting coasts and shared fossils point to a former join.
branches.cn: 证据：海岸吻合与共享化石指向曾经的连接。

branches.en: THE GAP: a description of motion without a driver is incomplete.
branches.cn: 缺口：只描述运动而不给出驱动力的说法是不完整的。

branches.en: AFTERLIFE: absorbed by plate tectonics, and borrowed as a metaphor for slow separation.
branches.cn: 后续：被板块构造吸收，也被借作缓慢分离的比喻。

intro.en: The phrase is a noun compound of two independent words, so its 'affixes' are the pieces of each word and the related family they build.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个独立词构成名词复合体，因此它的构词分析就是两个词的构件及各自词族。

latinIntro.en: Continental is Latin-derived (continere), while drift is native English (Old English drifan). The two halves come from different language layers, and there is no single Latin family for drift, so latinEntries lists only the Latin side.
latinIntro.cn: continental 源自拉丁语（continere），drift 则是英语本族词（古英语 drifan）。两半来自不同语言层，drift 没有对应的拉丁词族，因此 latinEntries 只列拉丁语一侧。

items.example: Continental blocks moved apart over time.
items.exampleCN: 大陆块随时间分开。

items.structure: Old English drifan 'to drive', noun use of the verb
items.example: The raft drifted with the current.
items.exampleCN: 木筏随水流漂走。

items.meaning: to be carried along by a current or force
items.example: The continents drift a few centimetres a year.
items.exampleCN: 大陆每年漂移几厘米。

items.meaning: a person or thing that drifts
items.meaningCN: 漂流的人或物（-er 表示动作执行者）
items.example: The drifter had no fixed route.
items.exampleCN: 这个漂泊者没有固定路线。

items.example: Driftwood collected along the tide line.
items.exampleCN: 浮木沿着潮线堆积。

items.example: The slow drifting of continents is measured by satellites.
items.exampleCN: 大陆的缓慢漂移由卫星测量。

items.example: Continental fragments can be recognised by their fossils.
items.exampleCN: 大陆碎块可以通过化石识别。

items.example: The two landmasses drifted apart.
items.exampleCN: 两块陆地漂移分开。

definition_zh: 水资源短缺；缺水；可用水量不足以满足需求的状况
definition_en: the condition in which the water available in a place falls short of what households, farms, industry and ecosystems require
core_image: 干涸的井口边排着一列水桶，桶底只刮到一层湿泥
scene: 旱季的村子里，人们在见底的井边排队等水，桶里只舀起一层泥浆。 Water scarcity turned a routine chore into a daily negotiation.
sceneCN: 这里 water scarcity 指「可用水量低于需求的缺水状况」（第 1 个义项：天然来水与取用量之间的实物缺口）；句意为缺水把日常家务变成每天的讨价还价。图中可辨识物件：干井、水桶、排队的人、泥浆。

pos.zh: 水资源短缺；缺水（不可数名词短语，也作 water scarcities 表示多地的缺水情形）

senses.title: Physical shortfall of water against demand
senses.titleCN: 来水不足以满足需求的实物缺口
senses.definition: the condition in which a region's natural supply cannot meet the water its users need
senses.definitionCN: 一个地区的天然供水无法满足其使用者所需水量的状况
senses.example: Water scarcity turned a routine chore into a daily negotiation.
senses.exampleCN: 缺水把日常家务变成每天的讨价还价。
senses.why: Scarcity names a gap, not a total: the word only appears when demand presses against a supply that cannot grow.
senses.whyCN: scarcity 命名的是一个缺口而非总量：只有当需求逼住无法增长的供给时，这个词才出现。

senses.title: Economic scarcity from missing infrastructure
senses.titleCN: 因缺少水利设施造成的经济性缺水
senses.definition: shortage caused not by absent water but by the lack of wells, pipes, pumps and money to deliver it
senses.definitionCN: 并非没有水，而是缺少井、管道、水泵与资金把水送到的短缺
senses.example: The district suffers economic water scarcity despite a full river.
senses.exampleCN: 这个区虽有满河的流水，却仍在经济性缺水之中。
senses.why: Development economists split the idea in two, because a place can be dry by poverty rather than by climate.
senses.whyCN: 发展经济学家把这个概念一分为二，因为一个地方可能因贫困而非因气候而干涸。

senses.title: A measured index per person
senses.titleCN: 按人均水量计算的量化指标
senses.definition: the condition classified by renewable water available per person per year against agreed thresholds
senses.definitionCN: 以每年人均可再生水量对照公认阈值所作的缺水分类
senses.example: The country crossed into absolute water scarcity last decade.
senses.exampleCN: 该国在上一个十年进入了绝对缺水区间。
senses.why: Policy needs a line to cross, so the shortage becomes a number that can be compared between countries.
senses.whyCN: 政策需要一条可越过的界线，于是短缺变成可在国家间比较的数字。

senses.title: Seasonal or intermittent shortage
senses.definition: a shortage that arrives with the dry season, the failure of monsoon rain or a shift in snowmelt
senses.definitionCN: 随旱季、季风降雨失败或融雪改变而来的短缺
senses.example: Seasonal water scarcity empties the upland villages each March.
senses.exampleCN: 季节性缺水每年三月让高地上的村子空掉。
senses.why: A supply can be adequate over a year and still fail in the weeks when nothing falls.
senses.whyCN: 按年计算足够的水，仍可能在滴雨不下的那几周里断掉。

senses.title: Farm-level shortage that threatens food
senses.titleCN: 威胁粮食生产的农田缺水
senses.definition: the shortage that forces irrigation to be cut, yields to fall and cropping patterns to change
senses.definitionCN: 迫使灌溉削减、产量下降、种植结构改变的缺水
senses.example: Water scarcity forced the valley to abandon its thirsty crop.
senses.exampleCN: 缺水迫使这个河谷放弃了耗水的作物。
senses.why: Because irrigation takes the largest share, scarcity is usually felt first in the field and then at the table.
senses.whyCN: 由于灌溉占最大份额，缺水通常先在田里被感到，然后才到餐桌上。

senses.title: Urban competition and rationing
senses.titleCN: 城市里各用户争水与配给
senses.definition: the shortage that sets households, industry and farms against one another and brings cuts and rationing
senses.definitionCN: 使家庭、工业与农业彼此争水，并带来限水与配给的短缺
senses.example: Water scarcity split the city into supply zones with different hours.
senses.exampleCN: 缺水把这座城市划成供水时段不同的若干区。
senses.why: When a fixed volume meets many claimants, shortage becomes an allocation problem rather than a physical one.
senses.whyCN: 当固定水量面对众多索取者，短缺就成了分配问题而非物理问题。

senses.title: Institutional scarcity: weak governance
senses.titleCN: 制度层面的缺水：管理能力不足
senses.definition: the shortage produced by missing data, unclear rights and agencies unable to enforce allocation
senses.definitionCN: 由数据缺失、权利不清与机构无力执行分配所造成的短缺
senses.example: Water scarcity persisted although the reservoir held enough.
senses.exampleCN: 水库的水还够，缺水却依旧持续。
senses.why: The scarcity literature added a third kind beyond physical and economic: the shortage made by institutions themselves.
senses.whyCN: 缺水研究在物理性与经济性之外加了第三种：由制度本身造成的短缺。

senses.title: Perceived shortage that changes behaviour
senses.titleCN: 感知上的短缺及其行为效应
senses.definition: a felt or anticipated shortage that makes people hoard, pay more or change what they grow
senses.definitionCN: 感到或预期到的短缺，使人囤积、多付钱或改变种植选择
senses.example: Water scarcity in the forecast drove up the price of pumps.
senses.exampleCN: 预报中的缺水推高了水泵价格。
senses.why: Scarcity can act before it arrives, because people respond to the expectation of a shortfall as strongly as to the shortfall itself.
senses.whyCN: 短缺可以在到来之前就起作用，因为人对缺口的预期，反应和对缺口本身一样强烈。

intro.en: Water scarcity joins the native word for water to a noun of shortage whose own derivation is disputed. The phrase itself is modern policy language. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: water scarcity 把本族的「水」词连到一个来源尚有争议的「短缺」名词上。这个短语本身是近代的政策语言。年代均为约数。

items.en: Wæter is the earliest English word for water. Its deeper origin is not established; the Indo-European form often proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: wæter 是英语最早的「水」词。其更深来源未得到证明；常为它提出的印欧形式属重构。

items.en: One account takes scarcity from Latin parcus 'sparing, frugal' through scarcitas. The deeper origin of parcus is uncertain, and the link sometimes suggested to parcere 'to spare' is a hypothesis.
items.cn: 一种说法认为 scarcity 经拉丁 scarcitas 出自 parcus「节省的、俭省的」。parcus 的更深来源不确定，有人把它与 parcere「节省」联系，那只是假说。

items.en: Another account connects the family to Vulgar Latin excarpsus 'plucked out', from ex- 'out' and carpere 'to pluck', the same source proposed for the adjective scarce. The two accounts are not reconciled.
items.cn: 另一种说法把这个词族连到俗拉丁 excarpsus「被摘出的」，出自 ex-「向外」与 carpere「摘取」，也就是形容词 scarce 被提出来的同一来源。两种说法尚未统一。

items.en: Old French scarcete meant 'smallness, scantiness, sparingness' and entered English in the fourteenth century as scarcity.
items.cn: 古法语 scarcete 意为「少、不足、俭省」，十四世纪以 scarcity 进入英语。

items.en: Water and scarcity were combined in development and hydrology writing once per-capita supply became a measured policy indicator.
items.cn: 当人均供水量成为可测的政策指标后，water 与 scarcity 在发展研究与水文学写作中连用。

items.en: Source uncertain (word root and first date): the derivation of scarcity is disputed between parcus and excarpsus, and no single earliest citation is fixed for the compound, so its first date is approximate; any older Indo-European forms offered for wæter are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根与首见年代）：scarcity 的词源在 parcus 与 excarpsus 两种说法之间有争议，该复合词也没有公认的最早书证，首见年代只能约计；凡为 wæter 给出的更早印欧形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds water phrases that look alike but name a dry spell, a stress measure or a calculated deficit; group two holds broader security and crisis terms that are often used in place of this phrase.
note.cn: 第一组是同含 water、外形相近，但分别指干旱时段、压力指标或计算出的缺口的短语；第二组是常被用来替换本短语的、更宽泛的安全与危机术语。

entries.definition: The plain phrase for not having enough water at a given moment; it is a temporary or local supply failure, while scarcity is a structural condition.
entries.definitionCN: 指某一时刻水不够用的日常说法；它是临时或局部的供应失败，而 scarcity 是结构性状况。

entries.definition: The share of renewable supply already withdrawn by users; it is an index, not the lived shortage itself.
entries.definitionCN: 可再生供水已被用户取走的比例；它是指标，而非实际感受到的短缺。

entries.definition: The gap between water needed and water supplied over a period, usually in millimetres or cubic metres.
entries.definitionCN: 一段时间内需水与供水之间的缺口，通常以毫米或立方米计。

entries.definition: A prolonged period of unusually low rainfall; it is a climatic event that can produce water scarcity.
entries.definitionCN: 降雨异常偏少的持续时期；它是可能造成缺水的气候事件。

entries.definition: A scarcity severe enough to disrupt health, food or order; it adds an emergency to the shortage.
entries.definitionCN: 严重到破坏健康、粮食或秩序的短缺；它在短缺之上加了紧急状态。

entries.definition: The condition of having acceptable water for health and livelihoods; it is the goal whose failure is called scarcity.
entries.definitionCN: 为健康与生计提供可接受水量的状态；它是目标，其失败即被称为缺水。

entries.definition: A permanent climatic dryness; a desert is arid whether or not anyone demands water.
entries.definitionCN: 长期的气候干旱；无论有没有人取水，沙漠都是干旱的。

entries.definition: Any gap between what is supplied and what is required; water scarcity is this gap applied to water.
entries.definitionCN: 任何供给与需求之间的缺口；水资源短缺就是这个缺口用在水的身上。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Scarcity is the noun of scarce, and scarce describes what cannot be had in enough quantity.
normal.cn: scarcity 是 scarce 的名词，scarce 形容数量不够取用。

normal.en: The development split is fixed in two collocations: physical water scarcity and economic water scarcity.
normal.cn: 发展领域的划分固定在两对搭配里：物理性缺水与经济性缺水。

normal.en: The family runs scarcity, scarce, scarcely, scarceness and water-scarce.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 scarcity、scarce、scarcely、scarceness 与 water-scarce。

normal.en: The phrase sits beside shortage, stress and deficit: shortage is temporary, stress is a ratio, deficit is a calculated gap.
normal.cn: 这个短语与 shortage、stress、deficit 相邻：shortage 是临时的，stress 是比率，deficit 是算出来的缺口。

normal.en: Policy writes it as an index: absolute water scarcity, per-capita thresholds, water-scarcity risk.
normal.cn: 政策把它写成指标：绝对缺水、人均阈值、缺水风险。

abstract.en: Picture a queue at a well where the rope comes up with mud instead of water.
abstract.cn: 想象井边排队的人，井绳拉上来的是泥而不是水。

abstract.en: Picture a full river that cannot reach the houses because no pipe was ever laid.
abstract.cn: 想象一条满水的河，因为从未铺设管道而到不了人家。

abstract.en: Picture a rumour of shortage emptying the shelves before the shortage arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象短缺的传言在短缺到来之前就把货架清空。

examples.en: Water scarcity is measured per person, not per river.
examples.cn: 水资源短缺按人均衡量，而不是按河流衡量。

examples.en: Economic water scarcity can be relieved by building wells and pipes.
examples.cn: 经济性缺水可以通过打井和铺设管道来缓解。

examples.en: The report warned that water scarcity would reshape the region's farming.
examples.cn: 报告警告说，缺水将重塑该地区的农业。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「water（水）+ scarcity（稀缺）」——水不够用 → 水资源短缺

root: 英语复合短语：water 来自古英语 wæter「水」，更深来源不确定；scarcity 经古法语 scarcete 出自拉丁 scarcitas，词根一说为 parcus「俭省的」，一说与俗拉丁 excarpsus「摘出的」相关，两说并列未定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gap: rain or supply falls short, demand presses in, the shortage is classified by cause, measured by index, felt by season, by field, by city, by institution and finally by expectation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个缺口展开：来水不足、需求逼近，短缺再按成因分类、按指标计量，并被季节、农田、城市、制度，最后是预期所感受。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of buckets at a dry well, each scraping up mud.
core.cn: 核心意象：干井边排成一列的水桶，每只都只刮到泥。

branches.en: TWO CAUSES: water may be absent or simply undelivered, so the same gap has a physical and an economic face.
branches.cn: 两种成因：水可能真的没有，也可能只是没送到，同一个缺口有物理面与经济面。

branches.en: MEASURED AND SEASONAL: a threshold number and a dry season describe the same shortage at different scales.
branches.cn: 计量与季节：阈值数字与旱季描述的是同一短缺在不同尺度上的样子。

branches.en: FELT BY USERS: the field loses its crop and the city loses its hours of supply.
branches.cn: 使用者感受：农田失去作物，城市失去供水时段。

branches.en: MADE BY INSTITUTIONS: missing data and weak enforcement can hold a shortage in place.
branches.cn: 制度造成：数据缺失与执行不力可以让短缺一直维持。

branches.en: EXPECTED: a forecast shortfall moves prices and behaviour before any tap runs dry.
branches.cn: 预期：预报中的缺口在任何水龙头干之前就推动了价格与行为。

intro.en: The phrase joins a native English noun to a noun of shortage whose suffix and root are both debated, so the morpheme reading must be given with that caveat.
intro.cn: 这个短语把英语本族名词连到一个词根与后缀均有争议的「短缺」名词上，因此语素读法须带上这一保留。

latinIntro.en: Latin parcus 'sparing' would give scarcity through scarcitas; the rival account uses ex- 'out' plus carpere 'to pluck'; scarce, scarcity and scarceness all belong to this debated family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 parcus「俭省的」经由 scarcitas 可得 scarcity；对立说法用 ex-「向外」加 carpere「摘取」；scarce、scarcity 与 scarceness 都属这个有争议的词族。

items.example: The water in the well fell below the bucket.
items.exampleCN: 井里的水落到桶够不着的地方。

items.example: A parcus household wastes little.
items.exampleCN: 俭省的人家很少浪费。

items.example: The rival account has the word plucked away.
items.exampleCN: 对立说法把词义解释为「被摘走」。

items.example: The suffix turns an adjective into a state.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成状态名词。

items.structure: Latin scarcitas via Old French scarcete
items.example: Scarcity raised the price of fodder.
items.exampleCN: 短缺抬高了草料价格。

items.structure: Old French scars, of disputed origin
items.example: Fresh water was scarce that summer.
items.exampleCN: 那年夏天淡水稀少。

items.example: They could scarcely fill one bucket.
items.exampleCN: 他们勉强装满一桶。

items.example: The scarceness of rain shaped the harvest.
items.exampleCN: 雨水的稀少决定了收成。

items.example: Water-scarce regions import grain instead of water.
items.exampleCN: 缺水地区进口粮食而不是水。

latinEntries.structure: parcus, parca, parcum (adjective, first and second declension)

definition_zh: 流域；河流盆地；以分水岭为界的汇水区域
definition_en: the whole area drained by a river and its tributaries, bounded by divides
core_image: 两条支流在谷口汇成一条大河，远处分水岭像碗沿一样把水收拢
scene: 两条支流在谷口汇成一条大河，远处分水岭像碗沿一样把水收拢。 A river basin gathers every drop that falls between its divides and carries it down one channel.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（流域）；句意为流域收拢分水岭之间的每一滴水，并把它送进同一条河道。

pos.zh: 名词短语：流域；河流盆地；汇水区域

derivatives.zh: 由「河流」加形容词词尾构成，义为「河流的；河岸的」
由「河流盆地」中的中心名词独立使用，义为「盆地；水盆」
由表示「在下、次级」的前缀加「盆地」构成，义为「子流域」
由「盆地」与「范围广阔的」复合而成，义为「全流域的」
由表示「之间」的前缀加「盆地」构成，义为「跨流域的」

senses.title: The area drained by one river system
senses.definition: all the land whose runoff reaches a single river and its tributaries
senses.definitionCN: 指径流最终汇入同一条河及其支流的全部陆地
senses.example: The river basin covers a fifth of the country.
senses.exampleCN: 这个流域覆盖全国五分之一的土地。
senses.why: The phrase starts as a shape on a map: everything that drains through one outlet.
senses.whyCN: 这条短语最初是地图上的一个形状：凡经同一出口排出的地方都算在内。

senses.title: A bowl-shaped lowland holding a river
senses.definition: a broad depression between higher ground through which a river and its tributaries flow
senses.definitionCN: 指高地之间、有河流及支流穿过的宽阔低地
senses.example: The river basin lies between two mountain chains.
senses.exampleCN: 这个河流盆地位于两条山脉之间。
senses.why: The container word supplies the image of a bowl, and relief supplies the walls.
senses.whyCN: 「盆」这个词提供碗的意象，地形则提供碗壁。

senses.title: A unit of water management
senses.definition: the basin treated as one administrative unit for allocation, pollution control and flood planning
senses.definitionCN: 指把流域作为分配、治污与防洪规划的一个行政单元
senses.example: The river basin is managed by a single agency.
senses.exampleCN: 这个流域由一家机构统一管理。
senses.why: Water crosses many jurisdictions, so managers redraw the basin as one budget line.
senses.whyCN: 水跨越许多辖区，管理者便把流域重画为一条预算线。

senses.title: A basin crossing political borders
senses.definition: a basin shared by two or more countries or provinces
senses.definitionCN: 指由两个或更多国家、省份共享的流域
senses.example: The river basin crosses three national borders.
senses.exampleCN: 这个流域跨越三条国界。
senses.why: Water ignores borders, so the map unit and the political map rarely agree.
senses.whyCN: 水不理睬边界，因此流域单元与政区图很少吻合。

senses.title: A closed basin with no sea outlet
senses.definition: a basin whose water ends in an inland lake or evaporates rather than reaching the ocean
senses.definitionCN: 指水最终进入内陆湖或蒸发、而不流入海洋的流域
senses.example: The river basin has no outlet to the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 这个流域没有通向海洋的出口。
senses.why: An enclosed basin is a bowl with no drain hole, and salts accumulate inside it.
senses.whyCN: 封闭流域像一个没有排水孔的碗，盐分因此在里面累积。

senses.title: A legal planning district
senses.definition: a basin defined by law for water-quality targets and permits
senses.definitionCN: 指为水质目标与许可证管理而依法划定的流域
senses.example: The river basin district must meet its water quality targets.
senses.exampleCN: 这个流域区必须达到其水质目标。
senses.why: Regulation needs fixed lines, so the natural basin is redrawn as a legal district.
senses.whyCN: 监管需要固定界线，自然的流域因此被重画为法定区。

senses.title: A sedimentary basin filled by river deposits
senses.definition: a depression progressively filled with sand, mud and gravel brought by the river
senses.definitionCN: 指被河流带来的砂、泥与砾石逐渐填满的低地
senses.example: The river basin filled with sand and mud over millennia.
senses.exampleCN: 这个盆地历经千年被砂与泥填满。
senses.why: The bowl collects sediment as well as water, and geology reads the fill as a record.
senses.whyCN: 这个碗既收水也收沉积物，地质学把填充物读作记录。

senses.title: A region of shared water dependence
senses.definition: the community of users, farms and cities that depend on the same river system
senses.definitionCN: 指依靠同一河系的水的用户、农田与城市群体
senses.example: Farmers and cities in the river basin depend on the same snowmelt.
senses.exampleCN: 流域内的农民与城市依靠同一份融雪水。
senses.why: A basin is also a set of claimants, and the phrase can name them rather than the land.
senses.whyCN: 流域也是一群用水者，这个词因此可以指人而不指地。

intro.en: River came from Latin ripa, a bank, through the Vulgar Latin adjective riparia, land along a bank, and Old French rivere. Basin came through Old French bacin from Medieval Latin bacinus, a word of uncertain ultimate origin, possibly Gaulish.
intro.cn: 「河流」出自拉丁语 ripa「河岸」，经通俗拉丁语形容词「沿岸的土地」与古法语进入英语。「盆地」经古法语来自中世纪拉丁语 bacinus，其最终来源不确定，可能出自高卢语。

items.en: Ripa meant the bank of a river, the edge rather than the water.
items.cn: 这个词意为河岸，指水边而非水本身。

items.en: The adjective named land along a bank, and it became the Romance word for a river.
items.cn: 这个形容词指沿岸的土地，后来成为罗曼语中表示「河流」的词。

items.en: Old French rivere carried the word into English as river.
items.cn: 古法语把这个词带进英语，成为「河流」。

items.en: The word for a basin or bowl is of uncertain origin; a Gaulish source has been suggested but not established.
items.cn: 表示盆、碗的词来源不确定；有人提出高卢语来源，但未得到确证。

items.en: Old French bacin named a wide shallow vessel.
items.cn: 古法语中这个词指宽而浅的容器。

items.en: English took the vessel word and later applied it to bowl-shaped land.
items.cn: 英语借入这个容器词，后来用它指碗状的地形。

note.en: The first group shares the river or basin element; the second group names the technical equivalents and the lines between them.
note.cn: 第一组共享「河流」或「盆地」的成分；第二组是技术同义词与它们之间的界线。

entries.definition: A bowl or a bowl-shaped area of land.
entries.definitionCN: 指盆、碗，或碗状的地形区域。

entries.definition: A large natural stream flowing to the sea or a lake.
entries.definitionCN: 指流入海洋或湖泊的大天然水道。

entries.definition: Relating to a river or its banks.
entries.definitionCN: 指与河流或其河岸有关的。

entries.definition: A smaller basin within a larger one.
entries.definitionCN: 指大流域内部较小的流域。

entries.definition: Extending across the whole basin.
entries.definitionCN: 指遍及整个流域的。

entries.definition: The technical synonym for the area drained by a river system.
entries.definitionCN: 指一条河系所排水区域的技术同义词。

entries.definition: The area from which water is collected, common in British usage.
entries.definitionCN: 指集水区域，英国用法中常见。

entries.definition: In American usage the basin itself; in British usage the divide.
entries.definitionCN: 美国用法指流域本身，英国用法指分水岭。

entries.definition: The ridge of high ground separating two basins.
entries.definitionCN: 指分隔两个流域的高地脊线。

entries.definition: The flat land beside a river that floods periodically.
entries.definitionCN: 指河边周期性泛滥的平地。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the bowl and the bank: water collected inside a rim and led out by one channel.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着「碗」与「岸」展开：水被收在碗沿之内，再由一条河道送出。

normal.en: Think of a bowl: the rim is the divide, the bottom is the outlet.
normal.cn: 想一只碗：碗沿是分水岭，碗底是出水口。

normal.en: Everything inside the rim drains through the same river.
normal.cn: 碗沿以内的水都经同一条河流出。

normal.en: A closed basin is a bowl with no drain hole; salt stays inside.
normal.cn: 闭流流域是没有排水孔的碗，盐分留在里面。

normal.en: Water ignores borders, so a basin often crosses several countries.
normal.cn: 水不理睬国界，所以流域常跨越数国。

normal.en: A basin district is the legal redrawing of a natural bowl.
normal.cn: 流域区是把自然碗形改画成法定界线。

abstract.en: A catchment is a lesson in dependence: every slope sends its water to the same place.
abstract.cn: 流域是一堂关于依存的课：每道坡都把水送往同一处。

abstract.en: The same shape can be a physical bowl, a budget unit and a community.
abstract.cn: 同一个形状可以是物理的碗、预算单元，也可以是一个共同体。

abstract.en: Lines drawn on water are always negotiations, not facts.
abstract.cn: 画在水上的界线永远是协商，而不是事实。

examples.en: The river basin supplies water to more than thirty million people.
examples.cn: 这个流域为三千多万人供水。

examples.en: A transboundary river basin needs an agreement between the states that share it.
examples.cn: 跨界流域需要共享它的各州达成协议。

examples.en: Sediment cores show how the river basin filled over ten thousand years.
examples.cn: 沉积柱样显示这个盆地在一万年间如何被填满。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「瑞弗·贝森」——一条河被装进一只大碗（贝森），碗沿就是分水岭：流域

root: 「河流」出自拉丁语 ripa「河岸」，经通俗拉丁语「沿岸土地」与古法语进入英语；「盆地」经古法语来自中世纪拉丁语 bacinus，最终来源不确定，可能出自高卢语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses treat one catchment as a mapped area, a physical bowl, a management unit, a border case, a closed bowl, a legal district, a sediment trap and a community.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一片集水区分别看作地图区域、物理碗形、管理单元、跨界案例、封闭盆地、法定区、沉积陷阱与依存共同体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two tributaries meeting at a valley mouth, with a rim of hills holding the water in.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条支流在谷口相会，一圈丘陵像碗沿把水收住。

branches.en: THE SHAPE: the drained area and the lowland that holds it.
branches.cn: 形状：被排水的区域，以及容纳它的低地。

branches.en: THE UNIT: a management area and a district fixed by law.
branches.cn: 单元：管理区域与依法划定的区。

branches.en: THE BORDER CASE: a basin shared by states that do not share a map.
branches.cn: 跨界案例：被不同国家共享、却不共享一张地图的流域。

branches.en: THE CLOSED BOWL: no outlet, so water and salt stay.
branches.cn: 封闭的碗：没有出口，水与盐都留下。

branches.en: THE FILL AND THE PEOPLE: sediment building the basin, and users sharing one snowmelt.
branches.cn: 填充与人：沉积物造出盆地，用户共享同一份融雪。

intro.en: One half names the bank, the other names the bowl; together they name a bowl of land drained by one river.
intro.cn: 一半说「岸」，一半说「碗」；合起来就是被一条河排水的一只陆地大碗。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the bank and the adjective of land along a bank; the bowl word reached Latin from an uncertain source, possibly Gaulish.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供「河岸」与「沿岸土地」的形容词；「碗」这个词进入拉丁语的来源不确定，可能出自高卢语。

items.example: It is the source of river and riparian.
items.exampleCN: 它是「河流」与「河岸的」等词的来源。

items.example: It became the Romance word for river.
items.exampleCN: 它成为罗曼语中表示河流的词。

items.example: Old French passed it to English.
items.exampleCN: 古法语把它传给英语。

items.example: The English word keeps the bank at its root.
items.exampleCN: 英语这个词的词根仍保留「岸」的意思。

items.example: It gave English basin.
items.exampleCN: 它构成英语中的「盆地」。

items.example: Its ultimate source is uncertain.
items.exampleCN: 其最终来源不确定。

items.example: English extended the vessel to land.
items.exampleCN: 英语把这个容器词扩展到地形。

items.example: It forms subbasin, a smaller basin inside a larger one.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「子流域」，即大流域内的小流域。

items.example: It forms basinwide, covering the whole basin.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「全流域的」。

derivatives.zh: 由「河流」加形容词词尾构成，义为「河流的」
由短语中心名词独立使用，义为「盆地；水盆」
由次级前缀加「盆地」构成，义为「子流域」
由「盆地」与「遍及」成分复合而成，义为「全流域的」
由「之间」前缀加「盆地」构成，义为「跨流域的」

definition_zh: 减损；贬低；有损于；分散（注意）
definition_en: to reduce the value, quality or reputation of something
core_image: 一面完好的墙上被划出一道浅痕，整面墙看上去都不再完整
scene: 那道裂缝本来很小，但每次有人经过都会先看它一眼。 A few scratches detract from the beauty of the table.
sceneCN: 这里 detract 指使某物的美感减损（第 1 个义项：减损价值）；句意为几道划痕有损这张桌子的美感。

pos.zh: 减损；贬低
分散；转移

senses.title: Reduce value or quality
senses.definition: to make something less valuable or less good
senses.definitionCN: 使某物价值降低或品质变差
senses.example: A few scratches detract from the beauty of the table.
senses.exampleCN: 几道划痕有损这张桌子的美感。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to draw away'; value is drawn off the way water is drawn from a full vessel.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「拉走」；价值被拉走，就像水从满的容器里被舀出。

senses.title: Diminish an achievement
senses.definition: to make an accomplishment seem smaller than it is
senses.definitionCN: 使一项成就显得比实际更小
senses.example: Nothing can detract from what the team achieved.
senses.exampleCN: 没有什么能贬低这个团队所取得的成就。
senses.why: Praise adds weight, and detraction removes it; the same scale is used in both directions.
senses.whyCN: 赞扬增加分量，贬低则移除分量；两个方向用的是同一杆秤。

senses.title: Spoil a pleasing quality
senses.definition: to lessen the pleasure or attractiveness of something
senses.definitionCN: 减少某物的愉悦感或吸引力
senses.example: The noisy road detracts from the charm of the house.
senses.exampleCN: 嘈杂的道路有损这座房子的魅力。
senses.why: Charm is a delicate balance; one wrong element pulls the whole composition down.
senses.whyCN: 魅力是一种精细的平衡；一个不对的元素就把整个构图拉低。

senses.title: Divert attention
senses.definition: to draw attention away from the main matter
senses.definitionCN: 把注意力从主要事情上引开
senses.example: Constant notifications detract attention from the work.
senses.exampleCN: 不断的通知分散了对工作的注意。
senses.why: Attention is a finite beam; whatever detracts turns part of it elsewhere.
senses.whyCN: 注意力是一束有限的光；任何减损都把其中一部分转向别处。

senses.title: Speak disparagingly
senses.definition: to speak of someone in a way that lowers their standing
senses.definitionCN: 以降低他人地位的方式谈论某人
senses.example: He never missed a chance to detract from his rivals.
senses.exampleCN: 他从不放过贬低对手的机会。
senses.why: Words can remove value from a reputation as surely as scratches remove it from a table.
senses.whyCN: 言语能从名声上拿走价值，正如划痕能从桌子上拿走价值。

senses.title: Harm a reputation
senses.definition: to damage the good name of a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 损害个人或团体的好名声
senses.example: The scandal detracted from the university's reputation.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻损害了这所大学的声誉。
senses.why: Reputation is held by others, so it can be lowered by talk even when nothing has changed.
senses.whyCN: 声誉由他人持有，因此即使事实未变，也能被言论拉低。

senses.title: Lessen enjoyment
senses.definition: to reduce the pleasure of an occasion
senses.definitionCN: 减少某个场合的乐趣
senses.example: One rude guest detracted from the whole evening.
senses.exampleCN: 一个无礼的客人破坏了整个夜晚。
senses.why: Pleasure is a total made of many small contributions, and one rude guest removes more than their own share.
senses.whyCN: 愉悦由许多小的贡献构成一个总数，而一个无礼的客人拿走的比他自己那一份更多。

senses.title: Subtract, in old use
senses.definition: in older mathematics, to take away a quantity
senses.definitionCN: 在旧时数学中，减去一个量
senses.example: The old text says to detract three from ten.
senses.exampleCN: 旧文本说从十中减去三。
senses.why: The arithmetic sense is the literal skeleton: detraction is subtraction applied to value.
senses.whyCN: 算术义是字面的骨架：减损就是把减法用在价值上。

intro.en: Detract comes from a Latin verb meaning to draw away, and the image of subtraction runs through every sense.
intro.cn: detract 来自一个意为「拉走」的拉丁动词，「减法」的意象贯穿所有义项。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the 15c. and fixed the phrase detract from for value and reputation.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个动词，并用 detract from 固定搭配表示价值与声誉的减损。

items.en: Detrahere meant 'to draw off, take away', from de- 'away' and trahere 'to draw'.
items.cn: detrahere 意为「拉走、拿走」，由 de-「离开」与 trahere「拉」构成。

items.en: Trahere 'to draw' also gives traction, tractor and attract, all about pulling.
items.cn: trahere「拉」也产生 traction、tractor 与 attract，都与拖拉有关。

items.en: Detractio meant 'a taking away', used for both subtraction and slander.
items.cn: detractio 意为「拿走」，既用于减法，也用于诽谤。

items.en: The word moved from arithmetic to reputation: to detract from a person is to subtract from their standing.
items.cn: 这个词从算术移到声誉：贬低一个人，就是从其地位中减去。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the tract root; the near-meaning group names kinds of reduction.
note.cn: 形近组共享 tract 词根；近义组列出各种削减。

entries.definition: the act of belittling or reducing value.
entries.definitionCN: 贬低或减损价值的行为。

entries.definition: someone who criticizes and lessens another's worth.
entries.definitionCN: 批评并贬低他人价值的人。

entries.definition: To draw together or become smaller; it shares tract- but pulls in rather than taking away.
entries.definitionCN: 拉拢或缩小；共享 tract-，但是往里拉而非拿走。

entries.definition: to draw something toward oneself.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物拉向自己。

entries.definition: to make something seem or become smaller.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物显得或变得更小。

entries.definition: to weaken something gradually and indirectly.
entries.definitionCN: 逐渐间接地削弱某物。

entries.definition: to speak of someone or something as unimportant.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人或某物说得不重要。

entries.definition: To reduce the value or worth of something.
entries.definitionCN: 降低某物的价值。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a scratch on an otherwise perfect surface.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把「完好表面上的一道划痕」这一画面留住。

normal.en: Tract means to draw; detract means to draw value away.
normal.cn: tract 意为拉；detract 就是把价值拉走。

normal.en: Think of a subtraction sign in front of a reputation.
normal.cn: 想象在声誉前面放一个减号。

normal.en: Picture a fine table with one deep scratch; the eye keeps returning to it.
normal.cn: 想象一张好桌子上有一道深划痕；目光总回到那里。

normal.en: Say dih-TRAKT, one clean pull away from the whole.
normal.cn: 读成 dih-TRAKT，从整体上干净地拉走一次。

normal.en: Link it with diminish: both make the total smaller.
normal.cn: 把它和 diminish 联系：两者都让总量变小。

abstract.en: Value can be removed without anything being taken.
abstract.cn: 不必拿走任何东西，价值也能被移除。

abstract.en: A single wrong element can pull down a whole composition.
abstract.cn: 一个不对的元素就能拉低整个构图。

abstract.en: Slander is subtraction performed on a person's standing.
abstract.cn: 诽谤就是在人的地位上做减法。

examples.en: A few scratches detract from the beauty of the table.
examples.cn: 几道划痕有损这张桌子的美感。

examples.en: The noisy road detracts from the charm of the house.
examples.cn: 嘈杂的道路有损这座房子的魅力。

examples.en: The scandal detracted from the university's reputation.
examples.cn: 丑闻损害了这所大学的声誉。

dict_mnemonic.text: de（离开）+ tract（拉）：把价值或注意力拉走，就是「减损」。

root: 拉丁语 detrahere（拉走）：de-（离开）+ trahere（拉）

sensesIntro.en: Detract always takes something away from a whole; the senses differ in whether what is removed is value, standing, pleasure or attention.
sensesIntro.cn: detract 始终从整体上拿走一点东西；各义项的差别在于被拿走的是价值、地位、乐趣还是注意力。

core.en: VALUE IS DRAWN AWAY
core.cn: 价值被拉走

branches.en: Beauty and quality reduced by a small flaw.
branches.cn: 被小瑕疵削减的美感与品质。

branches.en: Achievements and rivals measured downward by talk.
branches.cn: 被言论压低的分量与对手。

branches.en: Attention pulled away from the main matter.
branches.cn: 从主要事情上被拉走的注意力。

branches.en: Reputations and occasions that lose their shine.
branches.cn: 失去光彩的声誉与场合。

branches.en: The old arithmetic sense of subtracting.
branches.cn: 减去的古老算术义。

intro.en: The word belongs to the tract family, where every member involves pulling.
intro.cn: 这个词属于 tract 词族，其中每个成员都涉及「拉」。

latinIntro.en: Latin trahere 'to draw' supplies a large family of English words about pulling and dragging.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 trahere「拉」提供了大量关于拖拉的英语词。

items.meaning: the act of taking value away
items.example: The article was a long detraction of his career.
items.exampleCN: 这篇文章是对他职业生涯的长篇贬损。

items.example: His detractors called the plan naive.
items.exampleCN: 贬低他的人称这个计划天真。

items.example: The fence is detracting from the view.
items.exampleCN: 这道栅栏有损景观。

items.example: The remarks were detractive rather than helpful.
items.exampleCN: 这些话是贬损性的，而非有帮助的。

items.example: The exhibit attracts thousands of visitors.
items.exampleCN: 这个展览吸引成千上万的参观者。

items.example: The tires lost traction on the ice.
items.exampleCN: 轮胎在冰上失去了抓地力。

items.example: The tractor pulled the broken cart.
items.exampleCN: 拖拉机拉走了坏掉的车。

items.example: The idea is too abstract to picture.
items.exampleCN: 这个观念太抽象，难以想象。

definition_zh: 君主制；君主国；君主制度本身；某个王室家族；由单一力量支配的状态
definition_en: a form of government in which one hereditary ruler holds the throne, the state so governed, and by extension any system dominated by a single authority
core_image: 一顶王冠放在宪法文本上，书页压住了权杖的下端
scene: 议会厅的陈列柜里，王冠搁在一本宪法上，权杖被书页压住一截。 Constitutional monarchy keeps the crown but places the budget under parliament.
sceneCN: 这里 monarchy 指「由君主掌握国家元首之位的政体」（第 1 个义项：君主制这一政府形式）；句意为立宪君主制保留王冠，却把预算权交给议会。可辨识物件：陈列柜、王冠、宪法、权杖、议会席位。

pos.zh: 君主制；君主国；王室；单一支配的体系

derivatives.zh: monarchy 去掉 -y 回溯到希腊 monarkhes → 君主，语义由制度转为人
monarch + -ical（形容词后缀变体）→ 君主制的，语气更正式
monarch + -ism（主义后缀）→ 君主主义，语义由制度转为主张
monarch + -ist（主张者后缀）→ 君主主义者
anti-（反对前缀）+ monarchist → 反君主主义者

senses.title: Government by a single hereditary ruler
senses.titleCN: 由一位世袭君主执政的政体
senses.definition: a form of government in which one person holds the throne by inheritance
senses.definitionCN: 由一人凭继承占据王位的政府形式
senses.example: Constitutional monarchy keeps the crown but places the budget under parliament.
senses.exampleCN: 君主立宪制保留王冠，却把预算权交给议会。
senses.why: Greek monarkhia named the rule of one person, and English kept it as the name of a constitutional form.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 monarkhia 本指一人统治，英语把它保留为一种宪政形式的名称。

senses.title: A state ruled by a monarch
senses.definition: a country whose head of state is a king, queen or emperor
senses.definitionCN: 以国王、女王或皇帝为国家元首的国家
senses.example: The monarchy survived two republics before it fell.
senses.exampleCN: 这个君主国挺过了两个共和国时期才覆灭。
senses.why: Metonymy let the form of government stand for the country that uses it, as in 'a constitutional monarchy'.
senses.whyCN: 转喻让政体之名代表采用它的国家，如「一个君主立宪国」。

senses.title: The institution of royal rule
senses.definition: the enduring institution of the crown, apart from any one ruler or country
senses.definitionCN: 王权这一长期存在的制度，独立于任何具体君主或国家
senses.example: The monarchy as an institution lost its landed revenue.
senses.exampleCN: 作为制度的君主制失去了地产收入。
senses.why: Institutions outlast individuals, so the word can name the arrangement rather than the person or the state.
senses.whyCN: 制度比个人长寿，因此这个词可指安排本身，而非人或国家。

senses.title: A particular royal family
senses.definition: the royal house of a country, considered as a family and a public body
senses.definitionCN: 一国的王室家族，被视为家族与公共机构
senses.example: The British monarchy has narrowed its public role.
senses.exampleCN: 英国王室已缩小了其公共角色。
senses.why: Journalists use the word for the family in the palace, since the household is the visible face of the institution.
senses.whyCN: 记者用这个词指宫殿里的家族，因为王室家庭是这一制度可见的面孔。

senses.title: Rule without constitutional limit
senses.titleCN: 不受宪法限制的君主统治
senses.definition: a system in which the monarch's power is not limited by law or parliament
senses.definitionCN: 君主的权力不受法律或议会限制的制度
senses.example: Absolute monarchy left no room for a parliament.
senses.exampleCN: 绝对君主制没有给议会留下空间。
senses.why: The compound 'absolute monarchy' marks the older, unlimited reading of the word.
senses.whyCN: 「绝对君主制」这一复合词标出了该词较早的、不受限的读法。

senses.title: Rule limited by a constitution
senses.definition: a system in which the monarch reigns within constitutional limits and ministers govern
senses.definitionCN: 君主在宪法限度内临朝、由大臣治理的制度
senses.example: Constitutional monarchy made the crown ceremonial.
senses.exampleCN: 君主立宪制使王冠变为礼仪性的。
senses.why: The compound marks the modern settlement in which the title survives but power does not.
senses.whyCN: 这一复合词标出现代安排：称号保留，权力不留。

senses.title: Dominance by one power in a field
senses.titleCN: 某一领域由单一力量支配
senses.definition: a situation in which one firm or group rules an activity as a monarch rules a state
senses.definitionCN: 一家公司或团体像君主统治国家般支配某项活动的情形
senses.example: A handful of firms held a monarchy over the coffee trade.
senses.exampleCN: 少数几家公司对咖啡贸易形成了君主式的支配。
senses.why: The political image is borrowed for markets where one player sets terms for all the rest.
senses.whyCN: 这一政治意象被借到市场上：一个玩家为其余所有人定条件。

senses.title: The period of royal rule
senses.definition: the span of time during which a country was governed as a monarchy
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家作为君主国被治理的那段时期
senses.example: Many of the palaces were built during the monarchy.
senses.exampleCN: 许多宫殿建于君主制时期。
senses.why: As with empire, the name of the system can stand for the years it lasted.
senses.whyCN: 与 empire 一样，制度之名可以代表它延续的岁月。

intro.en: Monarchy comes through Latin monarchia from Greek monarkhia 'rule of one', built on monos 'alone' and arkhein 'to rule'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: monarchy 经拉丁 monarchia 来自希腊 monarkhia「一人统治」，由 monos「单独」与 arkhein「统治」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Monos 'alone, single' supplies the first element, the same one seen in monologue and monopoly.
items.cn: monos「单独、唯一」提供第一个成分，与 monologue、monopoly 中的相同。

items.en: Arkhein 'to rule, to begin' supplies the second element; its noun arkhe covers both a start and an office.
items.cn: arkhein「统治、开始」提供第二个成分；其名词 arkhe 兼指起点与职位。

items.en: The abstract noun monarkhia named the rule of one person, as opposed to oligarchy or democracy.
items.cn: 抽象名词 monarkhia 指一人统治，与寡头制或民主制相对。

items.en: Latin monarchia and French monarchie carried the word to English by the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 拉丁 monarchia 与法语 monarchie 在十四世纪前把这个词带入英语。

items.en: From the seventeenth century English writers distinguished absolute from constitutional monarchy, and both compounds became standard.
items.cn: 自十七世纪起，英语作者区分绝对君主制与君主立宪制，两个复合词都成为标准说法。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact first English citation is not established, and the extension to firms and markets has no single documented origin.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：确切的最早英语书证未有定论，向公司与市场的引申也没有唯一可考来源。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same Greek compound or words sharing one element; group two holds names of governing systems.
note.cn: 第一组是同出该希腊复合词或共享一个成分的词；第二组是各种政体名称。

entries.definition: The ruler himself or herself; monarchy is the office, system or state.
entries.definitionCN: 统治者本人；monarchy 指职位、制度或国家。

entries.definition: The relational adjective, meaning 'of a monarch or of monarchy'.
entries.definitionCN: 关系形容词，意为「君主的、君主制的」。

entries.definition: A longer variant of the same adjective, now more common in political writing.
entries.definitionCN: 同一形容词的较长变体，如今在政治写作中更常见。

entries.definition: From hieros 'sacred' plus arkhein: rule by priests, later any ranked order. It shares only the second element.
entries.definitionCN: 由 hieros「神圣」加 arkhein 构成：最初指祭司统治，后指任何等级秩序。只共享第二个成分。

entries.definition: The territory or state ruled by a king or queen; it names the country, while monarchy names the system.
entries.definitionCN: 由国王或女王统治的领土或国家；指国家，而 monarchy 指制度。

entries.definition: A small state ruled by a prince; it is a species of monarchy with a lower title.
entries.definitionCN: 由亲王统治的小国；是君主制的一种，称号较低。

entries.definition: Rule by one person with no constitutional limit; it stresses the absence of checks rather than heredity.
entries.definitionCN: 一人不受宪法限制的统治；强调缺乏制约，而非世袭。

entries.definition: A state whose head is chosen rather than inherited; it is the usual contrast to monarchy.
entries.definitionCN: 元首经选择而非继承的国家；是君主制通常的对立面。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: monos 'alone' + arkhein 'rule' + -ia 'system': the system of one ruler.
normal.cn: monos「单独」+ arkhein「统治」+ -ia「制度」：一人统治的制度。

normal.en: The family runs monarchy, monarch, monarchic, monarchical, monarchist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 monarchy、monarch、monarchic、monarchical、monarchist。

normal.en: Two fixed compounds split the field: absolute monarchy and constitutional monarchy.
normal.cn: 两个固定复合词划出领域：绝对君主制与君主立宪制。

normal.en: A republic is the usual contrast, since its head is chosen rather than inherited.
normal.cn: 共和国是通常的对照，因为其元首经选择而非继承。

normal.en: Journalists say 'the British monarchy' when they mean the royal family.
normal.cn: 记者说「英国王室」时，指的就是那个王室家族。

abstract.en: Picture a crown resting on a constitution as if pinned in place.
abstract.cn: 想象一顶王冠放在宪法上，像被压住一样。

abstract.en: Picture a throne that has outlived every person who sat in it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张御座比所有坐过它的人都活得久。

abstract.en: Picture one café chain setting the price for every other café on the street.
abstract.cn: 想象一家连锁咖啡馆替整条街的咖啡馆定价。

examples.en: The country moved from absolute monarchy to a limited one in a single century.
examples.cn: 这个国家在一个世纪内从绝对君主制转为有限君主制。

examples.en: Support for the monarchy fell after the war.
examples.cn: 战后民众对君主制的支持下降。

examples.en: The constitution defines the monarchy without naming the present king.
examples.cn: 宪法界定了君主制，却没有写出在任国王的名字。

root: 希腊 monarkhia「一人统治」= monos「单独」+ arkhein「统治」+ -ia（抽象名词后缀）；经拉丁 monarchia、法语 monarchie 入英语。英语 monarchy。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one system: rule by one person. It can be read as a form, a state, an institution, a family, two constitutional variants, a market habit and a stretch of years.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种制度展开：一人统治。它可被读作形式、国家、制度、家族、两种宪政变体、市场习性与一段岁月。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crown resting on a constitution, with a sceptre pinned under the pages.
core.cn: 核心意象：王冠放在宪法上，权杖被书页压住。

branches.en: FORM AND COUNTRY: the arrangement and the nation that adopts it share one name.
branches.cn: 制度与国家：安排本身与采用它的国家共享一名。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTION: the crown as a lasting body, not a person.
branches.cn: 制度：王冠作为持久的机构，而非个人。

branches.en: THE FAMILY: the household in the palace is the visible face of the system.
branches.cn: 家族：宫殿里的家族是该制度可见的面孔。

branches.en: TWO CONSTITUTIONS: unlimited rule and ceremonial rule are rival readings of one word.
branches.cn: 两种宪制：不受限统治与礼仪统治是同一个词的两种读法。

branches.en: THE IMITATION AND THE YEARS: a market can be ruled like a state, and a system's name can mark its era.
branches.cn: 模仿与岁月：市场可像国家一样被统治，制度之名也能标记其时代。

intro.en: Monarchy is a Greek compound plus an abstract suffix, and all three parts recur in English, so the family can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: monarchy 是希腊复合词加抽象后缀，三部分都在英语中反复出现，因此整个词族可按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Greek monos, arkhein and -ia give monarchy; Latin monarchia and French monarchie carried the form into English.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 monos、arkhein 与 -ia 构成 monarchy；拉丁 monarchia 与法语 monarchie 把该形式带入英语。

items.meaning: rule by priests, later ranked order
items.meaningCN: 祭司统治，后指等级秩序

senses.title: Following as a result

senses.definitionCN: 因另一事而发生

senses.why: The same following becomes reasoning.
